sections.title: Jurisdiction
sections.text:
1.1 JURISDICTION (KACP 1.2)
1.1.1 GEOGRAPHIC JURISDICTION
The jurisdiction of the Louisville Metro Police Department (LMPD) is contained within the geographical boundaries of Jefferson County, Kentucky, as currently incorporated.
The LMPD has the primary responsibility of providing all police services within Jefferson County, Kentucky. The department provides full law enforcement emergency services to the citizens that it serves 24 hours a day, 365 days a year (KACP 17.10, 27.6). Sworn members possess law enforcement authority any time they are within the boundaries of Jefferson County. Officers are authorized to enforce all applicable laws and ordinances within the boundaries of Jefferson County, both on-duty and off-duty.
Officers are authorized to carry concealed deadly weapons under Kentucky Revised Statute (KRS) 527.020(3) and Louisville Metro Code of Ordinances (LMCO) 41.03 and 135.06. This authorization allows both on-duty and off-duty officers to carry an authorized weapon within their jurisdiction (refer to SOP 5.1).
1.1.2 JURISDICTION EXCEPTIONS
Exceptions to SOP 1.1.1 include:
• Incidents occurring within the jurisdiction of the Louisville Metro Department of Corrections (LMDC). Officers assist when requested by competent authority (KACP 19.5).
• Airplane crashes.
• Violations of federal laws whereby federal law enforcement authorities have decided, or are obligated, to exercise jurisdiction.
1.1.3 CONCURRENT STATE JURISDICTION
Per KRS 431.007, an officer may assist another Kentucky law enforcement agency in any matter within the other agency’s jurisdiction when officially requested. This request will be forwarded, in writing, from the requesting agency’s Chief of Police, or their designee, to the LMPD Chief of Police, or their designee, for approval. If one or both Chiefs of Police are unavailable to participate in the request, the highest-ranking Bureau Commander or division/section/unit commander will participate in their absence. If the request does not occur between Chiefs of Police, a memorandum, documenting the request, will be forwarded to the Chief of Police and the Legal Advisor’s Office by the end of the member’s tour of duty. For the purposes of this policy, an email is acceptable as a written request.
In exigent circumstances, a telephone request is acceptable, however, the authorizing LMPD commander must submit a memorandum, documenting the specifics of the phone call, by the end of their tour of duty, to the Chief of Police and the Legal Advisor’s Office.
Reviewed 11/22/24
1.1.3 CONCURRENT STATE JURISDICTION (CONTINUED)
Once officially requested by the other agency and approved by the LMPD commander, the officer has full arrest powers in the county where they are assisting, for the duration of the matter for which the request was made.
1.1.4 CONCURRENT FEDERAL JURISDICTION
Real property that is leased by the federal government within the geographic jurisdiction of the LMPD is subject to concurrent jurisdiction by the department and federal officers. Real property that is owned by the federal government within the department’s jurisdiction is subject to exclusive jurisdiction by federal authorities. An officer should verify the controlling jurisdiction prior to taking official action.
1.1.5 JURISDICTIONAL CONFLICTS
When a police department of another government within Jefferson County refuses, or is unable, to respond to a police-related matter, the department will respond, take appropriate action, and forward any documentation to the appropriate agency.
Reviewed 11/22/24

sections.title: Contractual/Mutual Aid Agreements
sections.text:
1.2 CONTRACTUAL/MUTUAL AID AGREEMENTS (KACP 1.2)
1.2.1 CONTRACTUAL (INTERLOCAL) AGREEMENTS
Each contractual agreement between the Louisville Metro Police Department (LMPD) and another local government is based on a need for service. The Legal Advisor and the Chief of Police, or their designee, will review each contractual agreement. The Legal Advisor retains copies of the contractual agreements. Copies of the Small Cities Program Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs) are maintained in the Eighth Division.
1.2.2 SCHEDULING
The Eighth Division Commander designates a commanding officer to act as the Program Administrator. The Program Administrator is responsible for scheduling personnel assignments in accordance with contractual agreements. Any officer wishing to volunteer for this program should contact the Program Administrator, via email.
1.2.3 OFFICER RESPONSIBILITY FOR CONTRACTUAL AGREEMENT DETAIL
Officers working the detail are responsible for all calls for service, within the city to which they are assigned, and will remain within the boundaries of that city, unless exigent circumstances arise (e.g., 10-30, officer in trouble, officer needs help, etc.). Officers will perform their duties in accordance with the requirements of the contract, the Small Cities Program SOPs, and the LMPD’s SOPs. Officers may enforce state laws and Louisville Metro Code of Ordinances (LMCOs), but will not enforce ordinances of lesser jurisdictions, unless expressly authorized by the Chief of Police, or their designee. All officers are required to sign an accountability roster to indicate that they have read and understood the procedures regarding small cities. The rosters are maintained in the Eighth Division.
1.2.4 OFFICER RIGHTS
The employment rights of officers assigned under a contract for law enforcement services will not be abridged. Participation in a contracted law enforcement service will not penalize the officer in any way, nor will such assignment threaten their employment rights, promotional opportunities, training opportunities, or benefits.
1.2.5 MUTUAL AID AGREEMENTS
The Chief of Police, or their designee, has the authority to request assistance from other agencies to assist with law enforcement within the boundaries of Jefferson County, if needed. Agencies such as the National Guard, the Kentucky State Police (KSP), Jefferson County Sheriff’s Office (JCSO), or other local law enforcement agencies may be called to assist in a natural or man-made disaster or a civil disturbance that overwhelms the capabilities of the department. The LMPD may also be called to assist other agencies if a natural or man-made disaster or a civil disturbance overwhelms the capabilities of that agency.
Reviewed 08/20/25
1.2.6 MUTUAL AID RESPONSES
If an event overwhelms the capabilities of the LMPD, the Chief of Police, in coordination with the Louisville Metro Mayor, will have Louisville Metro Emergency Services contact local law enforcement agencies within Jefferson County to respond to the scene of the disturbance and assist, as needed. If an incident requires the assistance of other municipal (outside of Jefferson County), state (Kentucky or neighboring states), or federal agencies, the request will be routed from Louisville Metro Emergency Services to the Kentucky Division of Emergency Management’s Emergency Operations Center.
Officers should not self-deploy to the scene of a natural or man-made disaster or civil disturbance unless specifically requested by MetroSafe, at the request of the Chief of Police. Officers who respond without the proper training and equipment may actually hinder law enforcement efforts. The Incident Commander (IC), or their designee, will take the lead in the incident and direct the responsibilities of the appropriate support personnel (refer to SOP 8.36, SOP 12.6, and SOP 12.13).
When MetroSafe is contacted by other Jefferson County law enforcement agencies, MetroSafe will dispatch available personnel to the affected area to assist, as needed. Other agency requests will be sent to Louisville Metro Emergency Services from the Kentucky Division of Emergency Management’s Emergency Operations Center. LMPD officers should not self-deploy to an incident without specific instructions. The IC in the affected area’s jurisdiction will take the lead in the incident and direct the responsibilities of responding LMPD personnel.
1.2.7 MUTUAL AID TRAINING
The LMPD regularly participates in crowd control training and readiness exercises with mutual aid agencies. This training is coordinated by the Training Division in conjunction with mutual aid agencies.
The LMPD participates in regularly-scheduled tabletop exercises with mutual aid agencies to solidify roles, responses and unify policies associated with a natural or man-made disaster or a civil disturbance.
Reviewed 08/20/25

sections.title: Structure and Organization
sections.text:
1.3 STRUCTURE AND ORGANIZATION
1.3.1 ORGANIZATIONAL STRUCTURE/CHART (KACP 3.1)
The Louisville Metro Police Department (LMPD) utilizes the chain of command principle in which subordinate supervisors report to their bureau/division/section/unit commanders, who in turn, report directly to the Chief of Police. Each organizational component will be under the direct command of only one (1) supervisor. The organizational chart outlines the structure of the department and shows the relationship of components within the entire organization. The organizational chart will be periodically reviewed and updated, as needed.
1.3.2 JOB DESCRIPTIONS
Job descriptions are available to all personnel through the Louisville Metro Human Resources (HR) Department, Police Merit Board, and Civil Service Board (KACP 3.2). All job descriptions can be accessed via Workday.
1.3.3 MONTHLY PERSONNEL RUNDOWNS
Rundown: Summary of all sworn and professional staff personnel, including rank, who are assigned to each division/section/unit.
Rundowns for each division/section/unit will be updated on a monthly basis. The division/section/unit designee will post the rundowns on the LMPD Intranet by clicking on “Monthly Rundown” and placing the rundown in the appropriate folder. The rundowns will be posted by the 5th day of each month.
These monthly rundowns include a list of all personnel who are in the division/section/unit and a summary of the following:
• Number of personnel per unit or assignment
• Total number of officers and detectives
• Number of commanding officers per rank (e.g., majors, lieutenants, sergeants, etc.)
• Total number of commanding officers
• Total number of sworn personnel
• Number of personnel who are unavailable for duty
• Number of professional staff personnel
• Grand total of personnel assigned
• Grand total of personnel who are available for duty
If significant personnel changes occur at any other time during the month, the rundown will be updated at that time.

sections.title: Chief of Police
sections.text:
1.4 CHIEF OF POLICE
1.4.1 RESPONSIBILITIES
The Chief of Police is appointed by the Louisville Metro Mayor and reports directly to the Mayor.
The Chief of Police is empowered as the highest authority in the Louisville Metro Police Department (LMPD). Per Louisville Metro Code of Ordinance (LMCO) 36.02, the Chief of Police has the ultimate control over all aspects of departmental operations and command authority over all bureaus, divisions, sections, units, squads, groups, teams, or any other components of the department (KACP 4.1). Additionally, the Chief of Police is responsible for all fiscal matters of the department (KACP 8.1, 8.3).
The Chief of Police directly supervises the following personnel (KACP 3.3):
• Deputy Chief of Police/Chief of Operations (refer to SOP 1.5)
• Deputy Chief of Police/Chief of Staff (refer to SOP 1.5)
• Legal Advisor’s Office
• Special Investigations Division (SID) Commander (refer to SOP 1.9)
• Professional Standards Division (PSD) Commander (refer to SOP 1.9)
• Media and Public Relations (refer to SOP 3.3)
• Police Activities League (PAL) Director
• Chief’s Adjutant
In the event of an extended absence, the Chief of Police will designate an “acting authority.”
1.4.2 LEGAL ADVISOR’S OFFICE (KACP 2.1)
The Legal Advisor’s Office provides general legal advice to the department and acts as a liaison between the department and the Jefferson County Attorney’s Office (JCAO). The Legal Advisor’s Office reports directly to the Chief of Police, or their designee.
1.4.3 SPECIAL INVESTIGATIONS DIVISION (SID) COMMANDER (Major)
The SID Commander is appointed by the Mayor, upon the recommendation of the Chief of Police, and reports directly to the Chief of Police.
The SID Commander coordinates the activities of the Public Integrity Unit (PIU) and assists in officer reinstatement when the officer is returning from leaves of absence (refer to SOP 2.5, SOP 2.11, and SOP 8.12).
1.4.4 PROFESSIONAL STANDARDS DIVISION (PSD) COMMANDER (Major)
The PSD Commander is appointed by the Mayor, upon the recommendation of the Chief of Police, and reports directly to the Chief of Police.
1.4.4 PROFESSIONAL STANDARDS DIVISION (PSD) COMMANDER (CONTINUED)
The PSD Commander coordinates the activities of the Professional Standards Unit (PSU) and assists in officer reinstatement when the officer is returning from leaves of absence (refer to SOP 2.5, SOP 2.11, and SOP 8.12).
1.4.5 POLICE ACTIVITIES LEAGUE (PAL) DIRECTOR (Sworn)
The PAL Director reports to the Chief of Police. The PAL provides organized, educational, and sports-related activities for youths. The goal of the PAL is to bring officers and youths together to form bonds and foster relationships in order to make youths less apprehensive to both officers and law enforcement.

sections.title: Deputy Chief of Police
sections.text:
1.5 DEPUTY CHIEF OF POLICE
1.5.1 DEPUTY CHIEF OF POLICE/CHIEF OF OPERATIONS (Colonel)
The Deputy Chief of Police/Chief of Operations is appointed by the Mayor, upon the recommendation of the Chief of Police, and reports directly to the Chief of Police. When mandated by the Chief of Police, the Deputy Chief of Police/Chief of Operations may assume all responsibilities as the department’s chief executive officer (CEO) (KACP 4.2).
The Deputy Chief of Police/Chief of Operations coordinates the activities of the following (KACP 3.3):
• Administrative Bureau
• Patrol Bureau
1.5.2 DEPUTY CHIEF OF POLICE/CHIEF OF STAFF (Colonel)
The Deputy Chief of Police/Chief of Staff is appointed by the Mayor, upon the recommendation of the Chief of Police, and reports directly to the Chief of Police. When mandated by the Chief of Police, the Deputy Chief of Police/Chief of Staff may assume all responsibilities as the department’s CEO (KACP 4.2).
The Deputy Chief of Police/Chief of Staff coordinates the activities of the following (KACP 3.3):
• Accountability and Improvement Bureau (AIB)
• Support Bureau

sections.title: Patrol Bureau
sections.text:
1.6 PATROL BUREAU
1.6.1 ASSISTANT CHIEF OF POLICE/PATROL BUREAU (Lieutenant Colonel)
The Assistant Chief of Police/Patrol Bureau is appointed by the Mayor, upon the recommendation of the Chief of Police, and reports directly to the Deputy Chief of Police/Chief of Operations. When mandated by the Chief of Police, the Assistant Chief of Police/Patrol Bureau may assume all responsibilities as the department’s Chief Executive Officer (CEO) (KACP 4.2).
The Assistant Chief of Police/Patrol Bureau coordinates the activities of the eight (8) patrol divisions (KACP 3.3).
1.6.2 PATROL DIVISION COMMANDERS
The Patrol Division Commanders are appointed by the Mayor, upon the recommendation of the Chief of Police, and report directly to the Assistant Chief of Police/Patrol Bureau (Lieutenant Colonel) (refer to SOP 1.11).

sections.title: Support Bureau
sections.text:
1.7 SUPPORT BUREAU
1.7.1 ASSISTANT CHIEF OF POLICE/SUPPORT BUREAU (Lieutenant Colonel)
The Assistant Chief of Police/Support Bureau is appointed by the Mayor, upon the recommendation of the Chief of Police, and reports to the Deputy Chief of Police/Chief of Staff. When mandated by the Chief of Police, the Assistant Chief of Police/Support Bureau may assume all responsibilities as the department’s Chief Executive Officer (CEO) (KACP 4.2).
The Assistant Chief of Police/Support Bureau coordinates the activities of the following (KACP 3.3):
• Major Crimes Division (MCD)
• Special Operations Division (SOD)
• Criminal Interdiction Division (CID)
• Homeland Security Unit (HSU)
1.7.2 MAJOR CRIMES DIVISION (MCD) COMMANDER (Major)
The MCD Commander is appointed by the Mayor, upon the recommendation of the Chief of Police, and reports directly to the Assistant Chief of Police/Support Bureau.
The MCD Commander is responsible for planning the department’s response to unusual criminal activities and coordinating the activities of the following personnel (KACP 3.3):
HOMICIDE UNIT
The Homicide Unit is divided into three (3) squads:
• Homicide Squad: Investigates homicides, fatal shootings, critical assaults, suicides, suspicious deaths, kidnappings for ransom, or missing persons suspected of being victims of violent crimes, who cannot be located. This unit also investigates train vs. pedestrian accidents when the pedestrian is killed or death is imminent.
• Cold Case Squad: Investigates unsolved homicide cases that are at least two (2) years old or are considered “cold” by the Homicide Unit Commander, or their designee.
• Missing Persons Squad: Investigates all missing person reports, except for kidnappings for ransom or the victims of suspected violent crimes who cannot be located.
NON- FATAL SHOOTING UNIT
The Non-Fatal Shooting Unit investigates all non-fatal shootings which occur within the jurisdiction of the Louisville Metro Police Department (LMPD), with the exception of the following:
• Non-fatal shootings that involve a child when the suspect is a caretaker will be investigated by the Office of Sexual and Physical Investigations (OSPI)
1.7.2 MAJOR CRIMES DIVISION COMMANDER (CONTINUED)
• Non-fatal shootings that occur during a domestic violence (DV) incident will be investigated by the Domestic Violence Squad
• Non-fatal shootings that occur during a robbery or carjacking will be investigated by the Robbery/Financial Crimes Unit
• Uncontested self-inflicted shootings and non-criminal accidental shootings will be investigated by division detectives
The Non-Fatal Shooting Unit will place a high emphasis on the Crime Gun Intelligence Model. This model is an interagency collaboration focused on the timely collection, management, and analysis of crime gun evidence to identify shooters, disrupt criminal activity, and prevent future violence. The Crime Gun Intelligence Model primarily uses programs, such as the National Integrated Ballistic Information Network (NIBIN) and the Electronic Tracing (e-Trace) system, in conjunction with human intelligence and additional resources, to identify armed, violent individuals for investigation and prosecution.
Some of the terms applicable to the Crime Gun Intelligence Model include, but are not limited to, the following:
• Crime Guns: Firearms that department members have probable cause to believe have been used during the commission of a crime.
• Crime Gun Intelligence: Facts that include, but are not limited to, information collected and/or developed from seized firearms and ballistics evidence, incident and investigative reports, field interviews, surveillance, seized firearm tracing, laboratory examinations, Including Integrated Ballistics Identification System (IBIS)/NIBIN results and trace evidence and social media monitoring, which are related to illegal firearms use.
• Electronic Tracing (e-Trace) System: An internet-based system that allows participating law enforcement agencies to submit firearm traces to the Bureau of Alcohol, Tobacco, Firearms, and Explosives (ATF) National Tracing Center (NTC).
• Integrated Ballistics Identification System (IBIS): Technology that allows for the digital imaging of fired ammunition components so that they can be correlated against an electronic database of images to determine whether various shooting incidents can be linked to the same firearm or a particular firearm.
• National Integrated Ballistic Information Network (NIBIN) Hit: A confirmed linkage of two (2) or more firearm-related crimes made by two (2) certified firearms examiners.
• National Integrated Ballistic Information Network (NIBIN) Squad: Provides support for all departmental members and outside agencies, via the NIBIN Program which is maintained by the ATF. The NIBIN automates ballistics evaluations and provides actionable investigative leads in a timely manner by analyzing and entering scene cartridge cases and test fires from crime guns. NIBIN technicians enter cartridge casing evidence into the IBIS, where these images are then correlated against the NIBIN database.
Other outcomes of the Crime Gun Intelligence Model include, but are not limited to, the following:
• The identification of crime gun sources
• Efficient resource allocation
• Providing decision-makers with the most accurate crime data available
• Increasing case closure rates
The Non-Fatal Shooting Unit will continue its commitment to the Crime Gun Intelligence Model by having a dedicated Strategic Criminal Intelligence Analyst who will be co-located with the Non-Fatal Shooting Unit. Solving
1.7.2 MAJOR CRIMES DIVISION COMMANDER (CONTINUED)
gun crimes requires well-coordinated teams to manage the exchanges of data and information, as well as a proper balance of people, processes, and technology. The Strategic Criminal Intelligence Analyst will analyze all crime gun data collected from the NIBIN and e-Trace system, or other forensic analysis, and verify it is assessed, leveraged, and lawfully disseminated to appropriately link crimes, guns, and suspects.
ROBBERY/FINANCIAL CRIMES (RFC) UNIT
The RFC Unit is divided into two (2) squads:
• The Robbery Squad:
o Investigates all first-degree and second-degree robberies of retail businesses that operate from a permanent structure, when the intent of the suspect is to commit a robbery in order to obtain money or property from the business. The Robbery Squad also investigates first-degree and second-degree robberies of employees making bank drops or deposits, when a suspect commits the robbery in order to obtain the money being deposited from the business. o Investigates first-degree robberies involving motor vehicles, classified as a “carjacking,” where a firearm or deadly/dangerous instrument is used, or a citizen who is not involved in the crime sustains serious physical injury. The Robbery Squad does not investigate second-degree robberies involving motor vehicles, classified as a “carjacking,” where the victim does not sustain serious physical injury and/or a weapon is not used. o Investigates all first-degree and second-degree robberies of mobile food trucks. This does not include itinerant vendors (e.g., neighborhood ice cream trucks and pushcart vendors), vendors with barbeque smokers on trailers, or temporary food services set up for fairs or festivals (e.g., tents, trailers, or kiosks). o Investigates first-degree and second-degree robberies of financial institutions (e.g., banks and credit unions), pharmacies, armored cars, or armored car couriers in the performance of their duties. o Investigates, upon direction from the MCD Commander, first-degree street robberies that involve the same perpetrator(s) and span multiple divisions.
The Robbery Squad does not investigate robberies of delivery drivers not occurring on the premises of the business or incidents that begin as shoplifting.
• The Financial Crimes Squad:
o Investigates crimes involving forged or counterfeit checks, possession of forgery devices, identity thefts, consumer fraud, business fraud, embezzlement, and pigeon drops. o Conducts inspections of metal salvage and scrap dealers to verify compliance with applicable state statutes and local ordinances and assists members with issues surrounding metal/salvage locations and their role in ongoing investigations. o The Financial Crimes Squad does not investigate any metal thefts, such as catalytic converters. This is the responsibility of division-level detectives.
1.7.2 MAJOR CRIMES DIVISION COMMANDER (CONTINUED)
SPECIAL VICTIMS UNIT (SVU)
The SVU is divided into the following:
• Domestic Violence (DV) Squad: Investigates felony domestic/dating violence and abuse incidents. The Domestic Violence Squad will also follow-up on misdemeanor domestic/dating violence and abuse incidents where beat officers have not made an immediate arrest (refer to SOP 8.6).
• Animal Cruelty Enforcement (ACE) Sergeant: Investigates the correlation between animal abuse and crimes against people, particularly interpersonal violence such as domestic/dating violence and abuse. The ACE Sergeant collaborates with the MCD, SVU, patrol divisions, and Louisville Metro Animal Services (LMAS) Animal Control Officers (ACOs) to identify situations where multiple forms of abuse may be occurring (refer to SOP 8.33).
• The Office of Sexual and Physical Investigations (OSPI) investigates the following:
o Felony sexual assaults; o Misdemeanor sexual assaults involving children; o Physical abuse allegations where a caretaker is the perpetrator; o Reported cases of human trafficking, prostitution, escort services, and violations of the Sex Offender Registry; and o Internet Crimes Against Children (ICAC) cases (i.e., crimes perpetrated against juveniles) involving the use of a computer or other electronic means.
FORENSIC INVESTIGATIONS
Forensic Investigations consists of the following support personnel:
• Crime Scene Unit (CSU): Assists officers or Police Report Technicians (PRTs) at crime scenes by photographing, preserving, collecting, processing, packaging, and transporting evidence.
• National Integrated Ballistic Information Network (NIBIN) Squad: Provides support for all departmental members and outside agencies, via the NIBIN Program, which is maintained by the Bureau of Alcohol, Tobacco, Firearms, and Explosives (ATF). The NIBIN automates ballistics evaluations and provides actionable investigative leads in a timely manner by analyzing and entering scene cartridge cases and test fires from crime guns. NIBIN technicians enter cartridge casing evidence into the Integrated Ballistic Identification System (IBIS), where these images are then correlated against the NIBIN database.
• Latent Print Squad: Assists officers and CSU technicians with the photographing, preserving, analyzing, and processing of latent fingerprint evidence. The Latent Print Squad also evaluates latent evidence for entry into the Integrated Automated Fingerprint Identification System (IAFIS) and the Automated Fingerprint Identification System (AFIS) maintained by the Kentucky State Police (KSP).
• Video Forensics and Analysis Squad (VFAS): Provides support for all departmental members, which include conducting forensic video analysis of surveillance video seized from crime scenes and the videotaping of major crime scenes. The VFAS is also responsible for taping training exercises, special events, and other activities as deemed necessary by the Chief of Police.
• Polygraph Squad: Provides support to investigative units by conducting polygraph investigations and conducts pre-employment polygraph examinations (KACP 13.1).
1.7.2 MAJOR CRIMES DIVISION COMMANDER (CONTINUED)
• Pawn Investigations Squad: Conducts physical examinations of pawn shops/secondhand dealers, inspects the records of pawn shops/secondhand dealers to verify compliance with applicable state statutes and local ordinances, and assists members with issues associated with pawn shops/secondhand dealers or property from pawn shops.
VICTIM SERVICES UNIT (VSU) (Professional Staff Director)
The VSU Director reports directly to the MCD Commander. The VSU provides support to crime victims and witnesses of crimes by assuring that these individuals are treated with respect and dignity and are afforded rights and services designed to address the specific needs of their victimization. VSU Specialists respond to the physical, emotional, and financial needs of crime victims and witnesses through intervention, counseling, outreach, advocacy, and education.
1.7.3 SPECIAL OPERATIONS DIVISION (SOD) COMMANDER (Major)
The Special Operations Division (SOD) Commander is appointed by the Mayor, upon the recommendation of the Chief of Police, and reports directly to the Assistant Chief of Police/Support Bureau.
The SOD Commander coordinates the activities of the following sections/units (KACP 3.3):
SPECIAL EVENTS UNIT
The Special Events Unit facilitates the planning and implementation of public events. The Special Events Unit reviews all permits filed with Louisville Metro Government and determines the amount of assistance that the department may provide.
TRAFFIC UNIT
The Traffic Unit responds to, and investigates, collisions involving fatalities and life-threatening injuries. The Traffic Unit may also investigate collisions on the interstates (KACP 22.1).
COMMUNITY ENGAGEMENT UNIT
The Community Engagement Unit has the primary responsibility of enhancing the department’s community policing initiative by building public trust and addressing crime issues.
SPECIALTY TEAMS/UNITS SECTION
The Specialty Teams/Units Section coordinates the implementation of the following specialty teams and units:
• Air Unit: Provides aerial surveillance, search and apprehension duties, and rescue services.
• River Patrol Unit: Provides waterborne services on the Ohio River, and its tributaries, and within the waters of the department’s jurisdiction.
1.7.3 SPECIAL OPERATIONS DIVISION COMMANDER (CONTINUED)
• Canine Unit: Responds to situations calling for trained police dogs, which include building and area searches, evidence/property recovery, the tracking and apprehension of suspects, and searches for narcotics and hazardous devices.
• Mounted Patrol Unit: Provides patrol support by addressing citizen issues, deterring criminal activity through officer presence, assisting in crowd control at public events, and maintaining increased visibility in targeted areas.
• Special Weapons and Tactics (SWAT) Team: Responds to situations with hostage-takers, barricaded suspects, or other incidents that may involve a threat to human life, where specialized training or equipment could be utilized. The SWAT Team also assists with the execution of high-risk search warrants (KACP 19.6e).
• Hostage Negotiation Team (HNT): Negotiates the surrender of hostage-takers or barricaded suspects and the safe release of hostages, through the effective implementation of the negotiation process (KACP 19.7e).
• Underwater Search and Recovery Unit (USRU): Also known as the “Dive Team.” Provides for the recovery of property, injured persons, and corpses within the waters of the department’s jurisdiction.
• Hazardous Incident Response Team (HIRT): Responds to incidents involving human biological vectors and hazardous material (HAZMAT) situations that require a police presence.
• Bomb Squad: Provides the identification, recovery, transportation, and disposal of explosives and suspected explosive devices.
• Dignitary Protection Team (DPT): Escorts and provides protection for high-profile individuals, such as government officials, dignitaries, and celebrities.
• Honor Guard: Represents the department at ceremonious occasions that include funerals, parades, award ceremonies, and other functions as deemed appropriate by the Chief of Police.
• Special Response Team (SRT): Responds to situations that involve, or might involve, civil disturbances, weapons of mass destruction (WMD), natural disasters, and other major events.
1.7.4 CRIMINAL INTERDICTION DIVISION (CID) COMMANDER (Major)
The CID Commander is appointed by the Mayor, upon the recommendation of the Chief of Police, and reports directly to the Assistant Chief of Police/Support Bureau.
The Administrative Sergeant reports directly to the CID Commander. The Administrative Sergeant’s responsibilities include, but are not limited to, maintaining the daily operational status of the division and directing the operations of the division. The Administrative Sergeant also oversees special projects for the CID Commander.
The CID is divided into five (5) operational units, each under the command of a lieutenant, as follows (KACP 3.3):
The Support Unit performs the listed functions:
• Asset Forfeiture Squad: Tracks and controls all property seized by the CID by assisting detectives in determining the basis for a criminal or civil seizure/forfeiture action.
• Prescription Drug Diversion Squad: Conducts investigations pertaining to all complaints related to forged, altered, or otherwise fraudulent prescriptions. The Prescription Drug Diversion Squad enforces controlled prescription substance offenses involving the use or sale of prescription medications.
1.7.4 CRIMINAL INTERDICTION DIVISION COMMANDER (CONTINUED)
Personnel who are assigned to this unit may be used to perform various functions within the CID.
The Major Case Unit performs the listed functions:
• Major Case Narcotics Squad: Identifies mid-level and upper-level narcotics traffickers and disrupts drug trafficking organizations due to the relationship between narcotics and violence. The squad conducts physical and electronic surveillance operations and facilitates controlled buys of narcotics through the use and development of confidential informants.
• Interdiction Squad: Enforces controlled substance violations that occur through interstate and international commerce.
• Drug Enforcement Agency (DEA)/Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI) Task Force Officers: Work with various federal law enforcement agencies, as assigned.
The Major Case Unit Lieutenant coordinates the registration and record maintenance related to informants who are used by departmental members.
Personnel who are assigned to this unit may be used to perform various functions within the CID.
The Focused Intelligence Unit performs the listed functions:
• Louisville Metro Intelligence (LMINTEL) Squad: Investigates violent street gangs, armed criminals, and criminal enterprises involving gang members, while working with federal partners, including the FBI, the ATF, the DEA, and the Internal Revenue Service (IRS), leading to successful prosecutions at the state and/or federal level.
• Task Force Officers: Work with various federal law enforcement agencies, as assigned.
Personnel who are assigned to this unit may be used to perform various functions within the CID.
The Violent Crime & Fugitive Unit is comprised of the following:
Violent Crime Squads: Address violent crime in the Louisville Metro area utilizing intelligence-led strategies to focus on specific individuals/locations known to be associated with violent criminal activity. Squads will coordinate efforts with detectives at both the LMPD Patrol Division and MCD levels, as well as outside local and federal law enforcement agencies to accomplish the following tasks:
• Apprehending fugitives;
• Investigating and apprehending known violent offenders;
• Gathering intelligence on potentially violent actors;
• Monitoring known gang/violent group members; and
• Disrupting the illegal firearms and narcotics trafficking fueling violent crime in Louisville.
Personnel who are assigned to this unit may be used to perform various functions within the CID.
Fugitive Squad: Responsible for identifying and apprehending fugitives who are known violent offenders.
1.7.4 CRIMINAL INTERDICTION DIVISION COMMANDER (CONTINUED)
The Group Violence Victimology Unit is comprised of the Firearms Intelligence Squad.
Firearms Intelligence Squad: Comprised of detectives who are trained to focus on preserving, documenting, and collecting evidence resulting from firearms-related investigations. Detectives work closely with ATF Agents and Evidence and Property Unit (EPU) Technicians with NIBIN technology to identify perpetrators, link criminal activity, and investigate shooting incidents to disrupt the shooting cycle. The cooperative goal is to reach the next level of efficiency and effectiveness in firearms investigations for increased prosecution, firearm-related convictions, and the reduction of gun-related crime.
The Firearms Intelligence Squad of the Group Violence Victimology Unit will place a high emphasis on the Crime Gun Intelligence Model. This model is an interagency collaboration focused on the timely collection, management, and analysis of crime gun evidence to identify shooters, disrupt criminal activity, and prevent future violence. The Crime Gun Intelligence Model primarily uses programs, such as the NIBIN and the Electronic Tracing (e-Trace) system, in conjunction with human intelligence and additional resources, to identify armed, violent individuals for investigation and prosecution. Other outcomes include, but are not limited to, the following:
• The identification of crime gun sources
• Efficient resource allocation
• Providing decision-makers with the most accurate crime data available
• Increasing case closure rates
The CID also investigates vice-related crimes, such as gambling and handbooks.
1.7.5 HOMELAND SECURITY UNIT (HSU) (Lieutenant)
The HSU Lieutenant reports to the Assistant Chief of Police/Support Bureau and is responsible for coordinating departmental compliance with national preparedness goals.
The HSU investigates actual, or perceived, threats against facilities and events with the potential for mass casualties, as well as threats against high-profile individuals. The HSU investigates suspected terrorism, extremism, organized criminal groups, suspicious powders, and the theft/loss of nuclear, biological, chemical, or explosive material. The HSU also performs special assignments at the discretion of the Assistant Chief of Police/Support Bureau.
An Intelligence Liaison Officer (ILO) will be identified from each division. The ILO facilitates the information flow between their division and the HSU. The ILOs will meet regularly with the HSU and may assist HSU detectives with threat investigations and special assignments.
The HSU acts as the departmental liaison with the Kentucky Intelligence Fusion Center (KIFC) and federal and local law enforcement agencies.
JOINT TERRORISM TASK FORCE (JTTF)
The HSU Lieutenant acts as the departmental liaison with the Joint Terrorism Task Force (JTTF).
1.7.5 HOMELAND SECURITY UNIT (HSU) (CONTINUED)
The JTTF is comprised of locally-based investigators, analysts, and experts from various United States law enforcement and intelligence agencies who investigate threats and incidents related to terrorism and national security. The JTTF provides a single team response and strives to create familiarity among investigators and managers across the state of Kentucky before a crisis occurs.

sections.title: Administrative Bureau
sections.text:
1.8 ADMINISTRATIVE BUREAU
1.8.1 ASSISTANT CHIEF OF POLICE/ADMINISTRATIVE BUREAU (Lieutenant Colonel)
The Assistant Chief of Police/Administrative Bureau is appointed by the Mayor, upon the recommendation of the Chief of Police, and reports directly to the Deputy Chief of Police/Chief of Operations. When mandated by the Chief of Police, the Assistant Chief of Police/Administrative Bureau may assume all responsibilities as the department’s Chief Executive Officer (CEO) (KACP 4.2).
The Assistant Chief of Police/Administrative Bureau coordinates the activities of the following (KACP 3.3):
• Police Human Resources (HR)
• Administrative Services Division
• Executive Administrator of the Louisville Metro Police Department (LMPD) Budget
• Accident Review Board (ARB) (refer to SOP 2.12)
1.8.2 POLICE HUMAN RESOURCES (HR) (Professional Staff Director) (KACP 26.2)
The Police HR Director reports to the Assistant Chief of Police/Administrative Bureau. Police HR is responsible for maintaining records of past and current departmental members (includes all sworn and professional staff personnel). They handle administrative needs with regards to computing payroll, preparing reports, and completing paperwork on the hiring/resigning/terminating of members.
1.8.3 ADMINISTRATIVE SERVICES DIVISION (Major)
The Administrative Services Division Commander is appointed by the Mayor, upon recommendation of the Chief of Police, and reports directly to the Assistant Chief of Police/Administrative Bureau. The Administrative Services Division Commander acts as the departmental liaison with the Louisville Metro Emergency Management Agency (EMA) and is responsible for the following units/services:
STRATEGIC PLANNING (Lieutenant)
The Strategic Planning Lieutenant reports to the Administrative Services Division Commander and is responsible for the following:
• Recruitment and Selection – The Strategic Planning Lieutenant directly supervises the Recruitment and Selection Unit of the LMPD, which includes the testing and background investigations of applicants, as well as recruitment and all marketing/advertisement business.
• Strategic Plan – The Strategic Planning Lieutenant oversees the implementation of the strategic plan for the LMPD.
• Coordinating and managing grants related to the strategic plan.
• Acting as a liaison for Metro Facilities for LMPD property.
• Maintaining the department’s website.
1.8.3 ADMINISTRATIVE SERVICES DIVISION (CONTINUED)
• Creating maps for special events and for use in court.
• Maintaining department-wide performance measures and compiling executive summary reports of these performance measures.
RECORDS MANAGEMENT (Professional Staff Director) (KACP 5.1, 22.4d)
The Records Management Director reports to the Administrative Services Division Commander and is responsible for maintaining the integrity, compilation, security, and retention of data for the department (KACP 26.1). The Records Management Director is also responsible for the planning, implementation, system maintenance, and National Incident Based Reporting System (NIBRS) compliance for the LMPD Records Management System (RMS). The Records Management Director actively participates in the development of policies and procedures related to reporting, case management, evidence retention, and all interfaces with outside software systems that import data into the RMS. Records Management is comprised of the following units:
• Data Integrity Unit (DIU) (Professional Staff Manager and Professional Staff Supervisor): Reviews citations, incident reports, missing person reports, and JC-3 reports to verify compliance with system standards (KACP 22.2). The DIU reviews and validates incident reports and supplemental reports submitted by all LMPD members to verify compliance with the NIBRS, Uniform Crime Report (UCR) (KACP 26.5), and Uniform Offense Report (UOR). The LMPD, through Coplogic, allows incident reports to be taken online for certain crimes (refer to SOP 3.5). The DIU is responsible for reviewing, accepting, and importing online reports into the RMS. The DIU is also responsible for assisting in the preparation of the monthly NIBRS report provided to the Kentucky State Police (KSP) and the Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI).
• Data Resolution Unit (DRU) (Professional Staff Manager and Professional Staff Supervisor): The DRU consists of the following squads:
o Processing Squad: Sorts, processes, and logs all incoming mail and paperwork scanned from LMPD divisions/units. Creates additional logs for all arrests/citations, JC-3 reports, and missing person reports submitted through the Kentucky Open Portal Solution (KYOPS). They pull the portable document format (PDF) reports from the KYOPS and attach to the logs for Data Entry to complete. This work is then completed by personnel in the Central Records Unit (CRU). They receive, through DocuSign, all strangulation and lethality forms related to JC-3 reports and attach these to the incident in the RMS. They contact officers when information is incorrect, or missing, to correct documents to be entered into the RMS. The DRU is responsible for entering all paper Collision Report and Analysis for Safer Highways (CRASH) reports, as well as reviewing and approving electronically-entered CRASH reports. o False Alarm Squad: Implements and oversees the Louisville Metro False Alarm Ordinance. The False Alarm personnel act as liaisons and mediators between the LMPD, the Department of Codes & Regulations, the Office of Management and Budget (OMB), alarm businesses, alarm technicians, and alarm users. The alarms are managed through the Crywolf software. This squad is responsible for processing all Louisville Metro Code of Ordinances (LMCO) Chapter 71 (i.e., speed contest) violations for the Traffic Unit citations.
• Central Records Unit (CRU) (Professional Staff Supervisor): Consists of the following:
1.8.3 ADMINISTRATIVE SERVICES DIVISION (CONTINUED)
o Customer Service: Provides reports to the public, law enforcement officers, other governmental agencies, and private businesses over the phone, via the service window at the Edison Building, located at 701 West Ormsby Avenue, and through mailed/faxed requests and government transfers, in accordance with Kentucky Revised Statute (KRS) 189.635. Clerks collect payments on behalf of the department for official reports generated for customers. o Expungements: Processes court-ordered expungements. Expungement personnel verify that records held within the LMPD database are in compliance with the directives received within court orders. Additionally, personnel expunge juvenile arrest(s) once the individual has reached the age of 23, unless the juvenile was charged as an adult or if the record involved a child abuse case or a traffic offense (refer to SOP 6.1). Personnel are familiar with the RMS, CourtNet, and archiving procedures, which includes storing reports, boxing reports, and completing transmittal and destruction forms for records sent pursuant to an order. o Data Entry: Reviews all data that is imported from the KYOPS into the RMS (missing person reports, JC-3 reports, arrests/citations) to ensure all data is imported and correct. Additionally, they enter information that does not import and correct any discrepancies; attach all arrests/citations, JC-3 reports, missing person reports PDFs from the KYOPS to the corresponding record in the RMS; link all arrests to the related incident and create any additional reports that need to be completed based on the arrest.
• LMPD Service Center (Professional Staff Manager and Professional Staff Supervisors): Approves and rejects employee reports and fulfills open record requests for the audio files of calls and reports taken by the LMPD Service Center. The LMPD Service Center is also responsible for answering all calls that come through the police non-emergency dispatch number and (502) 574-LMPD (5643). Through this line, the LMPD Service Center handles the following types of calls:
o Crime Tips: Enters crime tips into the RMS and then disseminates crime tips to divisions/sections/units to investigate and, at times, helps in providing additional information on previously-reported crimes. o Telephone Reporting Unit (TRU): Completes incident reports, supplemental reports, and missing person reports from the public, via telephone, for various crimes, in lieu of sending an officer to the scene. o Private Tow and Repossessions: Receives calls and checks all of the vehicles that are repossessed, or towed, by private companies through the National Crime Information Center (NCIC) to verify that the vehicles are not stolen and enters the information into the RMS. o Officer Assistance: Provides assistance to officers with completing reports when they are experiencing issues.
EVIDENCE AND PROPERTY UNIT (EPU) (Sergeant)
The EPU Sergeant reports to the Administrative Services Division Commander. The EPU is responsible for the storing, classification, retrieval, and disposal of seized, found, or recovered property and forwarded evidence (including all evidence related to controlled substances) under the protective custody of the LMPD. The EPU safeguards the integrity of all property or evidence (KACP 27.2). Their other duties include maintaining and issuing a limited supply of certain police equipment.
1.8.3 ADMINISTRATIVE SERVICES DIVISION (CONTINUED)
VEHICLE IMPOUNDMENT UNIT (VIU) (Professional Staff Supervisor)
The VIU Supervisor reports to the Administrative Services Division Commander. The VIU is responsible for the impoundment of vehicles that are in violation of traffic regulations, blocking streets/right-of-ways, abandoned in public areas, trespassing on private property, or participating in illegal dumping (refer to SOP 7.9). The VIU is also responsible for providing towing and impoundment services for vehicles identified as nuisances by the Department of Codes & Regulations and clearing streets after vehicular accidents. The unit stores vehicles involved in fatal accidents, arson investigations, and other criminal activity. The VIU collects all towing and storage charges and releases vehicles on-site. Unclaimed vehicles are disposed of at public auctions, pursuant to state law.
FLEET MANAGEMENT (Professional Staff Coordinator)
The Fleet Management Coordinator is a professional staff position and reports to the Administrative Services Division Commander. The Fleet Management Coordinator is responsible for the management of the LMPD fleet budget and works with Metro Fleet Services to manage, operate, repair, and/or replace departmental vehicles.
TECHNICAL OPERATIONS (Lieutenant)
The Technical Operations Lieutenant reports to the Administrative Services Division Commander. The Technical Operations Lieutenant is responsible for the following:
• Technical Investigations (Sergeant): The Technical Investigations Sergeant reports to the Technical Operations Lieutenant. Technical Investigations provides operations support of all specialized investigative equipment and provides expertise in matters regarding electronic surveillance.
• Digital Forensic Unit (DFU) (Sergeant): The DFU Sergeant reports to the Technical Operations Lieutenant. The DFU Sergeant is responsible for the supervision of the DFU and the LMPD personnel who are assigned to the Kentucky Regional Computer Forensic Laboratory (KRCFL). The DFU Sergeant supervises, conducts, and/or actively leads digital forensic examinations. The DFU acts as a departmental liaison with local law enforcement agencies, federal agencies, and private companies. The DFU Sergeant attends meetings and briefings related to digital investigations and coordinates deconfliction efforts with other units within the LMPD and other law enforcement agencies. The DFU also provides technical support to other investigative units within the LMPD.
o KRCFL: The KRCFL personnel report to the DFU Sergeant. The KRCFL provides high-quality digital forensic services and assistance to any law enforcement agency with jurisdiction in the state of Kentucky, including the seizure and examination of computers, computer systems, computer media, and cell phones. The KRCFL is an American National Standards Institute (ANSI) National Accreditation Board (ANAB)-accredited laboratory, guaranteeing examiner qualifications and quality control procedures. Forensic examiners offer court testimony explaining how they conducted their examinations and what they discovered as a result.
1.8.3 ADMINISTRATIVE SERVICES DIVISION (CONTINUED)
• Small Unmanned Aircraft System (SUAS) Unit (Sergeant): The SUAS Sergeant reports to the Technical Operations Lieutenant. The SUAS Unit is responsible for providing aerial support to the department to enhance public safety and operational effectiveness. Core functions include assisting with incident overwatch to gain tactical advantage, intelligence, search and rescue operations, accident and crime scene documentation in accordance with legal standards, and disaster response. The SUAS Unit ensures compliance with FAA 14 CFR Part 107 regulations, departmental policies, and applicable laws while maintaining accurate flight, training, and maintenance records. Additional duties include equipment management, mission planning, airspace deconfliction, and interagency coordination. The SUAS Unit also upholds transparency through data accountability, policy adherence, and post-mission review to promote safety, efficiency, and public trust.
TECHNICAL SERVICES (Professional Staff Director)
The Technical Services Director reports to the Administrative Services Division Commander and assists as a liaison with Metro Technology Services (MTS), MetroSafe, and other Louisville Metro Government (LMG) entities, as needed. The Technical Services Director assists in the planning of the LMPD’s technical needs and special projects and coordinating the maintenance of the LMPD’s technical systems. Technical Services is responsible for maintaining departmental cell phones/smart devices, software, applications, database integrations, and other systems utilized by the LMPD. Technical Services also provides data for the LMPD command staff and for public dissemination, when requested through open records requests by citizens and/or members of the media (KACP 20.2b).
OPEN RECORDS (Professional Staff Director) (KACP 20.2b)
The Open Records Director reports to the Administrative Services Division Commander. Open Records works in conjunction with Louisville Metro Records Compliance to fulfill all open records requests, including Body-Worn Camera (BWC) and Mobile Video System (MVS) requests.
REAL TIME CRIME CENTER (RTCC) (Professional Staff Director)
The RTCC Director reports to the Administrative Services Division Commander, and is responsible for the planning, implementation, system maintenance, and compliance of the Metro Watch camera system, the fixed Flock Automatic License Plate Recognition (ALRP) system, and the Axon Fusus program. The RTCC Director actively participates in the development of policies and procedures, and budgets of these, and several other systems used by the units within the RTCC. The RTCC is comprised of the following units:
• RTCC Unit (Professional Staff Manager): The RTCC is a centralized hub that is responsible for providing real-time tactical support to sworn personnel by utilizing technology and information systems. Responsibilities of the RTCC include, but are not limited to, the following:
o Proactively monitoring Metro Watch cameras and relaying any significant activities (e.g., civil disturbances and/or disorderly crowds) to MetroSafe dispatchers and officers. o Monitoring MetroSafe dispatch communications to provide real-time intelligence and information before, during, and after officers arrive on the scene of a dispatched call.
1.8.3 ADMINISTRATIVE SERVICES DIVISION (CONTINUED)
o Providing ongoing strategic and tactical support for officers during critical incidents, significant activities, Special Weapons and Tactics (SWAT) Team callouts (e.g., civil disturbances and/or disorderly crowds), special events, and major disasters. o Researching and providing intelligence and information to officers in response to requests for information regarding current, or ongoing, investigations or calls for service. o Relaying Wanted flyers (LMPD #06-0046), Attempt to Locate (ATL) flyers (LMPD #06-0047), “Be- on-the-Lookouts” (BOLOs), etc. between other local regional agencies. o Responding to internal and external requests for data. o Providing officers with intelligence and informational bulletins. o Assessing the need for the real-time deployment of additional sworn personnel and expressing those needs to MetroSafe dispatch. o Creating and disseminating daily and weekly reports, such as the Significant Activities Report and the Weekly Events Report.
• Strategic Criminal Intelligence Unit (SCIU) (Professional Staff Manager): The SCIU is a team of strategic analysts housed in a centralized hub with analysts embedded in multiple divisions and units. The strategic analysts review crimes data, patterns, and intelligence to provide support to commanders and the Chief of Police for the development of strategies to enhance public safety. Strategic Criminal Intelligence Analysts complete tasks including, but not limited to, the following:
o Intelligence analysis for complex investigations consisting of many cases, long-term investigations, or incidents connected to subject(s) who are believed to be involved with an organized crime group(s). o Organized crime group/gang identification through the validation of organized crime group(s)/gang(s), per KRS 506. o Researching and providing intelligence and information to officers in response to requests for information regarding ongoing investigations. o Providing officers with intelligence and informational bulletins including prisoner releases, prisoner escapes, and repeat offenders within divisions. o Link analysis to further analyze and identify relationships between subjects, locations, vehicles, weapons, etc. o Maintaining the CrimeNtel intelligence database pursuant to 28 CFR Part 23 standards. o Utilizing crime-mapping technology. o Disseminating weekly reports regarding violent crimes. o Other projects regarding the strategic intelligence analysis of individuals, locations, connections, etc., as requested.
1.8.4 EXECUTIVE ADMINISTRATOR OF LMPD BUDGET (Professional Staff) (KACP 8.2)
The Executive Administrator acts as the departmental liaison with the OMB and reports to the Assistant Chief of Police/Administrative Bureau. The Executive Administrator is responsible for the department’s fiscal management functions and the internal monitoring and auditing of the department’s internal budget (KACP 8.5). The Executive Administrator receives written recommendations from the supervisors of the different departmental areas, based on operational and activity analysis, for use in formulating the department’s budget
1.8.4 EXECUTIVE ADMINISTRATOR OF LMPD BUDGET (CONTINUED)
(KACP 8.3). The OMB is responsible for collecting, safeguarding, and dispersing cash by maintaining an allotment system, preparing financial statements, and conducting internal audits of information provided by the custodial personnel who oversee petty cash or investigative funds and who have been appointed by the division/section/unit commander (refer to SOP 8.37) (KACP 8.6a-d).
The LMPD Grant Writer reports to the Executive Administrator of the LMPD Budget and is responsible for researching, identifying, securing, and managing grant funding to support the agency's mission and strategic goals. This role requires a strong understanding of law enforcement needs, grant-writing principles, and federal, state, and local funding opportunities.

sections.title: Special Investigations Division/Professional Standards Division
sections.text:
1.9 SPECIAL INVESTIGATIONS DIVISION (SID)/PROFESSIONAL STANDARDS DIVISION (PSD)
1.9.1 SPECIAL INVESTIGATIONS DIVISION (SID) COMMANDER (MAJOR)
The SID Commander of the Louisville Metro Police Department (LMPD) is appointed by the Mayor, upon the recommendation of the Chief of Police, and reports directly to the Chief of Police. The SID Commander coordinates the activities of the Public Integrity Unit (PIU) and assists in officer reinstatement when the officer is returning from certain types of leave (refer to SOP 2.5, SOP 2.11, and SOP 8.12).
Public Integrity Unit (PIU) (Lieutenant)
The PIU is responsible for conducting criminal investigations of departmental members, as well as conducting criminal investigations of Louisville Metro employees suspected of committing a felony or an offense involving the physical or sexual abuse of a minor. If a criminal investigation of a departmental member has already been initiated by another law enforcement agency, the PIU is responsible for monitoring the investigation. The PIU will be notified when a departmental member or Louisville Metro employee has been charged with a crime, or is alleged to have committed a crime, by the commanding officer of the division responsible for the investigation in question.
The PIU is also responsible for investigating:
• Officer-involved incidents resulting in the death or serious physical injury to persons while in the custody of departmental personnel or while incarcerated at the Louisville Metro Department of Corrections (LMDC), including inmates on the Home Incarceration Program (HIP) (KACP 1.11b).
• All traffic-related deaths, or serious physical injuries, resulting from pursuits or other officer-involved traffic collisions. These incidents will be investigated in conjunction with the Traffic Unit. The Traffic Unit will not investigate minor injuries involving pursuits or other officer-involved traffic collisions (KACP 23.1a).
• Incidents where an officer’s actions resulted in the death or serious physical injury to the public or to another officer (KACP 1.11b).
• Other officer-related incidents resulting in the death or serious physical injury to the public (KACP 1.11b).
• Incidents resulting in the death or serious physical injury to a departmental member while in the performance of their official duties.
• Incidents involving the discharge of firearms by an officer during police action, regardless of injuries. The only exceptions are departmental members discharging firearms for target practice or the humane destruction of animals (KACP 1.11a).
• Negligent or accidental discharges of firearms that cause injury (refer to SOP 4.13.15 for non-injury discharges).
• Incidents involving the discharge of a firearm at an officer, regardless of injuries.
In order to engender public trust, the PIU will complete its investigations in a timely manner, while ensuring thorough and complete investigations that meet all applicable law.
1.9.2 PROFESSIONAL STANDARDS DIVISION (PSD) COMMANDER (MAJOR)
The Professional Standards Division (PSD) Commander of the LMPD is appointed by the Mayor, upon the recommendation of the Chief of Police, and reports directly to the Chief of Police. The PSD Commander coordinates the activities of the Professional Standards Unit (PSU). The PSD Commander assists in officer reinstatement when the officer is returning from certain types of leave (refer to SOP 2.5, SOP 2.11, and SOP 8.12).
Professional Standards Unit (PSU) (Lieutenant)
The PSU is responsible for conducting internal, administrative investigations of departmental members and administering the department’s drug testing program. A record of all disciplinary actions issued by the Chief of Police is maintained by the PSU (refer to SOP 2.11).
In order to engender public trust, the PSU will complete its investigations in a timely manner, while ensuring thorough and complete investigations that meet all applicable law.

sections.title: Training
sections.text:
1.10 TRAINING
1.10.1 POLICY
It is the policy of the Louisville Metro Police Department (LMPD) to train LMPD members in order to provide a professional standard of law enforcement service to the community.
LMPD members will be trained, with sworn members receiving training as recruits and all members on a continuing basis. LMPD recruits will be trained with an emphasis on developing their interactions with the community, reasoning ability, and judgment. All LMPD officers are required to attend yearly in-service trainings in which preexisting knowledge is reinforced and new information and skills are taught.
To facilitate this policy, the LMPD has a Training Division which operates and maintains the LMPD Training Academy. The Training Division has priority usage of the Training Academy and its equipment.
1.10.2 TRAINING DIVISION (Major)
The Training Division Commander is appointed by the Mayor, upon the recommendation of the Chief of Police, and reports directly to the Assistant Chief of Police/Accountability and Improvement Bureau (AIB). Training Division instructors are Kentucky Law Enforcement Council (KLEC)-certified. Other LMPD members may be utilized as instructors, based on special skills, experience, and other needs.
The responsibilities of the LMPD Training Division include, but are not limited to, the following:
• Maintaining and updating all personnel training records for the department
• Developing, coordinating, and implementing training programs and curriculum for the department, including the following:
o Basic training o In-service training o Firearms qualifications o Remedial training o Department mandated re-certification classes o State mandated re-certification classes o Career development courses o Legal updates o Law enforcement seminars o Kentucky Law Enforcement Council (KLEC) compliance o Field Training Officer (FTO)/Field Training Sergeant (FTS) Programs o Veterans Affairs (VA) Program
1.10.3 SWORN MEMBER TRAINING REQUIREMENTS
Each officer, having responsibility for the enforcement of criminal laws in general, will graduate from a basic training program certified by the KLEC, prior to the exercise of such authority (KACP 14.1). The basic training curriculum encompasses those duties, skills, responsibilities, and actions that are job-related and includes tests/evaluations to measure the officer’s competency in these areas.
Upon graduation from the basic training program, sworn members are placed on a probationary period of at least one (1) year before the member is granted permanent status. The probationary period allows for the observation of the member’s performance and assistance in their new position. The probationary period may be extended up to six (6) additional months based upon just cause as determined by the Chief of Police.
Every sworn member who is assigned to a detective position will successfully complete at least 32 hours of investigative training that has been approved by the KLEC prior to, or as soon as practical after, being assigned to the position. When members are chosen for a detective position, their division commander, or their designee, will contact the Training Division Commander and request that the member be assigned to an approved investigative training class at the earliest available opportunity.
Every sworn member who is promoted to sergeant will successfully complete at least 40 hours of supervisory training that has been approved by the KLEC prior to, or within one (1) year of, such appointment or promotion (KACP 14.2).
Every sworn member who is promoted to lieutenant, or above, will successfully complete at least 40 hours of management training that has been approved by the KLEC prior to, or within one (1) year of, such appointment or promotion (KACP 14.3).
Every sworn member, having responsibility for the enforcement of criminal laws in general, will attend and complete at least 40 hours of certified in-service training annually, as assigned (KACP 14.4). This training includes relevant local, state, and federal legal updates which have recently been passed/enacted, annual updates on departmental use of force policies, and emergency vehicle operation procedures (KACP 21.1h). Sworn members will also qualify with departmentally-authorized firearms, twice annually, which is coordinated by the Firearms Training Center (FTC) (refer to SOP 4.13). One (1) firearms qualification session is held in low- light conditions (KACP 1.10a). Firearms qualifications will be properly documented for the member’s file and monitored by a certified firearms instructor (KACP 1.10b). Members who fail to qualify with their authorized firearm(s) will be subject to remedial training and successful requalification before they can resume their law enforcement duties.
1.10.4 PROFESSIONAL STAFF MEMBER TRAINING REQUIREMENTS
Newly-hired professional staff members are placed on a probationary period of at least six (6) months, but no longer than one (1) year, before the member is granted permanent status. Crime Scene Unit (CSU) technicians are placed on a probationary period of at least one (1) year before the technician is granted permanent status. The probationary period allows for the observation of the member’s performance and assistance in their new position. The probationary period may be extended at the discretion of Louisville Metro Civil Service.
1.10.4 PROFESSIONAL STAFF MEMBER TRAINING REQUIREMENTS (CONTINUED)
Professional staff members will receive information on the following, upon appointment to their positions:
• The department’s mission, goals, policies, and procedures
• Working conditions and regulations
• Employee’s responsibilities and rights
The following professional staff positions require pre-service and/or in-service training:
• Traffic Guards (refer to SOP 8.41)
• Police Report Technicians (PRTs) (refer to SOP 8.38)
• CSU Technicians
1.10.5 FIELD TRAINING OFFICER (FTO) PROGRAM
After graduating from the basic academy, the probationary officer (PO) begins the 800-hour FTO Program.
POs are supervised and evaluated to verify that their performance is in compliance with departmental policies and procedures and applicable laws (refer to SOP 2.21) (KACP 16.4).
Upon the successful completion of the FTO Program, the PO begins the Solo phase of training until their one (1)-year probationary period is complete. In this phase, the PO operates as a patrol officer independent of an FTO. However, the PO is still considered an officer in the training process and can be placed back with an FTO or Field Training Evaluator (FTE) in order to identify and/or address specific issues and to receive remedial training.
FTO candidates must have a minimum of three (3) years sworn service with the department and the selection process includes the following (KACP 14.5a):
• Interested officers must submit an FTO Application (LMPD #06-0045), through the appropriate chain of command, to the Training Division. The Training Division will advise officers when applications are being accepted.
• Files are developed for each applicant that includes, but is not limited to, the following information:
o Peer survey reviews o Disciplinary history o Performance evaluations o Supervisor recommendations o FTO Selection Committee’s recommendations based upon the applicant’s comprehensive interview
• The FTO Selection Committee will compile a list, from the files, of the applicants who are recommended to proceed through the FTO basic training course and will forward the list to the Training Division Commander.
• The Training Division Commander reviews the applicants’ files, the list, and makes the final selection(s).
1.10.5 FIELD TRAINING OFFICER (FTO) PROGRAM (CONTINUED)
• The division commanders are notified of the results.
• Applicants are then notified and those who are chosen to proceed must successfully complete the 24- hour FTO basic training course (KACP 14.5b).
• Officers who successfully complete the 24-hour FTO basic training course will then become certified FTOs.
• FTEs will be officers who have successfully completed the 24-hour FTO basic training course and who are certified FTOs.
FTOs, FTEs, and Field Training Sergeants (FTSs) fall under the command of the Training Division Commander and their division commander. The FTOs and FTEs are directly supervised by the FTSs in their respective divisions. Each of the eight (8) regular patrol divisions has two (2) FTSs. The FTSs review the associated FTO Program paperwork that they receive from the FTOs and FTEs, make recommendations, and forward the paperwork, through the appropriate division chain of command, to the FTO Coordinator at the Training Division (refer to SOP 2.21) (KACP 14.5c-d).
1.10.6 REMEDIAL TRAINING
A member’s performance may require remedial training in certain areas, including firearms qualifications. Supervisors will coordinate remedial training with the Training Division. The following forms of remedial training are offered by the Training Division:
• Remedial training for firearms
• Remedial driver’s training
• Specialized remedial training at the request of the supervisor or officer (e.g., search and seizure, use of force, interview techniques, etc.)
If members fail to successfully complete mandated remedial training, disciplinary action, up to, and including, termination may result.
1.10.7 SPECIALIZED TRAINING
Specialty teams/units require members to successfully complete specialized training (refer to SOP 1.7.3). The commanders of specialty teams/units are responsible for coordinating and mandating the specialized training for their teams/units and must provide the Training Division with training documentation for each member’s file, including training attendance rosters. The commanders of specialty teams/units are also responsible for coordinating any retraining that is needed by members who are under their command (KACP 19.7c).
SWAT Team members also regularly engage in training and readiness exercises (KACP 19.6c). These exercises are in addition to the initial training that a member must successfully complete before becoming a SWAT Team member.
1.10.8 CAREER DEVELOPMENT
The Training Division administers career development courses for the purposes of enhancing the member’s knowledge and performance within the department. Training Division personnel who conduct career development courses will receive classroom training on the techniques and skills needed to effectively administer career development courses based on KLEC requirements.
Career development courses are offered in several areas, including, but not limited to, the following:
• Patrol
• Investigations
• Management
1.10.9 ATTENDANCE
Members will be punctual in reporting to departmentally-elected and mandated training programs. Attendance exceptions are granted on a case-by-case basis. If a member is unable to attend training due to court requirements or a personal emergency, they will advise their commanding officer and the Training Division as soon as possible. Training does not automatically excuse a member from appearing in court (refer to SOP 8.2) and court does not automatically excuse a member from attending training. If a member misses more than ten percent (10%) of a training class, they are required to enroll in another training class.
Members will provide the Training Division with copies of any certifications received in an outside training class in order to update the member’s training record at the Training Division.
1.10.10 TRAINING REIMBURSEMENT
Members may be reimbursed for certain charges incurred as a result of out-of-town travel for training (refer to SOP 2.18).
1.10.11 SHIFT BRIEFING TRAINING
The department briefs officers of important and relevant information at roll-calls and through other forms of correspondence (e.g., interdepartmental mail, email, etc.). All policy updates and numbered correspondence are distributed to members, via email. Members will acknowledge that they have read and understood all policies, General Orders, Special Orders, and General Memorandums using the PowerDMS Document Management System. If members do not have computer access, they will acknowledge that they have read and understood all policies, General Orders, Special Orders, and General Memorandums by signing an accountability roster (KACP 4.6d). Members are responsible for reading all correspondence requiring acknowledgement within ten (10) calendar days of the date of issuance or be subject to disciplinary action. Each division/section/unit is responsible for running monthly compliance reports for its members in PowerDMS for accountability purposes (refer to SOP 3.4).
1.10.11 SHIFT BRIEFING TRAINING (CONTINUED)
In certain situations, the Training Division distributes videos, or other forms of electronic media, for training purposes. Members will acknowledge that they have read/viewed the training documents and understood all areas of the distributed training using the PowerDMS Document Management System. If members do not have computer access, they will acknowledge that they have read/viewed and understood all areas of the distributed training by signing an accountability roster (KACP 4.6d). Members are responsible for reading/viewing all distributed training documents requiring acknowledgement within ten (10) calendar days of the date of issuance or be subject to disciplinary action. Each division/section/unit is responsible for running monthly compliance reports for its members in PowerDMS for accountability purposes (refer to SOP 3.4).
1.10.12 ETHICS TRAINING
All members will receive initial training on departmental ethical standards of conduct. The Training Division is responsible for providing members with additional ethics training at least once every two (2) years.
1.10.13 FIRE EXTINGUISHER TRAINING (KACP 29.5)
The Training Division is responsible for providing all members with fire extinguisher training upon appointment and annually thereafter.
1.10.14 YOUTH PROGRAM TRAINING
The LMPD is host to numerous youth-related programs. LMPD employees and volunteers interact with youths on a daily basis, and the protection of our youths is of the utmost importance. It is also important that LMPD employees and volunteers are protected.
All LMPD employees and volunteers (including youth volunteers) will receive the LMPD’s Guidelines and Procedures Training for youth-related programs. Partnering agency volunteers who assist with LMPD-related youth programs and/or events more than once a year will also be subject to this training.
The LMPD’s Guidelines and Procedures Training will be conducted by the Training Division for all LMPD employees. The Volunteer Coordinator of the Community Engagement Unit (CEU) will conduct the training for all volunteers.
It is the responsibility of the appropriate division commander to verify the mandated training and vetting of volunteers has been conducted by the CEU before the volunteers are allowed to participate in a division-level program and/or event (refer to SOP 2.23).
1.10.15 ACCREDITATION
All personnel receive information on the departmental accreditation process. This information may be in the form of an email or memorandum. The departmental accreditation process consists of the compliance with Kentucky
1.10.15 ACCREDITATION (CONTINUED)
Association of Chiefs of Police (KACP) standards.
Departmental members receive information on the departmental accreditation process as follows:
• Within 30 days after their employment begins or within 30 days after completing basic training
• During the self-assessment phase associated with achieving initial accreditation
• Prior to an on-site assessment
The Research and Development (R&D) Supervisor acts as the departmental accreditation manager and will receive specialized accreditation manager training within one (1) year of being appointed to the position.

sections.title: Patrol Division Organization
sections.text:
1.11 PATROL DIVISION ORGANIZATION
1.11.1 DEFINITIONS
Calls for Service: Any requests for assistance from the public, emergency or non-emergency, resulting in the dispatch of at least one (1) member. Each call for service is assigned a unique Computer Aided Dispatch (CAD) number from MetroSafe.
Self-Initiated Activity: Any duties performed by patrol officers that are proactive in nature. Self-initiated activity includes crime detection and deterrence, providing a visible presence of law enforcement in the community, and assisting the public, as needed or as appropriate. Self-initiated activity does not include general patrol, administrative duties, or personal business (e.g., getting gas, eating meals, etc.).
1.11.2 CONFIGURATION
The Louisville Metro jurisdictional boundaries of the department are divided into eight (8) patrol divisions. Division responsibilities include the protection of life and property of the citizens, enforcement of the laws of the Commonwealth of Kentucky and the ordinances of Louisville Metro, and the prevention of criminal activities through the constant patrol of designated beats (KACP 3.2, 3.3).
1.11.3 PATROL DIVISION STRUCTURE AND ASSIGNMENTS (KACP 17.5)
Division Commander (Major): Responsibilities include, but are not limited to, overseeing all operations of the patrol division to which they are assigned. The division commander is appointed by the Mayor, upon the recommendation of the Chief of Police, and reports directly to the Assistant Chief of Police/Patrol Bureau.
