Members of the Recruitment and Selection Unit of the Administrative Services Division are responsible for the administration of the recruitment plan. The recruitment plan includes elements of the demographic/geographic characteristics of the city and also includes past successful recruitment initiatives/efforts of the LMPD and comparable law enforcement agencies. The recruitment plan includes the following:
• Statement of objectives
• Plan of action to achieve these objectives
The Recruitment and Selection Unit conducts a monthly analysis report of the recruitment plan. The analysis includes the following:
• Evaluation procedures to measure the progress toward the stated objectives
• The results of the recruitment efforts, such as the number of applicants from each source and the number of successful hires
• Any revisions to the plan, as needed
2.27.2 EQUAL EMPLOYMENT OPPORTUNITY (KACP 13.2)
The LMPD strives to offer equal employment opportunities on the basis of merit, without unlawful discrimination, and fills positions without regard to a person’s actual or perceived race, ethnicity/national origin, gender, gender identity/expression, sexual orientation, marital status, religion, socio-economic status, housing status, occupation, disability, age, politics, or other similar personal characteristics. The LMPD offers employment and promotional positions based on applicable federal law, Kentucky law, Louisville Metro Civil Service Board Rules and Regulations, Louisville Metro Police Merit Board Rules and Regulations, Louisville Metro Government (LMG) Personnel Policies, and current collective bargaining agreements (CBAs) (KACP 15.4).
If a member believes that they have been subjected to discrimination, they should report the incident to their supervisor, commanding officer, or Police Human Resources (HR) without delay.
2.27.3 EMPLOYMENT VACANCY ANNOUNCEMENTS
Louisville Metro HR is responsible for posting employment vacancies on the city’s website. Louisville Metro HR and/or the LMPD Recruitment and Selection Unit also advertise employment vacancies through other electronic
2.27.3 EMPLOYMENT VACANCY ANNOUNCEMENTS (CONTINUED)
media, print media, and community/social service organizations. These postings include, but are not limited to, the following:
• A description of the duties, responsibilities, requisite skills, educational level, and other minimum requirements or qualifications to be met by the applicant
• The notice that the LMPD is an equal opportunity employer
• The filing/closing date for the position
2.27.4 EMPLOYMENT APPLICATION PROCESS (KACP 13.1)
Louisville Metro HR, the Louisville Metro Civil Service Board, and the Louisville Metro Police Merit Board are responsible for accepting applications for employment vacancies within the LMPD. Louisville Metro HR, the Louisville Metro Civil Service Board, the Louisville Metro Police Merit Board, and/or the LMPD Recruitment and Selection Unit are also responsible for notifying applicants of application errors or omissions, important testing dates, and the final employment determination/disposition. Applications will not be rejected due to simple errors or omissions which can be quickly corrected.
The LMPD’s employment application process is in accordance with Louisville Metro Civil Service Board Rules and Regulations, Louisville Metro Police Merit Board Rules and Regulations, and LMG Personnel Policies. The employment application process is administered, scored, evaluated, and interpreted in a uniform manner, regardless of the desired position, by Louisville Metro HR, the Louisville Metro Civil Service Board, and the Louisville Metro Police Merit Board. The application process for sworn personnel consists of elements that are job-related (e.g., written examination, medical examination, psychological evaluation, etc.) in order to measure the applicant’s fitness for duty as a sworn officer.
The elements of the application process may consist of, but are not limited to, the following:
• Initial written application;
• Physical agility or proficiency;
• Job-related skills evaluation/examination;
• Oral interview;
• Background investigation/check;
• Polygraph examination (refer to SOP 8.28);
• Psychological examination/evaluation (refer to SOP 2.19); or
• Medical examination/evaluation (refer to SOP 2.19).
At the time of the individual’s formal application, candidates for all positions will be notified, in writing, of the following by Louisville Metro HR:
• All elements of the selection process.
• The expected duration of the application process for sworn positions.
• The process of reapplication, if the initial application is denied/rejected.
2.27.4 EMPLOYMENT APPLICATION PROCESS (CONTINUED)
Background investigations of each candidate will be conducted prior to employment. The background investigations will be conducted by personnel who are trained and knowledgeable in obtaining the required information. Background investigations consist of, but are not limited to, the following:
• A verification of qualifying credentials;
• A review of any criminal record; and
• A verification of at least two (2) personal references and two (2) professional references.
Background investigation materials are retained pursuant to applicable records retention schedules.
All who are applicants not selected for positions are informed, in writing, by the LMPD Recruitment and Selection Unit. The application records of those who are not selected for appointment are retained pursuant to applicable records retention schedules.
2.27.5 EMPLOYMENT APPLICATION RECORD RETENTION
All employment records (e.g., applications, forms, evaluations, etc.) will remain secure and confidential and accessed only by those individuals who are authorized to do so. Louisville Metro HR and the Administrative Services Division are responsible for the retention. The retention and disposal of all employment records (e.g., applications, forms, evaluations, etc.) is pursuant to applicable records retention schedules.

sections.title: Early Intervention Program
sections.text:
2.28 EARLY INTERVENTION PROGRAM (EIP)
2.28.1 POLICY
The purpose of the Louisville Metro Police Department’s (LMPD’s) Early Intervention Program (EIP) is to actively intervene and provide guidance and assistance to members who may be experiencing personal issues or displaying at-risk, or potentially problematic, behavior. The EIP will allow supervisors to monitor, identify, and guide members who may be in need of such assistance.
The EIP is a non-disciplinary and non-punitive program and will not be utilized for investigative or promotional purposes; it will only be used for employee assistance and well-being. It will be applied without discrimination and in a fair and equitable manner to promote and maintain the highest professional standards of performance and accountability, while preserving the privacy rights of each member.
2.28.2 DEFINITIONS
At-risk Behavior: The involvement in incidents and/or conduct that shows a pattern of behavior that, even if not a violation of LMPD policies and/or procedures, could be potentially detrimental to the member, their career, the department, or the community.
Early Intervention Performance Observation Form: An electronic entry in Smartsheet documenting an EIP meeting and the early intervention development plan. The form can be found on the LMPD Intranet by clicking on the “Electronic Forms” link.
EIPro: The database which utilizes specific incident-type information tracked by IAPro and allows supervisors to monitor a members’ standard deviation from their peers within a specific peer group.
EIP Coordinator: The person who administers and maintains the EIP.
EIP Meeting: A meeting between a supervisor and employee in a non-disciplinary and non-punitive setting to discuss the employee’s performance, using techniques designed to reinforce good performance, improve poor performance, and, when appropriate, correct potentially problematic behavior.
IAPro: The database utilized to track administrative investigations and Administrative Incident Reports (AIRs). Utilizing that information, the system feeds specific incident-type information into EIPro.
Purview: The dashboard of users who are under a commanding officer’s direct supervision.
Standard Deviation: An analytic measure of the amount of variation a member is from the mean within a specific peer group. There are three (3) levels of standard deviation used within EIPro. Each level is indicated with a different color.
• Standard Deviation (Level 1): The color yellow indicates a low standard deviation which advises the member has slightly deviated from the mean within a specific peer group.
2.28.2 DEFINITIONS (CONTINUED)
• Standard Deviation (Level 2): The color orange indicates the member has deviated further from the mean within a specific peer group.
• Standard Deviation (Level 3): The color red indicates the member has deviated over a wider range of the mean within a specific peer group.
Wellness Check: A contact initiated by the EIP Coordinator to check and discuss the member’s well-being.
2.28.3 EIP UTILIZATION (KACP 4.7a)
EIP Coordinator (KACP 4.7c)
The EIP Coordinator will monitor EIPro and Early Intervention Performance Observation form entries to maintain departmental compliance within the EIP.
Supervisor Role (KACP 4.7d)
The member’s supervisor is often the first to recognize changes in behavior and/or performance. Therefore, supervisors are the key to early intervention and a successful outcome. Supervisors are encouraged to speak with those under their command whenever changes in behavior and/or performance are noticed. If a member does not feel comfortable speaking to their supervisor, the supervisor will refer the member to another supervisor, Police Human Resources (HR), the departmental psychologist, the EIP Coordinator, or the Employee Assistance Program (EAP) (refer to SOP 2.17) (KACP 4.7f).
The EIP is not intended to replace, but rather supplement, the responsibility and authority of the immediate supervisor whose role it is to observe, guide, and, when necessary, correct the actions of their subordinates.
IAPro (KACP 4.7c)
As supervisors enter AIRs into BlueTeam, the database will track the number and types of incidents for each involved member and add them to EIPro for review.
The types of incidents tracked that contribute to EIPro analytics are as follows (KACP 4.7b):
• Use of force incidents
• Firearm discharges
• Vehicle pursuits
• Chief of Police-initiated investigations
• Citizen affidavits of complaint
• Discipline not handled by the Professional Standards Division (PSD), to include at-fault vehicle collisions
The EIP relies upon the understanding that individual incidents may be justified but, when reviewed collectively, may indicate a pattern of behavior that may warrant intervention.
2.28.3 EIP UTILIZATION (CONTINUED)
EIPro
Once incidents have been entered into EIPro, supervisors will be able to review members who fall under their supervision. The members will be compared to others within a set peer group and those who fall outside of the standard deviation will be identified within the system. Supervisors will be required to login once per work week and utilize EIPro as a supervisory tool. The purview will determine the data and analysis the user has available to them. Each supervisor will check their custom peer group to determine if standard deviation has applied to a member who is under their purview and determine if intervention is needed.
2.28.4 EIPRO PROCEDURES (KACP 4.7c-d)
All supervisors are required to oversee and address any members who are within their purview and fall outside of the standard deviation.
Majors
Majors will be responsible for all members who are within their purview and make certain supervisors utilize EIPro as a supervisory tool for identifying members who fall outside of the standard deviation. Majors will be required to login to EIPro once per work week and review.
Lieutenants
Each quarter, lieutenants will be required to conduct a review of the prior three (3) months and identify outliers.
• Standard Deviation Levels 1 and 2 (yellow and orange): Members who fall under standard deviation levels 1 and 2 will have a review completed by their lieutenant. The lieutenant is responsible for identifying if an EIP meeting and/or further intervention is needed. If an EIP meeting is required based on their review, the lieutenant will follow the same steps as Level 3. If the review of the officer showed no need for further intervention, no further action is needed.
• Standard Deviation Level 3 (red): Members who fall under standard deviation level 3 will have a mandatory EIP meeting with the reviewing lieutenant and the member’s sergeant. After the EIP meeting, the lieutenant will complete an Early Intervention Performance Observation Smartsheet form, located on the LMPD Intranet by clicking on the “Electronic Forms” link. The report will document the member who is identified and a detailed development plan. The Early Intervention Performance Observation form will be forwarded to the EIP Coordinator. It is the responsibility of the lieutenant to follow-up on any developmental plan.
Lieutenants will be required to check EIPro once per work week to review their purview. If, during their weekly review, they observe a member who has quickly escalated in standard deviation levels, they are to review the member and determine if an EIP meeting and/or further intervention is required. If no intervention is required, they can document the member during their quarterly review. If an EIP meeting is required based on a weekly review, the lieutenant will follow the same steps as their quarterly review.
2.28.4 EIPRO PROCEDURES (CONTINUED)
Occasionally, a lieutenant will review EIPro and there will be no members who fall outside of the standard deviation. In those circumstances, during the quarterly review only, the lieutenant will advise their respective major and notify the EIP Coordinator that a review of the EIPro was conducted but no members required intervention during that time.
Sergeants
Sergeants will be required to login and review the EIPro Dashboard once per work week. Sergeants will use the information within the dashboard for their supervision. If, during their weekly review, they observe a member who has quickly escalated in deviation levels, they are to advise the lieutenant and they will review to determine if an EIP meeting and/or further intervention is required.
2.28.5 EIP MEETING (KACP 4.7c-d)
When a lieutenant reviews EIPro and recognizes that a member who is under their purview has fallen outside of the standard deviation and requires intervention, the lieutenant will conduct an EIP meeting. No more than two (2) commanding officers will attend the EIP meeting with the member. The member will be notified that they have fallen outside of the standard deviation and will be given the opportunity to discuss any action or incidents resulting in the standard deviation during the EIP meeting. Regardless of whether it is needed at the time of the EIP meeting, the lieutenant must give a copy of the LMPD Wellness Resource document to each officer for their use.
Prior to the EIP meeting, the member’s supervising lieutenant and immediate supervisor will review the incidents and/or behaviors which resulted in the EIP meeting, along with any other necessary materials, to determine if any trends or patterns are probable. Some suggested resources would include, but are not limited to, the following:
• Use of sick leave
• Recent Mobile Video System (MVS) or Body-Worn Camera (BWC) recordings
• Activity levels and paperwork
• Administrative investigations
• Secondary employment activity
• Performance evaluations
• Questionable social media posts
The purpose of the EIP meeting is to:
• Help the member recognize a pattern of potentially at-risk or problematic behavior;
• Provide guidance to prevent future reoccurrence of problematic performance;
• Advise the member of departmental resources available to meet their individual needs;
• Commend positive work and behavior;
• Provide guidance in career development;
• Encourage the member’s participation in the process; and
• Provide a tool to help commanding officers lead their subordinates.
2.28.5 EIP MEETING (CONTINUED)
Upon the completion of the EIP meeting, the member’s lieutenant will complete the Early Intervention Performance Observation Smartsheet form. The entry will note whether there is a need for further intervention. If intervention is required, a member development plan will be noted with the type of intervention selected.
If needed, members will be provided with the resources necessary to obtain assistance with personal and professional issues. These resources include, but are not limited to, the following (KACP 4.7f):
• Referral to the departmental psychologist
• Supervisory mentoring
• Periods of supervised observation in the field
• Remedial training by their supervisor or Training Academy personnel (KACP 4.7e)
• The Peer Support Team (PST)
• The EIP Coordinator
• Departmental chaplains
• EAP referral (mandatory, recommended, or voluntary) (refer to SOP 2.17)
• Kentucky Post-Critical Incident Seminar (KYPCIS)
Supervising lieutenants will encourage members who are needing assistance to utilize the appropriate resource(s) for improvement. Supervisors are responsible for monitoring the member’s work performance for improvement and scheduling and/or coordinating any needed resources. The EIP Coordinator is available to assist, when needed, by the supervisor or member.
2.28.6 WELLNESS CHECK (KACP 4.7e)
The EIP Coordinator will initiate a secondary contact, referred to as a wellness check, with a member who generates an Early Intervention Performance Observation entry, and/or shows a Level 3 standard deviation for incident types which include: Chief Initiated (CI) and/or Citizen Affidavit (CA). The purpose of the wellness check is to verify the member’s well-being and provide them with an opportunity to discuss underlying issues with someone outside of their immediate chain of command. This wellness check is independent from the EIP meeting and the EIP Coordinator will not report the findings to the member’s command staff.
The EIP Coordinator will have the ability to report directly to the Deputy Chief of Police/Chief of Staff to assist in facilitating matters, which the EIP Coordinator deems urgent, for the benefit of the member’s mental health and wellness.
2.28.7 CONFIDENTIALITY (KACP 4.7d)
Except as otherwise stated in the policy, it is the duty and obligation of the member’s supervising lieutenant and immediate supervisor to maintain strict confidentiality regarding matters that are personal or health-related and may come to their attention within a review of the EIPro or during an EIP meeting. All EIP confidentiality of records and communications will be retained in accordance with Kentucky Revised Statutes (KRS) 15.409.
2.28.7 CONFIDENTIALITY (CONTINUED)
Recognizing that conversations within the EIP meeting and the wellness check are designed to focus on the training, mental health, and overall wellness of members, the PSU will not ask questions related to those meetings as a matter of routine. Circumstances that could lead to the EIP meeting or wellness check being used in PSD investigations include, but are not limited to: when the meetings form the basis of the complaint/investigation (e.g., insubordination by the officer during an EIP meeting, sexual harassment, etc.) and/or the duty to report as a law enforcement official (see below).
Supervisors are obligated to report, with the appropriate authority, matters concerning a member when:
• The member presents a danger to themselves or others, including drug abuse, excessive use of alcohol, the use of alcohol while on-duty, and/or mental or physical disability (KACP 30.8).
• There is reason to believe that the member has committed a felony and/or a misdemeanor.
• There is reason to believe that the member has committed child abuse or domestic violence (DV).
2.28.8 ANNUAL EVALUATION/RETENTION
The EIP will be reviewed annually by the EIP Coordinator. Any desired changes to the system will be forwarded, through the appropriate chain of command, to the Chief of Police.
Any records generated by the EIP will be retained pursuant to applicable records retention schedules.

sections.title: Traumatic Events
sections.text:
2.29 TRAUMATIC EVENTS
2.29.1 POLICY
The Louisville Metro Police Department (LMPD) recognizes traumatic events may cause significant distress. It is the policy of the LMPD to provide assistance to members who have experienced traumatic events and assist in relieving the distressing effects of these events. The department has numerous resources available to assist members with the distressing effects of traumatic events. This policy covers all traumatic or distressing events other than those covered by SOP 2.5 and SOP 8.12.
2.29.2 DEFINITIONS
Departmental Psychologist: A Licensed Professional Clinical Psychologist who provides professional therapeutic and supportive services to departmental members and affected family members, as needed. The departmental psychologist will assess and monitor the member’s emotional and mental status and provide treatment, as needed.
Traumatic Event: An experience that causes physical, emotional, or psychological distress/harm. It is an event that is perceived and experienced as a threat to one's safety or to the stability of the area around the person. This challenging event has the potential to create significant human distress and can overwhelm one’s usual coping mechanisms. Examples of traumatic events include, but are not limited to, the following:
• Significant events involving children (e.g., deaths, serious injuries, etc.)
• Line-of-Duty Deaths (LODDs)
• The suicide of a colleague
• Serious injury in the line-of-duty
• Homicide response
• Traffic fatalities
• Disaster or multi-casualty incidents
• Events with excessive media interest
• Known victims of crime
• Cumulative events
• Any event with a significant threat to those involved
2.29.3 SUPERVISOR RESPONSIBILITY
The member’s supervisor is often the first to recognize a member has experienced a traumatic event. Therefore, supervisors are the key to early intervention and helping members cope with the distressing effects of a traumatic event. Supervisors are encouraged to speak with members who are under their command and have potentially experienced a traumatic event to inquire about their well-being.
If a supervisor believes that a member who is under their command has experienced a traumatic event which is causing the member significant distress, the supervisor will contact the Peer Support Team (PST) Commander.
2.29.3 SUPERVISOR RESPONSIBILITY (CONTINUED)
The PST provides assistance to the member to help them cope with the distressing effects of the traumatic event. If the PST Commander believes that a traumatic event has occurred, the departmental psychologist will contact the affected member(s). A member of the PST, the member’s supervisor, and the departmental psychologist will work with the member to determine the level of assistance needed and the most appropriate resource(s) to assist the member.
Regardless of what level of assistance has been provided or the resources used, the goal is to provide mechanisms to facilitate the resistance, resilience, and recovery from traumatic events.
2.29.4 MEMBER RESOURCES
Members will be provided with the resources necessary to obtain assistance in dealing with the distressing effects of traumatic events. These resources include, but are not limited to, the following:
• The member’s supervisor.
• The Employee Assistance Program (EAP) (refer to SOP 2.17).
• The departmental psychologist.
• The departmental chaplains – Members should contact MetroSafe, who will page the on-call chaplain.
• Kentucky Post-Critical Incident Seminar (KYPCIS) (refer to SOP 2.5 and SOP 8.12).
• The PST – Members can contact PST members via the following methods:
o Rundowns – On-call rundowns for the PST will be emailed bi-monthly by the PST Commander. A list of PST officers and contact information can be found on the LMPD Intranet by clicking on the “Accountability & Improvement” link and clicking on the “Wellness” link. o MetroSafe - MetroSafe can page a PST member; or o Email - An email can be sent to “LMPD Peer Support,” located within the department’s email distribution list.

sections.title: Death or Catastrophic Injury to Member
sections.text:
2.30 DEATH OR CATASTROPHIC INJURY TO MEMBER
2.30.1 PURPOSE
The Louisville Metro Police Department (LMPD) recognizes the death of a member will have devastating effects on the member’s family as well as a significant impact upon other members of the department. When death occurs as a direct result of that member’s duties or status as a law enforcement officer or member of the department, the effects will be even more substantial and far-reaching, likely impacting family members of other members of the department and the community, at-large. With regard to line‐of‐duty deaths (LODDs) and non-LODDs, the manner in which the LMPD responds may potentially have significant long‐term effects on all concerned.
The purpose of this policy is to establish responding guidelines to the catastrophic injury or death of a member by having response protocols, support procedures, and support resources in place. This policy will focus primarily on deaths classified as occurring in the line‐of‐duty and will provide an overview of the department’s immediate response and procedures to be followed during the days leading up to the funeral. While the final determination of classification for agency purposes will be made by the Chief of Police, the parameters for classification, listed in SOP 2.30.5, will guide on‐scene personnel in making a preliminary classification and, therefore, in rendering the appropriate initial honors.
Because of benefits available to families of sworn law enforcement officers whose deaths occur in the line‐of‐duty, it is important to properly classify a death or catastrophic injury, as soon as practical. Although the department does not approve or deny external LODD benefits, it is important to inform survivors, as soon as practical, of the benefits that may be available to them. Informing a survivor of possible LODD benefits can free them from financial concerns and enable them to focus more on their family and grief. Care should be exercised when advising of these benefits so the survivors do not expect benefits for which they may not be entitled. Nothing contained herein is intended to expand, enhance, alter, or broaden the Workers’ Compensation laws and regulations of the Commonwealth of Kentucky or the Collective Bargaining Agreement (CBA) between Louisville Metro Government and the River City Fraternal Order of Police (FOP) (KACP 10.4c).
It is important to render the appropriate professional honors to individuals who have served the department and/or the law enforcement profession honorably, as well as the importance of preserving the integrity of those honors. There are important distinctions between rendering such honors in recognition of service and sacrifice, after an LODD, and rendering them for service only, after a non‐LODD.
2.30.2 POLICY
It is the policy of the LMPD to notify the immediate family and/or emergency contact of a member who has suffered a life‐threatening injury or death. Such notification is to be made with respect, empathy, and without delay. In the event of an LODD, the Public Integrity Unit (PIU) will request notification and response of the on-call deputy coroner, as soon as practical.
2.30.2 POLICY (CONTINUED)
When the death of a member occurs as a result of that member’s duties or status, it will be classified as an LODD and considered the ultimate sacrifice made in service to both the department and the citizens of Louisville Metro. The LMPD will take every reasonable and prudent measure to respond to the tragedy with respect to the deceased member and to provide support to their family. When doing so, the department will consider the effects on other members of the department and their families. Recognizing the many needs of those affected may be beyond the scope of what can be provided internally; therefore, the LMPD will identify resources and support mechanisms that may be needed in such circumstances and establish relationships and response guidelines in advance.
The non-LODD death of an active member will also have significant effects on the individual’s family and other members of the department who are co‐workers and friends. The LMPD will strive to be respectful of the needs of those affected and provide support, as needed and when available.
2.30.3 DEFINITIONS
Casket Watch: A vigil consisting of one (1) or two (2) Honor Guard personnel who guard the deceased member. The number of Honor Guard personnel who are guarding the member will vary depending upon the classification of the death.
Color Guard: A minimum of three (3) members, consisting of one (1) flag bearer and two (2) riflemen.
Firing Party: A minimum of at least three (3) riflemen who will fire three (3) volleys of blank ammunition.
Line-of-Duty Death (LODD): This classification means an employee’s death occurred as a result of, or complications from, their duty. In essence, it means that the employee died as a direct result of their duty, or complications that occurred as a direct result of their duty. . Non-LODD: Any other death of a member, other than an LODD, including death as a result of illness or an accident, not directly related to their duty. This sworn member should be in good standing, as determined by the Chief of Police.
Non-Sworn Member: Any member who is currently employed by the LMPD and holds a position that does not require Kentucky Law Enforcement Council (KLEC) Peace Officer Professional Standards (POPS) certification as a condition of their employment. Police recruits are non-sworn members.
Retired Sworn: A former employee who retired from a sworn position in the LMPD, Jefferson County Police Department (JCPD), or Louisville Division of Police (LPD) and remains in good standing, as determined by the Chief of Police.
Riderless Horse: A member of the LMPD Mounted Patrol will lead an unmounted horse in front of the deceased member during the last segment of travel to the member’s final resting place.
Special Guard: An officer who guards the deceased member until relieved by the Casket Watch.
2.30.3 DEFINITIONS (CONTINUED)
Sworn Member: An active-duty member of the LMPD who maintains KLEC POPS certification as a requirement to maintain their employment as a police officer of any rank within the LMPD. A sworn member has arrest powers. Police recruits are not sworn members of the department.
2.30.4 COMMAND STRUCTURE FOR A DEATH OR CATASTROPHIC INJURY TO MEMBER
A response to an LODD or catastrophic injury to a member will result in a massive outpouring of assistance. A temporary command structure will be utilized to coordinate response and eliminate the duplication of efforts by members who are wishing to assist. To effectively and appropriately manage all aspects of such an incident, the LMPD will use a coordinated response, as outlined below. The basic duties are divided into the initial scene control that will be handled by responding personnel/commanding officers; the criminal investigation and/or death investigation which will be handled by the PIU; and the hospital/funeral detail that will be led by the Special Operations Division (SOD) Commander. The member’s division commander’s primary responsibilities will be to support the deceased/injured member’s coworkers and to maintain division operations.
Initial Scene Commander Duties
The first officer who is on-scene is responsible for control of the scene, including security, medical care, and preservation of evidence, until relieved by a commanding officer. The commanding officer is then responsible for the scene until relieved by the PIU. The on-scene commanding officer is also responsible for notifying the division commander and the executive command staff through MetroSafe, briefing superior officers, and establishing a staging area for the media. The member’s division commander will assume all hospital command duties if the member is transported to the hospital for medical care. The duties of the Initial Scene Commander are delineated on the Initial Scene Commander Checklist, which is located at the end of this policy.
Member’s Division Commander
The member’s division commander, or their designee, has the ultimate authority of bestowing honors on the deceased member until relieved by the Funeral Detail Commander.
The first task of the member’s division commander at the hospital is to verify that access for Emergency Medical Services (EMS) vehicles and personnel is not impeded. They act as a liaison between hospital staff and the Family Liaison Officer (FLO) or the member’s family. The family will receive all pertinent information as it relates to the member before being released to any other personnel. The division commander provides updates on the member’s condition to the departmental physician, executive command staff, and departmental members. The division commander will establish a private area for the family of the deceased/seriously injured member, as well as an additional gathering area for LMPD members. It will also be the responsibility of the division commander to verify there is an officer/detective with the member at any hospital facility while receiving care any time they are on-duty and injured. The guarding officer will escort the injured member anywhere in the hospital facility.
2.30.4 COMMAND STRUCTURE FOR A DEATH OR CATASTROPHIC INJURY TO MEMBER (CONTINUED)
The affected member’s division commander will manage ongoing division operations and will obtain additional resources, as needed, during the crisis period. The member’s division commander will coordinate with the PST, departmental psychologist, departmental chaplains, Louisville Metro Government (LMG) Life Solutions representatives, and/or other contract psychological services to assist LMPD members in crisis, in recognition that members may need additional assistance during the grieving process.
The division commander works with the FLO on follow-up issues such as retrieving the deceased or seriously injured member’s property or equipment and coordination of peer support for employees who are assigned to the division.
Funeral Detail Commander Duties (Special Operations Division (SOD) Commander)
The SOD Commander will serve as the Funeral Detail Commander (FDC), unless otherwise determined by the Chief of Police. The FDC will receive special training to lead, manage, and coordinate a funeral detail for the consistent response to the death of an active member. The FDC’s responsibilities include the coordination of all liaison officers. They will communicate with all liaison officers (Funeral Coordinator, FLO, Family Support Officer (FSO), Peer Support Team (PST) Commander, and the member’s division commander) at least once daily until the member is laid to rest.
The FDC will manage the event utilizing the LMPD Funeral Detail Checklist, which is located at the end of this policy. The FDC will prepare an After-Action Report (LMPD #08-0005) for review by the Chief of Police, as soon as practical, after the member is laid to rest.
Funeral Coordinator (Honor Guard Commander)
The Funeral Coordinator works with the family, funeral home, and FLO to respect the wishes of the family and to coordinate appropriate honors for the deceased member. The duties of the Funeral Coordinator are delineated on the Funeral Coordinator Checklist, which is located at the end of this policy.
Peer Support Team (PST)
The PST Commander will provide assistance throughout the incident and the funeral. Specifically, the PST Commander will provide guidance and assistance to the FLO(s) and support to the member’s division at the request of the division commander.
The PST squad that is on-call at the time of the event will be placed on special duty time for the visitation and funeral in order to provide assistance to members of the department who attend these events.
The PST will continue to provide assistance to surviving officers who are involved in the incident, as outlined by SOP 8.12 (Critical Incidents).
2.30.4 COMMAND STRUCTURE FOR A DEATH OR CATASTROPHIC INJURY TO MEMBER (CONTINUED)
Departmental Psychologist
The departmental psychologist will provide assistance throughout the incident and at the funeral. Specifically, the departmental psychologist provides guidance and assistance to the PST Commander and support to the member’s division at the request of the division commander.
Family Support Officer (FSO)
Following an LODD or non-LODD of a member, at least one (1) FSO will be assigned to the immediate family. Members have the option of identifying a FSO in advance by using the LMPD Employee Emergency Contact Information Form (LMPD #14-0007). The member’s division commander will attempt to utilize the pre-designated member as the FSO, if that member is available, willing, and able to perform the assignment. The most important consideration when selecting the FSO is the comfort of the family. For the purposes of the FSO, they are relieved of chain of command responsibilities as to be able to directly contact the appropriate personnel to fulfill the wishes of the family.
If the family requests a specific individual, every effort should be made to honor that request. They should be emotionally able to fulfill this duty. The FSO serves as a communication conduit between the family and the FLO. The FSO should refer all questions regarding departmental procedures, honors, arrangements, and benefits to the FLO. The FSO will be placed on special duty time until the member is laid to rest or as directed by competent authority.
Family Liaison Officer (FLO)
Following an LODD or non-LODD of a member, at least one (1) FLO will be appointed by the PST Commander. FLO(s) will be members of the PST and receive specific training for this duty, as soon as practical. The FLO(s) will serve as a communications conduit between the FSO, the Funeral Coordinator, the Funeral Detail Commander, the member’s division commander, and the Benefits Liaison Coordinator (BLC). FLO(s) will assist the family, as needed, within the bounds set by competent authority. The FLO should refer all questions regarding honors and arrangements to the Funeral Coordinator and any questions regarding benefits to the BLC.
FLO(s) are assigned until the member is laid to rest or as directed by competent authority. A member who is assigned as an FLO will be placed on special duty time for the duration of this assignment. The duties of the FLO are delineated on the Family Liaison Officer Checklist, which is located at the end of this policy.
Benefits Liaison Coordinator (BLC) (Police Human Resources Director)
The Police Human Resources (HR) Director will serve as the BLC. The BLC is responsible for handling benefits- related issues of the injured or deceased member. The BLC will report the status of their actions to the Assistant Chief of Police/Administrative Bureau.
2.30.4 COMMAND STRUCTURE FOR A DEATH OR CATASTROPHIC INJURY TO MEMBER (CONTINUED)
The BLC may be contacted directly by the FLO and/or family representatives with questions or requests for information regarding the application for benefits related to the death of, or serious injury to, a member. The BLC will prepare benefit information for the family of a seriously injured or deceased member. The BLC will contact the appropriate agencies that provide disability/death benefits.
The following personnel will attend the meeting, unless otherwise dictated by the family:
• FDC (Special Operations Division Commander)
• FLO (PST member)
• BLC (Police HR Director)
• FSO
The benefits for which those that are covered and those that are not (e.g., funeral services, burial services, plots, headstone, etc.) will be clearly defined for the family.
It is the responsibility of the BLC and the FLO to inform the member’s family of outside organizations and support services that provide benefits to them in response to the death of an active sworn member. It is the responsibility of the FLO to coordinate communication between the FSO and the outside organizations and support service groups.
The BLC is responsible for administering the 36-month health insurance coverage for the families of LODD sworn members. Dependents will have the ability to change coverage levels during open enrollment periods.
During this meeting, the member’s family will be advised of the appropriate honors established by this policy as they relate to the circumstances surrounding the member’s death. Furthermore, the member’s family will be advised of the member’s LMPD Employee Emergency Contact Information Form and/or Living Will as they relate to the member’s wishes. Most importantly, the FLO will request any additional wishes the family may have, and every attempt will be made to comply with their wishes so long as those wishes are within the honors established by this policy.
2.30.5 NOTIFICATIONS
Unless all suitable alternatives have been exhausted or significant extenuating circumstances exist, the notification of death or a catastrophic injury to a member will not be made, via telephone or any method, other than in-person. Equal respect and consideration will be given to all immediate family members, including a spouse or significant other, parents, siblings, and adult children. The spouse is to be given priority. However, if special circumstances dictate, the notification of other immediate family members should not be delayed.
Because of the impact of social media and other modern communication channels and technologies, it is imperative that the department make every effort to deliver proper respectful notification before the family members receive word via other impersonal and uninformed channels (e.g., news media).
2.30.5 NOTIFICATIONS (CONTINUED)
The principle guiding factor should be a quick and sensitive notification; therefore, the notification should not be delayed while waiting for the Chief of Police, or their designee, to become available.
Once it is determined that a member of the LMPD has died or sustained a catastrophic injury, MetroSafe will be instructed to make notifications as indicated in SOP 2.7. The notification is to include the member’s identity, if known, and basic information about what has occurred. This information will not be communicated in a manner accessible by the public. Once the identity of the affected member is known, the notification procedures, found below, will be initiated. In the event of an LODD, the PIU will request notification and response of the on-call deputy coroner, as soon as practical.
Notification of Death
In the event that a notification needs to be made regarding the death of a member, whenever practical, the nearest available commanding officer, regardless of division, will be directed by the Initial Scene Commander to maintain visual contact of the affected member’s family, as soon as possible. It is recommended that the commanding officer take another sworn member with them to assist. The commanding officer should not initiate contact, take action, or park in a position likely to alert the family, unless they observe someone leaving the home who appears to be a family member. In that event, they should initiate contact and ask the individual to remain.
Recognizing that their presence in that circumstance may cause alarm, it may become necessary for the commanding officer to make a notification before the notification team arrives. The commanding officer should be prepared to do so, but only if they deem it absolutely necessary. Notification of the immediate survivor is to be made by the highest‐ranking member of the department who can do so, without delay. Ideally, this notification will be made by the Chief of Police.
The Chief of Police, or their designee, will select one (1) or two (2) of the most appropriate individuals who are available and make the notification, as soon as possible. If available, at least one (1) member of the notification team should be in uniform. The notification officer should be accompanied by the affected member’s division commander, or their designee, and a support person, such as a PST member, departmental chaplain, or other person with relevant training or experience. A close friend, family member, or departmental member who is familiar to the family may also be considered. The notification should be made by at least two (2) individuals, but generally not more than three (3) individuals.
Additional notification teams are to be assembled and sent to personally notify other immediate survivors, including parents, siblings, and adult children. Notification teams are to remain with family members as long as necessary to assist, as needed. If multiple teams are deployed, the Chief of Police, or their designee, should make an effort to personally visit and extend condolences to each immediate family member.
All members of the notification teams are to drive separate vehicles, whenever practical. Team members should communicate prior to their arrival and establish a notification plan, clearly identifying who will take the lead and what will be said. If necessary, EMS or other resources are to be placed on standby near the location.
2.30.5 NOTIFICATIONS (CONTINUED)
When it is necessary to make a death notification outside of a reasonable driving distance of Louisville Metro, the commanding officer will contact the law enforcement agency from the appropriate jurisdiction. If necessary, such contact may be initiated through MetroSafe. Arrangements will be made for that agency to make the notification as close to these guidelines as possible, conducted by a staff‐level officer of that agency along with a chaplain or other support person, without delay. Whenever possible, the commanding officer should speak directly to the officer who will make the notification before the notification is made. The notifying officer will be properly briefed and appropriate actions will be agreed upon.
Once LODD procedures are in place and further information or a review causes a re-classification to a non-LODD, special care will be given when transitioning from LODD protocols to non-LODD protocols. Transition plans must include provisions for the respectful notification of family members prior to such changes and be approved by the Chief of Police, or their designee, before notification or implementation.
Notification of Catastrophic Injury
In the event of a catastrophic injury and it is believed that the member is still alive, the process of notification will include transportation of immediate family members, without delay, to the hospital where the member is being treated. Under no circumstances will a member of the department misrepresent the injured member’s status, condition, or prognosis. If a member is known to be deceased, family members will not be transported under false pretenses.
Unless otherwise directed by a superior officer, it will be the responsibility of the Initial Scene Commander to initiate notification. If the injury occurs outside of Louisville Metro, it will be the responsibility of the on‐duty commanding officer of the division/section/unit to which the member is assigned.
If necessary, the commanding officer may delegate the responsibility for the notification. It is recommended that the responsibility be passed to the on‐duty commanding officer of the division in which the notification is to be made or closest to the area, if it is to be made outside of Louisville Metro.
The Initial Scene Commander, or their designee, will identify and send the closest available and appropriate unit(s) to notify and transport family members. When determining who to send, consideration should be given to the personality, demeanor, training, and experience of any member who is chosen to make the notification. A commanding officer should be sent, if available, and if the assignment of this commanding officer would not cause a delay in notification. If it is known that young children, or others who are requiring special care, are present in the home, a second unit will be sent to remain at the home until alternative care can be established.
2.30.6 SENSITIVITY
Whenever possible, a death notification should be made in private. If the notification occurs at a residence, the notification team should ask to go inside. If others are present, particularly children or multiple adults, the team should request privacy. The purpose is to show respect and preserve the dignity of the survivors by affording them the opportunity to react to the tragic news away from guests and others.
2.30.6 SENSITIVITY (CONTINUED)
It is also desirable to give loved ones the opportunity to process the information and make important decisions regarding when and how to tell the children. The notification should be made using plain language, with clear terms such as “killed” or “dead,” not ambiguous terms such as “expired,” “passed on,” or “no longer with us.” Clarity should be provided in the first few sentences spoken by using the words “dead” or “died.”
The deceased member should always be referred to respectfully by their name and never with terms such as “the deceased,” “body,” or “remains.”
The leader of the notification team should provide the family with as much factual information as possible regarding the incident and death in order to avoid speculation.
Members should avoid making any promises to the family until arrangements can be discussed with competent authority. Any promises made must be kept.
Notification personnel are not to bring any personal items of the deceased member to give to the family. The proper disposition of personal property is to occur at a later date and in a more dignified manner.
2.30.7 TRANSPORTING FAMILY MEMBERS
While transporting family members, personnel should turn off all radios and refrain from engaging in phone or other communication that is not essential to the transport. Transporting officer(s) should provide basic known facts about the incident, if asked, but not speculate or repeat rumors. Family members are to be transported safely and directly to the appropriate destination. No deviation or additional stops are to be made, unless specifically requested by the family member.
Prior to departure or while en route to the hospital, the transporting officer will make contact with the member’s division commander to advise they are en route and provide an estimated time of arrival. This will assist the division commander in making sure they have obtained updates to provide the family and have reserved a place as a designated area for the family to have privacy.
It should be anticipated that family members will not be able to drive themselves. Arrangements for transportation should be established for them, before the notification unit arrives. If family members insist otherwise and refuse to accept the provided transportation, the notifying officer should, at the very least, ask to accompany them in their vehicle or follow them in a departmental vehicle.
2.30.8 FAMILY AT THE SCENE OF AN INCIDENT
When a member has been killed and not immediately removed from the scene of an incident, the arrival of family members should be anticipated. When the family has learned of the incident before the notification team arrives or upon formal notification, the family may insist upon being taken to the scene. Grieving family members will be handled respectfully and compassionately, while maintaining the safety for all and preserving the integrity of the scene.
2.30.8 FAMILY AT THE SCENE OF AN INCIDENT (CONTINUED)
When feasible, the Incident Commander (IC) will prepare for the possible arrival of the family. Traffic and perimeter personnel will be alerted to the possible arrival and instructed accordingly. While it might not be safe or appropriate for the family to come close to the actual scene, a location will be designated for them away from the news media and onlookers. If the identity of the deceased member has not already been confirmed to the family, the IC, or highest-ranking officer available, should do so as soon as possible.
2.30.9 VISITING/VIEWING THE DECEASED
In order to be able to hold guilty persons responsible for criminal acts, the integrity of the evidence, and the proper collection thereof, are of the utmost importance. Family members should be briefed that everything possible will be done to conduct all necessary tests as quickly as possible, but investigative thoroughness and evidence collection will not be compromised for expediency. Family members should be counseled that the Medical Examiner’s Office treats all decedents with compassion and dignity and members of the department will stand watch over the decedent, at all times.
Family members will be offered the opportunity to visit the deceased member at the funeral home after the deceased has been released from the Medical Examiner’s Office. Seeing, touching, and spending time with the deceased member may be a critically important part of the grieving and healing process, but should be undertaken in a setting that can provide the appropriate environment and comfort (e.g., funeral home) and after all necessary evidence has been documented and collected.
If a deceased member is badly disfigured, family members should be respectfully discouraged from viewing. However, if a family member insists, a private viewing will be arranged at the funeral home. Family members should be cautioned and prepared for what they will see. Unless refused by the family member, a support person, such as a chaplain, other clergy, counselor, or close friend, should accompany them.
In all such situations, the expressed wishes of the family will be considered while verifying that evidence is not lost or compromised. The IC, or their designee, will coordinate with the coroner and/or funeral home leadership to assist with the access requested by the family.
2.30.10 DEPARTMENTAL NOTIFICATIONS AND BRIEFING
As soon as practical following the LODD of a member, a department‐wide notification will be made by the Chief of Police, or their designee, via email, radio, and/or other methods. A subsequent briefing may be held for members of the department (without a media presence) with update sessions, as necessary. At the discretion of the Chief of Police, or their designee, family members of LMPD personnel may be included.
The Deputy Chief of Police/Chief of Staff will verify that a funeral logistics memorandum is disseminated with logistical information, the uniform of the day, and other pertinent information regarding funeral arrangements.
2.30.11 RELEASE OF INFORMATION
The release of the identity of a deceased member, or information likely to identify the deceased member, is strictly prohibited until authorized and agreed upon by the coroner and the Chief of Police, or their designee.
The identity of the deceased member will only be released after all immediate family members have been properly notified. Members are prohibited from making radio transmissions, unless absolutely necessary, or any public statement or posting via Facebook, X (formerly known as Twitter), or other social media or public forum that would identify the deceased member prior to the official release (KACP 20.5a). Members will not directly contact, in any manner, the family of the deceased member, unless as directed in this policy, prior to the formal notification by the coroner in coordination with the Chief of Police, or their designee.
However, members are encouraged to contact their own family members, as soon as practical, following such an incident, in order to let them know that they are okay. Members will not give information about, or even hint at, the identity of the deceased member prior to the formal release by the Chief of Police, or their designee.
2.30.12 HOME SECURITY DETAIL (SWORN LODD OR SPECIAL CIRCUMSTANCES ONLY)
As soon as possible following the notification of an LODD of a sworn member and the formal notification of the family, a 24-hour security detail will be established at the immediate family members’ residence. The primary purpose, especially in the event of a felonious death, is to afford a sense of security for the family. In addition, it may prevent the news media, and others, from entering the personal space of the family without invitation. The detailed officer will remain outside, unless invited inside by the family for short periods of time. A home security detail may be extended to non‐sworn personnel or non‐LODD circumstances by the approval of the Chief of Police, or their designee. The detail will be maintained around the clock until at least 24 hours following the funeral, unless directed by the Chief of Police, or their designee.
2.30.13 PERSONAL EFFECTS
Unless investigative, evidentiary, or other needs dictate, the personal effects of a deceased member will be left in place in their workspace (e.g., desk, locker, assigned vehicle, etc.) until the family determines what they want to do with them. Compassion will be exercised. Family members will be given ample opportunity to personally retrieve such items from the workspace and/or assigned vehicle just as they were left by the deceased member. However, items of value will be secured by the member’s division commander. Supervisors will survey the workspace and secure any sensitive materials (e.g., investigative notes, case files, etc.) or weapons. Otherwise, the space should be left as undisturbed as possible.
2.30.14 OTHER NOTIFICATIONS
Within 24 hours of the determination that the death of a member will be treated as an LODD, the following will be notified by the BLC:
• Public Safety Officers’ Benefits Office (federal and state)
2.30.14 OTHER NOTIFICATIONS (CONTINUED)
• Louisville Metro Police Foundation
• Supporting Heroes
• Concerns of Police Survivors (C.O.P.S.)
• Kentucky Law Enforcement Officer’s Memorial Foundation
• National Law Enforcement Officer’s Memorial Fund and Officer Down Memorial Page
• Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI) Field Office
• Louisville Metro Health and Safety Office, in writing
Within 30 days of the LODD, the BLC will begin processing applications for federal, state, local, and other benefits.
Within 30 days of the LODD, the Special Investigations Division (SID) Commander will begin processing applications to include the deceased officer’s name on federal, state, and local monuments honoring officers who are killed in the line-of-duty.
2.30.15 REPORTING ON-DUTY INJURIES
Supervisors will report all work-related incidents involving the death of any member, including death resulting from a heart attack, either verbally at (502) 574-3305, (502) 574-1287, or (502) 574-3047, or in-person to the Louisville Metro Health and Safety Office, located in Metro Hall at 527 West Jefferson Street, 6th floor, Louisville, KY 40202, within eight (8) hours of the time from which the supervisor first became aware of the incident. If the supervisor needs to contact the Louisville Metro Health and Safety Office outside of normal operating hours (0800 to 1700 hours, Monday through Friday), they may call the Louisville Metro Health and Safety Administrator at (502) 528-
6376. If the supervisor who is making the report is unable to get in contact with someone in the Louisville Metro Health and Safety Office, the member must verbally report the incident to the Kentucky Occupational Safety and Health Administration (OSHA) Office, Division of Compliance, at (502) 564-3535. If the incident occurs outside of the normal operating hours of the Kentucky OSHA Office (0800 to 1630 hours, Monday through Friday), the supervisor will call the Federal OSHA Office at (800) 321-OSHA (6742). All work-related incidents involving a non- fatal heart attack, amputation, loss of an eye, or the in-patient hospitalization of a member from a single incident must be reported verbally at (502) 574-3305, (502) 574-1287, or (502) 574-3047, or in-person to the Louisville Metro Health and Safety Office, within 24 hours of the time from which the supervisor first became aware of the incident. If the supervisor needs to contact the Louisville Metro Health and Safety Office outside of normal operating hours (0800 to 1700 hours, Monday through Friday), they may call the Louisville Metro Health and Safety Administrator at (502) 528-6376. If the supervisor who is making the report is unable to get in contact with someone in the Louisville Metro Health and Safety Office during this timeframe, the supervisor will verbally report the work-related incident to the Kentucky OSHA Office, Division of Compliance, at (502) 564-3535.
2.30.16 HONORS
It is the policy of the LMPD to appropriately recognize and honor members who have given their lives in the line‐ of‐duty. Keeping with the traditions of law enforcement, the LMPD will only render ultimate honors for the ultimate sacrifice (e.g., LODD as defined above). Current and former members will receive professional honors as
2.30.16 HONORS (CONTINUED)
recognition for their service. Members whose deaths occur as a result of service (LODD) will receive additional honors in recognition of both service and sacrifice.
The listed honors are those typically rendered during funeral services by the LMPD Honor Guard and those of other agencies. At the request of family members, and by the approval of the Chief of Police, or their designee, all or part of the services offered for any particular funeral type may be performed; however, the honors performed must be in keeping with the parameters of the category fitting the manner of death. For members whose deaths appear likely to be classified as an LODD, additional special honors are to be rendered immediately and maintained until the member is laid to rest.
It is the policy of the LMPD to preserve the integrity of these honors and to render them for those members whose deaths are classified as an LODD. Additionally, members of the LMPD are prohibited from assisting in the rendering of LODD honors to members of other agencies whose deaths are not classified as an LODD.
Special Guard (LODD/Active Sworn Member)
The Special Guard is utilized to show respect by having members of the department watch over the deceased member every minute of every day until they are laid to rest. It is also intended to provide comfort to the family by knowing that their loved one will not be alone and as a statement to the community, and others. Personnel who are utilized in this manner will conduct themselves in a very respectful and reverent manner, at all times, while maintaining their post and not engaging in other activities.
Upon the determination that the circumstances of the death may be classified as an LODD, a uniformed member will be immediately assigned to watch over the deceased member. It is preferred that uniformed members be in Class A uniform with a tie unless that is not immediately practical. Even if the decedent is not at the hospital (e.g., still at a crime scene, wreckage, or other situation from which they have not yet been removed), the assigned Special Guard will be standing watch and/or ready to assume watch, as soon as it is safe and practical.
The uniformed member will stay with the deceased member until a member of the Honor Guard arrives on-scene to assume the watch. The Honor Guard will maintain the watch for the first 24 hours. At that time, the Special Guard will be taken over by sworn personnel from within the member’s division. The Honor Guard Commander, with the assistance of the division commander from the deceased member’s unit, will be assigned to supervise and schedule the Special Guard for around-the-clock coverage until the member is laid to rest.
The Special Guard is not the same as the formal Casket Watch, which is performed by the LMPD Honor Guard.
The Special Guard will be comprised of sworn personnel in uniform. Shifts will be set according to need, ideally two (2) to four (4) hours in length. Volunteering coworkers, academy classmates, etc. are to be given priority in scheduling. The Special Guard may be doubled if there is an overwhelming number of volunteers. The role of the Special Guard will be assumed by the LMPD Honor Guard during periods of the visitation and funeral (e.g., Casket Watch), as well as during any transport of the deceased member and during any autopsy or preparation.
To respect the dignity of the member, the Special Guard will be posted outside of the room where the member is located during an autopsy, cleaning, dressing, or other preparation. The Special Guard will show similar respect
2.30.16 HONORS (CONTINUED)
and be posted outside during the private family visitation, unless otherwise requested. At all other times, the Special Guard will remain with the deceased member.
Removal from the Scene with Honors (LODD/Active Sworn Member)
When a sworn member has been declared deceased at a location other than a medical facility, such as a crime or crash scene, the removal will be conducted with honor, while maintaining scene integrity and considering safety concerns. If possible, public safety personnel should be assembled in a formation and the Honor Guard will coordinate a cordon or gauntlet of sworn personnel through which the member will pass. Assembled public safety personnel will be called to “Attention” and commanded to render the appropriate hand salute as the member is moved.
Special Escorts (LODD/Active Sworn Member)
When a sworn member whose death is considered an LODD is to be moved from one (1) location to another, the move will be conducted formally with an escort. The LMPD Honor Guard, when possible, will serve as pallbearers, unless the family requests otherwise. The Traffic Unit will implement a traffic control plan. Moves will be conducted in a respectful and reverent manner, traveling at funeral procession speeds. Sirens should be utilized only when necessary for traffic control and safety. The use of emergency lights will be contingent upon traffic control and conditions and is determined on a case-by-case basis.
Except when safety or other necessity dictates, traffic control personnel will come to the position of “Attention” and render a hand salute as the hearse approaches and passes. The fallen member will be saluted, not the motorcade.
Whenever the approximate time of a move is known in advance (e.g., from the Medical Examiner’s Office to a funeral home or from a funeral home to a church), the details will be shared with the media through the Media and Public Relations Office, with as much advance notice as possible. This will allow members of the community the opportunity to stage along the route in order to show respect and appreciation for the member’s service and sacrifice. Family members will also be notified in advance of each move and, if appropriate, given the opportunity to participate.
LODD Funeral Honors
Formal LODD honors will be offered to the family of any deceased member whose death is classified as an LODD. Such honors will be rendered during the funeral visitation and services.
A family may refuse honors or reject individual components as they choose.
LMPD SWORN MEMBER HONORS
Active LMPD Sworn Member LODD – Sworn Level 1 Memorial Service
2.30.16 HONORS (CONTINUED)
The following honors may be performed for an active LMPD Sworn Member LODD (Sworn Level 1) Memorial Service:
• Special Guard: An officer will watch over the deceased member until they are relieved by the Casket Watch.
• Casket Watch: Members of the LMPD Honor Guard (or assisting agencies) will stand guard at the casket during periods of visitation and prior to the start of the funeral service. One (1) member will be posted at the head of the casket and one (1) at the foot. The LMPD Honor Guard will be the sole unit that is responsible for accompanying and/or moving the member at each stage of movement.
• Firing Party: A minimum of three (3) riflemen will fire three (3) volleys of blank ammunition.
• Riderless Horse: A member of the LMPD Mounted Patrol will lead an unmounted horse in front of the hearse during the last segment of travel to the member’s final resting place.
• Air Unit Flyover: A flyover tribute may be conducted by the LMPD Air Unit during the graveside service, depending on weather and safety considerations.
• Final Call: A final radio call will be conducted for the fallen member during the graveside service, which is located in Appendix 1 at the end of this policy.
• Garrison Flag: With the assistance of the fire department, a Garrison Flag(s) (large U.S. flag) will be hung over the roadway for the motorcade to pass under while en route to the cemetery (Exception: A Garrison Flag may also be utilized in a non‐LODD service, but the motorcade will not pass underneath).
• Color Guard: A minimum of three (3) members, consisting of one (1) flag-bearer and two (2) riflemen.
• Bugler: An Honor Guard bugler will play Taps.
• Flag Folding Detail: Members of the LMPD Honor Guard will conduct this detail with an eight (8)-member folding unit. This detail may be conducted at either the FOP service or memorial service, or both. The Chief of Police, or their designee, will present the flag to the family.
• Gauntlet: Honor Guards from all participating agencies will form a gauntlet for the deceased member while moving them during the memorial service.
Active LMPD Sworn Member Non-LODD Death – Sworn Level 2 Memorial Service
The following honors may be performed for an active LMPD Sworn Member Non-LODD Death (Sworn Level 2) Memorial Service: Active sworn members who become deceased as a result of illness, accident, injury, or natural causes not related to any performance of duty or police action.
• Special Guard: An officer will watch over the deceased member until they are relieved by the Casket Watch.
• Casket Watch: Members of the LMPD Honor Guard will stand guard at the casket during periods of visitation and prior to the start of the funeral service. One (1) member will be posted at the head of the casket.
• Color Guard: A minimum of three (3) members, consisting of one (1) flag-bearer and two (2) riflemen.
• Firing Party: A minimum of three (3) riflemen will fire three (3) volleys of blank ammunition.
• Radio Remembrance and Silence: An observed moment of silence will be conducted over LMPD radio channels for the fallen member during the graveside service.
• Bugler: An Honor Guard bugler will play Taps.
2.30.16 HONORS (CONTINUED)
• Flag Folding Detail: Members of the LMPD Honor Guard will conduct this detail with a two (2)-member folding unit. This detail may be conducted at either the FOP service or memorial service, or both. The Chief of Police, or their designee, will present the flag to the family.
• Mounted Patrol Unit: Members of the LMPD Mounted Patrol will provide a uniformed presence and/or mounted escort at the memorial or graveside service.
Retired Sworn Member Death – Sworn Level 3 Memorial Service
The following honors may be performed for a Retired Sworn Member Death (Sworn Level 3) Memorial Service: Retired sworn members of the LMPD, JCPD, or LPD who are not currently under indictment or been convicted of a felony offense. The memorial service for retired members will only be performed locally, or within a reasonable distance of travel, as determined by the Chief of Police.
• Firing Party: A minimum of three (3) riflemen will fire three (3) volleys of blank ammunition.
• Bugler: An Honor Guard bugler will play Taps.
• Flag Folding Detail: Members of the LMPD Honor Guard will conduct this detail with a two (2)-member folding unit. This detail may be conducted at either the FOP service or memorial service, or both. The Chief of Police, or their designee, will present the flag to the family.
LMPD NON-SWORN MEMBER HONORS
Active LMPD Non-Sworn Member LODD – Non-Sworn Level 1 Memorial Service
The following honors may be performed for an active LMPD Non-Sworn Member LODD (Non-Sworn Level 1) Memorial Service:
• Casket Watch: Members of the LMPD Honor Guard (or assisting agencies) will stand guard at the casket during periods of visitation and prior to the start of the funeral service. One (1) member will be posted at the head of the casket. The LMPD Honor Guard will be the sole unit that is responsible for accompanying and/or moving the member at each stage of movement.
• Firing Party: A minimum of three (3) riflemen will fire three (3) volleys of blank ammunition.
• Bugler: An Honor Guard bugler will play Taps.
• Flag Folding Detail: Members of the LMPD Honor Guard will conduct this detail with a two (2)-member folding unit. This detail will be conducted at the memorial service with a Louisville Metro Government flag. The Chief of Police, or their designee, will present the flag to the family.
• Gauntlet: Honor Guards from all participating agencies will form a gauntlet for the deceased member while moving them during the memorial service.
Active LMPD Non-Sworn Member Non-LODD Death – Non-Sworn Level 2 Memorial Service
The following honors may be performed for an active LMPD Non-Sworn Member Non-LODD Death (Non-Sworn Level 2) Memorial Service: Active non-sworn members of the LMPD who become deceased as a result of illness, accident, injury, or natural causes not related to any performance of their official duties.
2.30.16 HONORS (CONTINUED)
• At least two (2) Honor Guard members will be present at the funeral service to render honors decided by the detail commander.
LMPD SERVICE ANIMAL HONORS
Active LMPD Service Animal LODD – Service Animal Level 1 Memorial Service
The following honors may be performed for an active sworn service animal (canine, Mounted Patrol horse) whose death occurred as a direct result of or complications from their duties. The services performed at the memorial service will be at the discretion of the sworn handler who was responsible for the sworn service animal at the time of death.
• Firing Party: A minimum of three (3) riflemen will fire three (3) volleys of blank ammunition.
• Color Guard: A minimum of three (3) members, consisting of one (1) flag-bearer and two (2) riflemen.
• Bugler: An Honor Guard bugler will play Taps.
• Flag Folding Detail: Members of the LMPD Honor Guard will conduct this detail with a two (2)-member folding unit. This detail will be conducted at the memorial or graveside service with a Louisville Metro Government flag. The Chief of Police, or their designee, will present the flag to the handler/Mounted Patrol officer.
• Gauntlet: LMPD Honor Guard members, and any other members who are present, will form a gauntlet for the deceased member while moving them during the memorial service.
• Canine Unit: Members of the LMPD Canine Unit will provide a uniformed presence and/or escort at the memorial or graveside service.
• Mounted Patrol Unit: Members of the LMPD Mounted Patrol will provide a uniformed presence and/or mounted escort at the memorial or graveside service.
2.30.17 MOURNING BANDS
Solid black, thin blue-line, or custom mourning bands approved by the Chief of Police may be worn across a member’s badge in the following circumstances:
• Upon the order of the Chief of Police, or their designee, following the LODD of a member of the department. Once ordered, mourning bands will be removed at the end of the day that the officer is laid to rest.
• Upon the approval of the Chief of Police, or their designee, following the LODD of a law enforcement officer of a neighboring jurisdiction. The mourning band will be removed at the end of the day that the officer is laid to rest.
• On National Peace Officer’s Memorial Day (May 15).
• While attending any memorial service that is held in honor of law enforcement officers who have died in the line-of-duty.
• At the direction of the Chief of Police, or their designee.
2.30.17 MOURNING BANDS (CONTINUED)
The Administrative Services Division’s Management Assistant is responsible for maintaining a supply of mourning bands.
2.30.18 MEMORIAL FUNDS
Members are prohibited from independently establishing funds to raise money in honor of a fallen member or for the benefit of a fallen member’s family.
Members may assist an immediate survivor in setting up such a fund, but only if the survivor is given full control of the fund.
2.30.19 CONTINUED FOLLOW-UP WITH THE FAMILY
In addition to concerns for the spouse of the member, the LMPD should be sensitive to the needs of the other loved ones as well. This includes adult-aged or younger children, parents, siblings, etc. Too often, surviving family members say that they feel abandoned by the department following the funeral. Continued support and follow-up can, and should, be given. Listed below are some of the follow-up options available; however, this is not meant to be an exhaustive list:
• The departmental psychologist or PST members should meet with the family for a short debriefing session a few days after the funeral.
• When plaques or memorabilia are given to the surviving spouse, consider making something available to the surviving parents.
• Invite the surviving family to agency activities.
• Remember children from a former marriage. They should also be provided, when possible, personal memorabilia of their parent.
• Division commanders should reach out to the family through monthly phone calls during the first year.
• The Honor Guard will observe the anniversary date of the member’s death with a short ceremony.
2.30.20 ULTIMATE HONORS COMMITTEE
The Ultimate Honors Committee is a part-time committee that is comprised of members from a broad range of different units within the department. It is the committee’s responsibility to meet twice a year and after any LODD, or as deemed necessary by the SOD Commander. During this meeting, the committee will discuss the effectiveness of this policy and determine if there is a need for any changes within this policy.
2.30.21 REPRESENTATION AT SURROUNDING AREA LODDS
When there is an LODD in the Commonwealth of Kentucky or in a surrounding area, the Chief of Police, or their designee, will decide whether the department will be represented. That representation will be in keeping with the
2.30.21 REPRESENTATION AT SURROUNDING AREA LODDS (CONTINUED)
current CBA between Louisville Metro Government and the River City FOP Lodge #614. In all instances of representation, the Chief of Police, or their designee, will appoint one (1) of the representatives as the person who is in charge.
The Ultimate Honors Committee’s assistance may also be requested through the Chief of Police to assist with another agency’s LODD service planning in the Commonwealth of Kentucky, or in a surrounding area.
2.30.22 LMPD FACILITY AMERICAN FLAGS
Upon the order of the Chief of Police, or their designee, following the occurrence of an LODD of a member of the department, all departmental facility American flags are to be flown at half-staff until the end of the day that the member is laid to rest.

sections.title: Social Media
sections.text:
2.31 SOCIAL MEDIA
2.31.1 POLICY
It is the policy of the Louisville Metro Police Department (LMPD) to maintain departmental social media accounts (e.g., Facebook, X (formerly known as Twitter), Instagram, YouTube, Nextdoor, etc.) for the purposes of citizen engagement and victim/witness contact. The LMPD restricts the use of departmental resources for accessing social media sites to official business purposes only.
