4.10.14 MEDALS AND BREAST BARS
All service recognition medals and breast bars previously awarded to members of the Louisville Division of Police (LPD) and the Jefferson County Police Department (JCPD) are approved for wear. These decorations may only be worn with the Class A uniform.
Medals and breast bars may be worn ¼ inch above, parallel, and centered on the nameplate. If more than one (1) decoration is worn, they should be worn side-by-side, parallel, and centered on the nameplate with the highest decoration worn to the extreme right.
If both medals and breast bars are worn at the same time, the medals will be worn ⅜ inch above, and parallel to, the breast bars. All should be centered on the nameplate.
4.10.15 SERVICE MEDAL PIN
The service medal pin may be worn on the right uniform pocket flap, with the top edge of the pin ½ inch under, and parallel with, the center of the nameplate.
4.10.16 INSTRUCTOR PINS
Instructor pins may be worn on the left uniform pocket flap, parallel to the top edge of the pocket, and centered between the left and right edges. If more than one (1) instructor pin is worn, they should be placed side-by-side.
4.10.17 SPECIALIZED UNIT INSIGNIA
Specialized unit insignias may be worn on the left uniform pocket flap, parallel to the top edge of the pocket, and centered between the left and right edges. If more than one (1) insignia is worn, they should be placed side-by- side.
4.10.18 MARKSMANSHIP MEDAL
Marksmanship medals may be worn centered over the left uniform pocket flap, directly beneath the badge.
4.10.19 AMERICAN FLAG PIN
An American flag pin may be worn on the left uniform pocket flap, centered between the bottom and top edges. The flag should measure no more than ½ inch by ½ inch.
4.10.20 SUPPORTING HEROES PIN
The Supporting Heroes pin may be worn on the right uniform pocket flap, with the top edge of the pin ½ inch under, and parallel with, the center of the nameplate. If worn with the service medal pin, they should be placed side-by-side.
4.10.21 KENTUCKY ASSOCIATION OF CHIEFS OF POLICE (KACP) ACCREDITATION PIN
The KACP Accreditation pin may be worn on the right uniform pocket flap, with the top edge of the pin ½ inch under, and parallel with, the center of the nameplate. If worn with the service medal pin, they should be placed side-by-side.
4.10.22 CONCERNS OF POLICE SURVIVORS (C.O.P.S.) PIN
The C.O.P.S. pin may be worn on the right uniform pocket flap, with the top edge of the pin ½ inch under, and parallel with, the center of the nameplate. If worn with the service medal pin, they should be placed side-by-side.
4.10.23 LOUISVILLE METRO POLICE OFFICERS ASSOCIATION (LMPOA) PIN
The LMPOA pin may be worn on the right uniform pocket flap, with the top edge of the pin ½ inch under, and parallel with, the center of the nameplate. If worn with the service medal pin, they should be placed side-by-side.

sections.title: Protective Vest
sections.text:
4.11 PROTECTIVE VEST
4.11.1 POLICY
For the purposes of SOP 4.11, a “protective vest” is comprised of ballistic panels that are appropriately fitted to each officer. These panels may be worn concealed under the officer’s clothing in a concealment carrier or in an outer carrier that is worn on the outside of the officer’s clothing. The inner carrier and outer carrier are fitted specifically to the officer’s ballistic panels.
Sworn members with the rank of officer, sergeant, and lieutenant must wear their departmentally-issued or approved protective vest, at all times, while on-duty and when engaged in patrol activities/duties outside of a secure building of the Louisville Metro Police Department (LMPD) (i.e., responding to calls for service, conducting traffic or pedestrian stops, and/or engaging in proactive enforcement activity).
Officers who are not required to wear their protective vest must have it readily available and accessible while on-duty.
All sworn members must wear their departmentally-issued or approved protective vest, while on-duty, under the following circumstances:
• When executing a search warrant at a residence, building, or structure;
• When engaged in any active aggressor or similar high-risk situation; or
• When directed or ordered by a supervisor.
Further, officers must wear their departmentally-issued or approved protective vest while working authorized secondary employment in Class A or Class B uniform.
It is understood that police work is often rapid, tense, and uncertain. As a result, there may be reasonable and articulable instances where a member may be unable to comply with this policy due to quickly unfolding events in their immediate presence.
4.11.2 PROTECTIVE VEST ISSUANCE (KACP 10.5a)
The LMPD issues protective vests to all officers. Officers may purchase an alternate protective vest to be worn while on-duty (refer to SOP 4.11.4). The decision to wear a non-issued protective vest should be based on the individual needs of each officer.
Issued protective vests, regardless of assignment, will be readily available to all officers during on-duty hours.
4.11.3 PROTECTIVE VEST MAINTENANCE
All officers are responsible for the care and safekeeping of their issued protective vest, in accordance with the manufacturer’s instructions.
4.11.3 PROTECTIVE VEST MAINTENANCE (CONTINUED)
Officers will not wear a protective vest that has expired, that has sustained the impact of a gunshot, or when the ballistic panel has been damaged (refer to SOP 4.11.5 for replacement instructions).
4.11.4 ALTERNATE BALLISTIC PANEL CARRIERS
Ballistic panel carriers are permitted to assist officers in performing police-related functions by allowing versatility in how they carry necessary and required uniform equipment. Alternate ballistic panel carriers will be standardized and uniform in order to present a professional appearance at all times. The following ballistic panel carriers are optional uniform items that may be purchased by officers. Only the listed ballistic panel carriers are approved for wear with LMPD duty uniforms. Previously-issued carriers for plainclothes officers may not be worn with the uniform except in an emergency situation (e.g., active gunfire).
Point Blank Tailored Armor Carrier (TAC): The TAC, in midnight blue, is an optional uniform item that can be purchased by any officer. It is worn on the outside of the uniform.
The TAC may be worn:
• With the Class B uniform.
• With the Class C uniform (navy blue polo shirt).
• By any officer, at any time, during an emergency situation.
The TAC will have:
• The standard LMPD cloth badge or a similar badge made of rubber or a polyvinyl chloride (PVC)-type of material. Officers will have a silver badge and commanding officers will have a gold badge embroidered on the left breast area.
• The officer’s first initial and last name will be embroidered on the right breast area. Lettering will be silver for officers and gold for commanding officers.
• The ballistic panels from the officer’s issued protective vest will be removed and placed in the TAC (refer to SOP 4.11.2).
Information for purchasing a TAC can be found on the LMPD Intranet. Click on the “Forms” link, double click on the “Other Information” folder, and double click on the “Uniform Contracts” folder.
Point Blank Outer Duty Carrier (ODC)—Laser Cut: The ODC, in black, is an optional uniform item that can be purchased by any officer. It is worn on the outside of the uniform. The ODC is designed to transfer weight from the officer’s belt to the vest and to ease the access of the necessary uniform items. All equipment pouches attached to the ODC will meet the manufacturer’s specifications and guidelines. The addition of equipment pouches that are not made by Point Blank will require the approval of the LMPD Health and Safety Officer (HSO) prior to use.
The ODC may be worn:
4.11.4 ALTERNATE BALLISTIC PANEL CARRIERS (CONTINUED)
• With the Class B uniform.
• With the Class C uniform (navy blue polo shirt).
• By any officer, at any time, during an emergency situation.
The ODC will have:
• The standard LMPD cloth badge or a similar badge made of rubber or a PVC-type of material. It will be attached with Velcro or sewn to the ODC over the left breast area. Officers will have a silver badge and commanding officers will have a gold badge.
• The officer’s first initial and last name will be printed on a Velcro patch and attached on the right breast area. Lettering will be reflective silver for officers and reflective gold for commanding officers.
• A single “POLICE” identification panel attached with Velcro to the front and to the back of the ODC. Officers will have “POLICE” in silver reflective lettering and commanding officers will have “POLICE” in gold reflective lettering.
The size of the name tape and “POLICE” identification panel will be standardized based on the dimensions of the ODC.
The following duty equipment and pouches are authorized for carry on the ODC:
• Departmentally-approved Oleoresin Capsicum (OC) spray
• Radio
• Issued flashlight
• ASP or similar authorized expandable baton
• Tourniquet pouch
• Medical glove pouch
• Body-Worn Camera (BWC) pouch
• Handcuff pouch and/or strap matching the specific belt worn
• Conducted Electrical Weapon (CEW) utilizing the currently-issued Blackhawk holster. The CEW will be attached in a cross-draw manner if it is mounted on the ODC.
• One (1) patrol rifle magazine in a soft or hard pouch, black in color.
Handgun ammunition pouches are not approved for carry on the ODC.
The above mentioned items are the only approved items listed for wear on the ODC. Additional patches and/or Velcro insignias are not authorized for wear on the ODC.
The ballistic panel from the officer’s issued protective vest will be removed and placed in the ODC (refer to SOP 4.11.2).
Information for purchasing an ODC can be found on the LMPD Intranet. Click on the “Forms” link, double click on the “Other Information” folder, and double click on the “Uniform Contracts” folder.
4.11.4 ALTERNATE BALLISTIC PANEL CARRIERS (CONTINUED)
Mocean External Vest Carrier: The Mocean External Vest Carrier, in dark navy, is an optional uniform item that may be purchased by any departmentally-certified bike, All-Terrain Vehicle (ATV), or Electric Standup Vehicle (ESV) officer. It is worn on the outside of the uniform.
The Mocean External Vest Carrier may be worn with:
• The Class E uniform.
• By any officer, at any time, during an emergency situation.
The Mocean External Vest Carrier will have:
• The standard LMPD cloth badge. Officers will have a silver badge and commanding officers will have a gold badge embroidered on the left breast area.
• The officer’s first initial and last name will be embroidered on the right breast area. Lettering will be white for officers and gold for commanding officers.
• The protective plates from the officer’s issued protective vest will be removed and placed in the Mocean External Vest Carrier (refer to SOP 4.11.2).
Officers will have one (1) of the protective vest options readily available, at all times.
4.11.5 PROTECTIVE VEST REPAIRS, ALTERATIONS, AND REPLACEMENT
No repairs or alterations to issued protective vests will be made without the approval of the HSO.
Officers whose protective vest is expired or damaged in the line-of-duty will contact the HSO to obtain a temporary loan of another properly-fitting protective vest until such time as a permanent replacement protective vest may be issued to, or replaced by, the affected officer(s). In the unlikely event the department fails to issue a new or temporary properly-fitting replacement vest, the officer will be placed on non-punitive administrative duties in the division or unit to which the officer is assigned until a proper replacement is issued.
Officers may be held responsible for the replacement of an issued protective vest if it is lost, stolen, or damaged beyond serviceability due to the officer’s negligence. The replacement of any alternate ballistic panel carrier will be at the expense of the individual officer.

sections.title: Dress and Equipment Requirements for Plainclothes Sworn Personnel
sections.text:
4.12 DRESS AND EQUIPMENT REQUIREMENTS FOR PLAINCLOTHES SWORN PERSONNEL (KACP 12.1)
4.12.1 POLICY
1) All plainclothes officers will abide by this policy, with the exception of units specified by the Chief of Police, or their designee.
2) Officers and detectives who work, or have the potential to work, in an undercover capacity or in certain specialty units may dress according to standards established by their commanding officer (refer to SOP 4.28).
3) An employee will be supported in complying with SOP 4.12 consistent with the employee’s gender identity or expression and will be required to comply with the same standards of dress and appearance that apply to other LMPD sworn members.
4.12.2 DRESS
1) Officers will be neat, clean, and well-groomed.
2) Clothing will consist of a business-like appearance that promotes a professional image of the department.
3) Solid-colored polo shirts may be worn at the discretion of the division/section/unit commander.
a) Division/section/unit commanders are responsible for approving the shirt colors. b) The official Louisville Metro Police Department (LMPD) patch will be embroidered on the left breast area. c) The officer’s first initial and last name will be embroidered on the right breast area.
A) Male Plainclothes Officers
1) Male plainclothes officers will wear a dress shirt, or other collared shirt, and dress pants. Sweaters, sports jackets, or suits are optional.
2) Dress shirts with ties may be required by division command.
3) Earrings are prohibited, except as provided in SOP 4.2.7.
4) Tight, revealing, or otherwise inappropriate work attire is not allowed.
B) Female Plainclothes Officers
1) Female plainclothes officers will wear dress pants, dress shirts, blouses, sweaters, skirts, or dresses.
4.12.2 DRESS (CONTINUED)
2) Earrings must be in compliance with SOP 4.2.7.
3) Tight, revealing, or otherwise inappropriate work attire is not allowed.
4.12.3 HAIR
1) Extreme hair styles (i.e., Mohawks, shaved-in lines other than a part, shaved-in images, etc.) or hair coloring in hues that are not found in the natural spectrum of human hair (i.e., pink, blue, purple, green, fluorescent colors, etc.) are prohibited.
2) If secondary employment dictates that a uniform is to be worn, an officer whose normal duty assignment is non-uniform will conform to the more stringent requirement in SOP 4.2 (Uniform Guidelines).
A) Male Plainclothes Officers
1) Male officers’ hair will not extend completely over the ears or below the top of the shirt collar.
2) Beards, mustaches, sideburns, and goatees are permitted in accordance with the requirements contained in SOP 4.2 (Uniform Guidelines).
B) Female Plainclothes Officers
1) Female officers’ hair must be neat in appearance.
4.12.4 EQUIPMENT
1) Plainclothes officers will carry the following equipment:
a) Departmentally-approved firearm with at least one (1) fully-loaded spare magazine; b) Departmentally-approved impact weapon, Oleoresin Capsicum (OC) spray, or Conducted Electrical Weapon (CEW) (CC ¶175). The CEW will be kept in a holster that is positioned on the opposite side of the body from the firearm (CC ¶182(j)); c) Appropriate badge and identification (ID) card; AND d) Departmentally-approved handcuffs. Handcuffs will be either black in color or silver, chrome, or other natural colors of metal. Any other colors, excluding handcuffs that have been altered in color by the department, will not be used while on-duty or off-duty.
2) Plainclothes officers will have departmentally-issued green wristbands readily available at the scene of an incident for identification purposes to other responding officers or civilians (refer to SOP 4.28).
4.12.5 FIREARMS
1) Officers who are wearing plainclothes attire must have their badge displayed next to their duty holster, or otherwise visible, at all times.
2) Members should refer to SOP 8.2 for information on court attire and securing firearms, and/or concealment of firearms, when wearing business attire to court, respectively.
4.12.6 BADGE AND IDENTIFICATION
1) Patrol officers who are permanently assigned to detective positions will be assigned a detective badge and ID card. Unless approved by the Chief of Police, or their designee, only the following sworn personnel will be assigned a detective badge and ID card:
• Major Crimes Division (MCD) detectives
• Criminal Interdiction Division (CID) detectives
• Patrol Bureau detectives
2) If a detective is temporarily assigned to a detail or performs secondary employment requiring a uniform, they will wear the detective badge, in accordance with SOP 4.10.
3) Officers and detectives are prohibited from exchanging badges with each other.
4) If a detective is permanently transferred or reassigned to a uniform position, or if an officer is permanently transferred or reassigned to a detective position, they will contact the Assistant Chief of Police/Administrative Bureau, or their designee, within seven (7) days to obtain an appropriate replacement badge.
5) Officers and detectives who are permanently transferred or reassigned to, or from, a uniform or detective position will also go to the LMPD Photo Lab within seven (7) days and obtain an appropriate ID card.
6) Uniformed officers who are temporarily assigned to a state, federal, or departmental task force will not be issued a detective badge or ID card.
4.12.7 TEMPORARY ASSIGNMENT
1) Officers who are temporarily assigned to a unit will dress appropriately for the assignment, as directed by the unit supervisor and/or in accordance with SOP 4.2 (Uniform Guidelines).
4.12.8 COURT ATTIRE
1) Officers will appear in court in uniform or appropriate business attire (refer to SOP 8.2).

sections.title: Firearms
sections.text:
4.13 FIREARMS (KACP 1.9)
4.13.1 OVERVIEW (KACP 1.3f)
1) It is the policy of the Louisville Metro Police Department (LMPD) to train and qualify all sworn personnel in the use of departmentally-approved firearms, holsters, accessories, and ammunition, and be instructed in the use of force policies outlined in Chapter 9 of this Standard Operating Procedure (SOP), prior to being authorized to carry a weapon (KACP 4.6d, 5.3).
2) The use of firearms is only authorized in deadly force situations, excluding training and the humane destruction of animals (refer to SOP 9.1.9 and SOP 8.33.2).
3) The use of any force by officers will be guided by the Use of Force Principles referenced in SOP 9.1.1.
4) Officers are authorized to carry concealed deadly weapons under Kentucky Revised Statute (KRS) 527.020(3) and Louisville Metro Code of Ordinances (LMCO) 41.03 and 135.06. This authorization allows both on-duty and off-duty officers to carry an authorized weapon within their jurisdiction (refer to SOP 5.1).
5) Authorized firearms are those that comply with the department's specifications and have been properly inspected and registered with the Firearms Training Center (FTC) prior to being approved for service (KACP 1.10b).
6) Officers and recruits will receive departmental training on the proper and safe use of authorized firearms.
7) Training is conducted and documented by certified firearms training instructors (KACP 1.10b).
8) As required by the FTC, officers must qualify with their approved uniform service pistol (USP) twice annually, one (1) of which will be in night/low-light conditions (CC ¶209) (KACP 1.10a).
9) If assigned, plainclothes service pistols (PSPs) will require an annual supplemental weapon system (SWS) qualification (KACP 1.10a).
10) These qualifications will occur before the officer is authorized to carry the weapon (KACP 1.10a-b).
11) Records of weapon qualifications, dates, and results, including the make, model, caliber, and serial number of each firearm, are maintained by the Training Division. This applies to all departmentally-approved weapons, whether on-duty, off-duty, and/or backup weapons (KACP 1.10b).
12) 18 U.S.C 922(g)(3) prohibits any person who uses or possesses marijuana to receive any firearm or ammunition. Under the federal law, there is no exception for state-authorized medicinal marijuana or cannabis. Therefore, sworn police officers who carry a firearm as part of their job duties cannot possess or consume medicinal cannabis, regardless of being a registered cardholder.
4.13.2 OFFICIAL DEPARTMENTAL FIREARMS (KACP 1.9)
1) All USPs and PSPs used in an on-duty or official capacity will be issued by the LMPD.
2) Authorized firearms not issued by the LMPD will meet the required specifications determined by the FTC.
3) All USPs and PSPs will be equipped with night sights if not equipped with a Micro Red Dot System (MRDS) optic.
4) USPs and PSPs will also be equipped with a weapon-mounted light (WML) approved by the FTC.
5) PSPs are optional and may be used by officers in a plainclothes or administrative assignment when not in uniform in lieu of the USP.
6) Any modifications of the issued equipment, to include the WML and MRDS, must be performed only by FTC staff.
7) If an officer chooses to utilize an approved personally-owned accessory that replaces departmentally-issued equipment, the departmentally-issued equipment must be turned in to the FTC. FTC staff will then install the personally-owned accessories.
8) The FTC should be consulted prior to officers purchasing equipment to certify compatibility with the weapon system.
9) The determination as to whether an accessory is authorized for duty use will be at the discretion of FTC command staff.
10) Should officers elect to use a personally-owned accessory, it should be with the understanding that it will not be replaced by the department if the weapon in which it is attached is seized for evidence within the course of an investigation.
4.13.3 UNIFORM SERVICE PISTOLS AND ACCESSORIES
A) Approved Uniform Service Pistols
1) The following are the official issued USPs of the department:
• Glock Model 17 (black) (9mm).
• Glock Model 17 Modular Optic System (MOS) (black) (9mm).
• Glock Model 47 (black) (9mm).
• Glock Model 47 MOS (black) (9mm).
B) Uniform Service Pistol Accessories
1) Officers are authorized to purchase extended magazine base plates for issued USP magazines. The extended capacity base plates must be one (1) of the following options:
4.13.3 UNIFORM SERVICE PISTOLS AND ACCESSORIES (CONTINUED)
• Arredondo Accessories Base Pad and Spring, +3 or +6 variants, black in color; or
• Glock factory +2 Mag Extension Kit, black in color.
4.13.4 PLAINCLOTHES SERVICE PISTOLS AND ACCESSORIES
A) Approved Plainclothes Service Pistols
1) The following are the official issued PSPs of the department:
• Any of the approved USPs.
• Glock Model 48 (black) (9mm).
• Glock Model 48 MOS (black) (9mm).
B) Approved Plainclothes Service Pistol Accessories
1) Officers are authorized to purchase accessories for use on issued PSPs that include magazines and MRDS that meet the below specific specifications:
• Shield Arms Magazines (Gen 3 or greater) – 15 round capacity.
o The use of Shield Arms Magazines requires the purchase of a Shield Arms metal magazine release.
• MRDS options include:
o Holosun EPS Carry. o Holosun 507K or 407K.
2) Officers must have completed the LMPD MRDS transition course to utilize a MRDS on their issued PSP (KACP 1.10b).
4.13.5 LONG-BARRELED WEAPONS
A) Shotguns
1) Effective July 1, 2023, shotguns are no longer issued by the LMPD; therefore, personally-owned shotguns are authorized for on-duty or official use and will meet the following specifications:
• Remington 870 (black or with a stainless-steel finish).
• Stocks, foregrips, and other accessories must be black or have a woodgrain finish.
2) Exceptions must be approved by the Firearms Training Section Commander.
3) All shotguns must meet departmental specifications and be inspected by the FTC (KACP 1.10b).
4.13.5 LONG-BARRELED WEAPONS (CONTINUED)
4) The FTC will be consulted on any potential purchases of shotguns and any optional accessories by officers for qualification or on-duty use prior to purchase (KACP 1.10b).
B) Rifles
1) Effective June 15, 2023, the LMPD issued ArmaLite Model 15 (AR-15)-style patrol rifles to officers to be used in an on-duty or official capacity.
2) The official rifle issued by the department is an FN 15 Small Rifle Platform (SRP), Generation Two (2) Precision (G2P) Carbine in the 16-inch or 11.5-inch barrel configuration.
3) Departmental rifles will have the following equipment installed prior to being issued:
• Aimpoint Red Dot Sight (RDS) Optic.
• Streamlight Rail Mounted Series Two (2) (RM2) WML.
• Fabrique Nationale (FN) backup iron sights.
• Two (2)-point sling.
• Dust cover.
• Forward assist.
• Two (2) magazines.
4) The FTC will issue FN 15 Rifles in the 11.5-inch configuration to members of the following units:
• Bomb Squad.
• Criminal Interdiction Division (CID) – Violent Crime Unit and Fugitive Unit.
• Homeland Security Unit (HSU).
• Canine Unit.
5) Members, who are issued an 11.5-inch rifle and transfer from a position in their unit, will turn in the rifle to the FTC and will be issued another rifle in the 16-inch configuration upon their reassignment, at the discretion of the FTC Staff and based on the needs of the department.
6) All officers will successfully pass an approved patrol rifle course, prior to carrying a rifle while on-duty (KACP 1.10b).
7) Officers who are left-handed may request an ambidextrous safety from the FTC upon being issued their rifle. The FTC will provide and install the equipment for the officer.
8) Personally-owned patrol rifles are not authorized for use on-duty or off-duty in an official capacity.
C) Rifle Accessories
1) Officers are authorized to purchase the following accessories for use on issued rifles:
a) Vertical Grips (must be one (1) of the following four (4) options):
4.13.5 LONG-BARRELED WEAPONS (CONTINUED)
o Bravo Company Manufacturing (BCM) Modular Lock (M-Lok) vertical grip. o Magpul M-Lok vertical grip. o Unity Tactical M-Lok vertical grip. o Emissary Development Handbrake.
b) WMLs (must be from one (1) of the following reputable manufacturers):
o Modlite. o Surefire. o Cloud Defensive. o Streamlight.
c) Ambidextrous Controls:
o Radian Weapons Raptor-LT Ambidextrous Charging Handle (black in color). o Radian Weapons Talon 45/90 – Two (2) Lever Kit, Ambidextrous Safety Selector AR-15 (black in color).
d) Magnifiers
o Officers may utilize personally-owned magnifiers on their issued patrol rifles if the following conditions have been met:
 The officer has completed the eight (8)-hour “LMPD Patrol Rifle Magnifier Course.” The course may not be substituted by any other training class or certification.  The personally-owned magnifier must be attached to the rifle with a “flip to side” mount that places the center of the lenses at a height of 1.54” to ensure capability with the issued Aimpoint Duty Red Dot Sight issued with the LMPD rifle. The mount should also be a quick detach or “QD”-style mount allowing for easy removal from the rifle, if needed.  The magnifier must be 3x magnification only. Higher levels of magnification are not authorized.  The personally-owned magnifier must be from one (1) of the following reputable manufacturers:
• Aimpoint.
• EoTech.
• Holosun.
• Trijicon.
• Vortex.
e) Iron Sights
o For improved compatibility with magnifier systems, the following iron sights may be utilized:
 Magpul MBUS Pro Front and Rear Sights (offset variants are not authorized).
4.13.6 NON-LETHAL/LESS-LETHAL WEAPONS (KACP 1.8)
1) The FTC will assign LMPD divisions 12-gauge less-lethal shotguns.
2) Less-lethal shotguns will be equipped with an orange stock and forend, prior to being placed into service. A shotgun lacking orange equipment is prohibited for use as a less-lethal system.
3) The division commanders, or their designees, will conduct an inventory and inspect their division’s less-lethal systems monthly for functionality.
4) All less-lethal systems will be inspected prior to being reassigned to another officer.
5) Should deficiencies be discovered, the less-lethal system will be returned to the FTC for repairs as soon as possible.
4.13.7 SPECIALTY UNIT WEAPONS
A) Specialty Unit Firearms
1) All specialty unit firearms will be approved by the Chief of Police, or their designee, and comply with standards established by the team commander and the FTC.
2) Only trained and authorized members will use specialty unit firearms.
3) Specialty unit members who are issued weapons, approved by the FTC, will attend and successfully complete all applicable training courses and be recertified on these weapons twice annually (KACP 1.10a- b).
B) Specialty Unit Less-Lethal (KACP 1.8)
1) All less-lethal weapons will be marked by the manufacturer and/or FTC in order to designate that they are only to be used for less-lethal responses.
2) The following less-lethal systems will be maintained, assigned, and deployed by either the Special Weapons and Tactics (SWAT) Team or the Special Response Team (SRT), in accordance with each team’s respective operations manual:
• Pepper ball carbine launcher.
• 40mm less-lethal launcher (Special Impact Munitions System (SIMS)).
4.13.8 OFF-DUTY/BACKUP WEAPONS
1) While within Jefferson County, an officer will carry an approved issued or personally-owned pistol of .380 caliber or larger, which has a minimum of a five (5)-shot capacity, with which they have qualified (refer to SOP 5.1).
2) Off-duty/backup weapons will be carried in a holster.
4.13.8 OFF-DUTY/BACKUP WEAPONS (CONTINUED)
3) For a personally-owned firearm to be approved, the weapon must be from a reputable manufacturer that is International Organization for Standardization (ISO) 9001-certified and the weapon must be inspected by the FTC staff prior to being placed into service (KACP 1.10b).
4) The approval of any off-duty weapon is dependent upon the discretion of the FTC. Members are encouraged to contact the FTC prior to the purchase of an off-duty weapon (KACP 1.10b).
5) Officers should carry the pistol in a concealed manner. When an officer’s activity is such that concealment is not practical, the weapon will be kept as readily accessible as circumstances permit (refer to SOP 5.1).
6) Pursuant to KRS 237.137, an officer may carry their issued USP, issued PSP, or off-duty/backup pistol concealed, while not acting in an official capacity, at any location within the state where an on-duty officer is permitted to carry a firearm.
4.13.9 OFFICIAL DEPARTMENTAL HOLSTERS
1) The following Safariland brand holsters are the only departmentally-approved holsters for uniformed duty use:
a) Class A, Class B, Class C, and Class D Issued Uniform Holster:
o Safariland 7365 Stainless Target Extreme (STX)/plain black finish holster. o Safariland 7360RDS STX/plain black finish holster.
b) Class A, Class B, Class C, and Class D personally-owned holster:
o Safariland 7360 STX/plain black finish holster. o Safariland 7362 STX/plain black finish holster. o Safariland 7360RDS STX/plain black finish holster. o Safariland 7362RDS STX/plain black finish holster.
2) Any holsters with the SERPA-style (or similar) retention and release are prohibited for departmental use, including training. This includes any holster with an external release button primarily designed to be disengaged by use of the trigger finger.
3) Duty holsters issued for USPs will be equipped with an Axon Signal Sidearm Activator (SSA) device that will be installed by the FTC prior to issue. FTC personnel will be the only authorized members of the department to maintain these devices and will change the batteries in each unit annually. Should an officer’s SSA malfunction, the officer will contact the FTC, as soon as possible, and take the device to the FTC at the earliest opportunity during their current shift or at the beginning of their next tour of duty.
4) The LMPD will issue officers an approved uniform holster compatible with a Streamlight Tactical Light Rail (TLR)-7A pattern WML when they are issued a USP.
5) Officers who wish to utilize another authorized WML, such as the Surefire X-300 or the Streamlight TLR- 1/High Lumens (HL), will purchase an approved holster from the preceding list in order to be in compliance
4.13.9 OFFICIAL DEPARTMENTAL HOLSTERS (CONTINUED)
with SOP 4.13.10. The personally-owned holster will be brought to the FTC to have an Axon SSA installed prior to being used in an official capacity. The FTC will verify that the SSA device functions with the officer’s weapon/light/holster combination prior to authorizing it for service.
6) If a member chooses to utilize a personally-owned holster, the issued holster must be returned to the FTC.
7) Officers may elect to utilize a personally-owned tourniquet pouch attached to their holster. The only authorized tourniquet pouch for on-duty use is the Safariland Tourniquet (TQ) System. As with any personally-owned item, this must be installed by the FTC.
4.13.10 SERVICE PISTOL WEAPON-MOUNTED LIGHTS
1) The FTC will issue officers a Streamlight TLR Pattern WML when they are issued a USP.
2) Officers may carry the following departmentally-approved optional accessory WMLs for their service pistols if they have been trained and qualified in their use:
• Streamlight TLR-1/HL.
• Streamlight TLR-7A.
• Surefire X300 (all variants).
• Cloud Defensive EPL Duty.
3) Officers who wish to utilize another approved WML may purchase one at their own expense for official use but will be required to purchase an approved compatible holster specifically designed for the pistol and light combination (refer to SOP 4.13.9).
4) If a member chooses to utilize a personally-owned WML, the Streamlight TLR Pattern must be turned in to the FTC.
5) Members are encouraged to contact the FTC prior to the purchase of a WML to verify compatibility with other issued equipment. The determination as to whether a WML is authorized for duty use will be at the discretion of FTC personnel.
6) WMLs will only be activated by the integrated paddle switch using the support hand. The use of the dominant hand, trigger finger, or any other finger of the dominant hand to activate the WML is prohibited, except in extreme emergency situations (e.g., the support hand is injured).
7) The use of grip and/or pressure activation switches on a pistol are prohibited.
8) The use of the WML does not replace the handheld flashlight as the primary illumination device.
9) Officers shall not use a WML in situations which do not call for them to have a firearm ready.
4.13.10 SERVICE PISTOL WEAPON-MOUNTED LIGHTS (CONTINUED)
10) Officers who wish to carry the accessory WML will be required to qualify with the WML and handheld flashlight in night/low-light conditions (KACP 1.10a).
4.13.11 MICRO RED DOT SYSTEM OPTICS
MRDS optics are authorized for use on departmentally-issued USPs and personally-owned, off-duty firearms if the following criteria have been met.
A) Departmentally-Issued USPs
1) Officers who wish to receive an LMPD-issued USP equipped with an MRDS optic for official use must complete the FTC’s MRDS Transition Course (KACP 1.10b).
2) Upon completion of the course and the availability of equipment, the officer will turn in their iron sight-only Glock 17 and will be issued either a Glock 17 MOS or Glock 47 MOS USP equipped with one (1) of the approved MRDS optics.
3) Employees who were hired prior to January 1, 2024, are not required to transition to the MRDS optic.
4) The following are the approved MRDS optics of the department for official use:
• Holosun 509T.
• Aimpoint Acro P-2.
B) Personally-Owned, Off-Duty Firearms
1) Officers who wish to carry an MRDS optic on their personally-owned, off-duty firearm must meet the following requirements:
a) The officer must have completed a course on the use of MRDS optics on pistols from a reputable source. This training can come from the LMPD’s curriculum, Department of Criminal Justice Training (DOCJT), or private outside training companies. It will be at the discretion of the FTC as to whether an outside training company is reputable. Officers are encouraged to contact the FTC prior to attending any course from an outside training company to make certain that the curriculum will be accepted as a qualifying school. Officers who pay for a school that is not authorized through the appropriate process of official requests for training or who attend a training class that is not deemed reputable by the FTC will not be reimbursed for any out-of-pocket expenses (KACP 1.10b). b) The officer must provide a certificate of training for any MRDS optic class from outside of the LMPD to be kept on file (KACP 1.10b). c) Aftermarket or third party milled slides will not be authorized. MRDS optic-equipped off-duty firearms will be factory manufactured weapon systems with modular slide mounted cut-out mounting systems designed to accept MRDS optics. d) The firearm, MRDS optic, and MRDS optic mounting system will be inspected by the FTC prior to qualification (KACP 1.10b).
4.13.11 MICRO RED DOT SYSTEM OPTICS (CONTINUED)
e) The officer must pass the LMPD’s Off-Duty Qualification Course with the MRDS optic-equipped off- duty firearm as specified in SOP 4.13.21 (KACP 1.10a-b). f) All other guidelines from SOP 4.13.8 regarding off-duty firearms apply.
2) Only the following reputable manufacturer’s MRDS optics will be approved for use on off-duty firearms:
• Holosun.
• Aimpoint.
• Trijicon.
• Leupold.
• Steiner.
• Vortex (Defender series model only. Contact the FTC for clarification prior to purchasing).
3) Each optic is subject to individual inspection and approval from the FTC (KACP 1.10b).
4.13.12 ALTERING
1) Authorized firearms, including magazines, magazine floor plates, and rifle dust covers, will not be altered in any way unless approved by the FTC. Such alterations include, but are not limited to, the addition of laser sights or ghost ring sights.
2) Officers who carry approved service pistols will only utilize night sights or MRDS optics authorized by the FTC.
3) Engravings, decals, or other markings on authorized firearms, including magazines, magazine floor plates, and rifle dust covers, are limited to those applied by the manufacturer for identification purposes only (as approved by the FTC) or those required by state or federal law or regulation. A small LMPD logo is authorized.
4) Firearms with unauthorized engravings, decals, or other markings will be removed from service.
4.13.13 AMMUNITION
1) Officers will only carry ammunition issued or approved by the FTC in all authorized firearms and extra ammunition pouches. Ammunition will not be altered.
2) Uniformed officers will carry a minimum of two (2) complete reloads for their on-duty weapon.
3) Plainclothes officers will carry at least one (1) complete reload.
4) Weapons and magazines will be loaded to the maximum recommended capacity.
4.13.14 APPROPRIATE DEPLOYMENT OF LONG-BARRELED WEAPONS
1) Officers will be held strictly accountable for the deployment of all long-barreled weapons.
2) Situations calling for the deployment of long-barreled weapons may include, but are not limited to:
• Potentials for mass violence (e.g., active aggressor).
• Perimeter containment in barricaded suspect situations with a known weapon potential.
4.13.15 UNITED STATES HOUSE OF REPRESENTATIVES (H.R.) 218 – THE LAW ENFORCEMENT OFFICERS’ SAFETY ACT (LEOSA)
1) Officers who are traveling outside of Kentucky will abide by H.R. 218 (Law Enforcement Officers’ Safety Act (LEOSA) of 2004) in regard to the carrying of concealed firearms.
2) H.R. 218 exempts qualified active law enforcement officers from local and state prohibitions on the carrying of concealed firearms. However, the following laws are still applicable to qualified active law enforcement officers:
• Federal laws or regulations governing the carrying of firearms onto aircraft, in federal buildings, on federal property, and in national parks.
• State laws which prohibit the carrying of firearms on state or local government property.
• State laws which allow private entities to prohibit firearms on their private property.
3) The LEOSA excludes machine guns, firearm silencers, and other destructive devices from the definition of firearms.
4) In order to qualify for H.R. 218, an officer must have their departmentally-issued identification (ID) card on their person. Therefore, if an officer’s police powers have been suspended, for any reason, they will not be in compliance with H.R. 218. Additionally, an officer will not be covered under this act if they are under the influence of alcohol or drugs.
5) Officers who carry concealed firearms in accordance with H.R. 218 are further restricted by the department to carry only their approved USP and/or the off-duty/backup pistol on which they are currently qualified.
6) If an officer does not meet the standards as outlined above and is traveling outside of Kentucky, they will abide by all firearms regulations of the jurisdiction through which they travel.
4.13.16 FIREARMS ABOARD COMMERCIAL AIRCRAFT
A) Authorization
1) Officers will abide by all Federal Aviation Administration (FAA), Transportation Security Administration (TSA), and individual airline regulations regarding weapons on aircraft.
4.13.16 FIREARMS ABOARD COMMERCIAL AIRCRAFT (CONTINUED)
2) In order to carry a departmentally-approved firearm aboard a commercial aircraft, officers must first complete the TSA’s Law Enforcement Officer Flying Armed (LEOFA) Training Course. Officers should contact the HSU Commander to request the LEOFA Training Course.
3) For each assignment that requires a departmentally-approved firearm to be carried aboard a commercial aircraft, the officer must complete the Law Enforcement Officers Flying Armed form (LMPD #08-0020) and forward the form to the Chief of Police, or their designee, at least 24 hours prior to the planned departure.
4) If approved by the Chief of Police, or their designee, they will forward the form to the National Crime Information Center (NCIC) Unit.
5) The NCIC Unit will forward the necessary information to the TSA, who will make the final approval or denial.
6) If the request is approved, the TSA will forward a receipt message with a unique alphanumeric identifier to be used, by the officer at the airport, on the day of travel.
7) If the date or route of travel changes, the officer must contact the NCIC Unit to obtain a new unique alphanumeric identifier to reflect the new travel information.
B) Day of Travel
1) On the day of travel, the officer must identify themself as an LEOFA upon check-in at the airline ticket counter.
2) The officer may be required to complete additional paperwork for the airline on which they are flying.
3) Upon arrival at the TSA Security Checkpoint, the officer will be required to use the designated LEOFA checkpoint lane and provide the TSA with their departmentally-issued badge/credentials, boarding pass, second form of government identification, the alphanumeric identifier issued by the TSA, and any additional paperwork for the airline on which they are flying.
4) The officer will then complete the TSA Checkpoint sign-in log entry and proceed to their boarding gate.
5) At the boarding gate, the officer will inform the gate agent of their presence and armed status and provide any requested paperwork.
6) The gate agent will identify any additional armed officers on the flight and escort the officer to meet the Pilot in Command, Federal Air Marshal(s), and Federal Flight Deck Officer(s) on the flight.
4.13.17 FIREARMS IN COURTROOM
1) Officers may be armed in a courtroom at the discretion of the presiding judge.
4.13.17 FIREARMS IN COURTROOM (CONTINUED)
2) When a presiding judge prohibits a firearm in their court, the officer will secure the weapon in a locked receptacle as close to the courtroom as possible.
3) An officer who is wearing business attire to court must have their firearm concealed, at all times.
4.13.18 FIREARMS IN RESTRICTED AREAS
1) When an officer enters an area of another government agency that restricts, or has regulations governing, firearms (e.g., correctional facilities, Central State Hospital, Hall of Justice, Federal Court House), they will abide by that agency’s regulations.
2) However, under all circumstances, the weapon will be properly secured.
3) Pursuant to KRS 237.137, officers may carry their firearms on private property (e.g., malls, schools, restaurants, theaters), even if a weapons prohibition is posted. If a private venue denies entry to an off-duty officer with a concealed firearm, the officer should refer to SOP 5.1.
4.13.19 CARE OF FIREARMS
1) Officers will not use or handle firearms in a careless or imprudent manner.
2) When storing a pistol in all LMPD vehicles, the pistol must be stored in a locked compartment (e.g., trunk, glove compartment, or console) and the vehicle must be locked.
3) Long-barreled weapons will be carried in the vehicle’s trunk or in a locking device inspected and approved by the FTC and the Administrative Services Division Commander (KACP 1.10b). For the purposes of this policy, the passenger compartment/cargo area of a truck or sport utility vehicle (SUV) is not considered a trunk.
4) Metro Fleet Services technicians will install all approved locking devices within LMPD vehicles.
5) Firearms will be maintained and stored in such a manner that they will be clean and in serviceable condition.
6) The FTC armorer has the responsibility of removing from service any weapon determined to be unsafe or nonfunctional.
7) Any officer who is issued a loaner weapon will qualify with that weapon, prior to carrying it while on-duty or off-duty.
8) Personally-owned weapons that are deemed unsafe will be repaired and/or replaced by the officer, at their own expense.
4.13.20 DISCHARGE OF FIREARMS (KACP 1.11a-b)
A) Notification
1) Officers are required to immediately report any instance of a discharge of a firearm to their division/section/unit commander, while on-duty or off-duty, in the below situations:
a) When the discharge involves an authorized firearm. b) When the discharge involves an unauthorized firearm while on-duty.
2) Exceptions to the notification requirement include:
• Target practice.
• Training purposes.
• Off-duty recreational purposes (e.g., hunting, competitions).
B) Investigative Responsibility
1) The division/section/unit commander is responsible for the investigation of discharges of firearms when:
a) Negligent or accidental discharges of firearms occur without injury or directed at a subject; or b) Discharge of firearms against domesticated animals (refer to SOP 8.33.2).
o Investigations are not required for the humane destruction of non-domesticated (wild) animals.
2) The Public Integrity Unit (PIU) will be responsible for the investigation of discharges of firearms when (refer to SOP 1.9.1 and SOP 8.12.2):
a) Incidents involving the discharge of firearms by an officer during police action, regardless of injuries.
o Excluding the discharge of firearms for training or the humane destruction of animals.
b) Negligent or accidental discharges of firearms that cause injury.
C) Investigative Documentation Requirement
1) The division/section/unit commander of the officer involved is responsible for documenting the investigation through the completion of an Administrative Incident Report (AIR), via BlueTeam (refer to SOP 3.1.1).
2) The division/section/unit commander will include all pertinent information known to them within the AIR and, if applicable, will reference the PIU investigation.
3) All findings and recommendations will be forwarded, through the appropriate chain of command.
4) The PIU investigation will be documented within a case file and in accordance with the PIU Operations Manual.
4.13.21 FIREARMS QUALIFICATIONS (KACP 1.10a-b)
A) Approved Uniform Service Pistols
1) All officers will qualify with their approved USP on a schedule determined by the FTC. At a minimum, these qualifications will be held biannually (CC ¶209).
2) Qualifications will be based on proficiency standards and scored on a pass/fail basis.
3) Officers who are experiencing difficulty passing the approved USP qualification course after three (3) attempts will be given a maximum of one (1) hour of remedial training by the FTC, within the same tour of duty. The full hour may be verbally waived by the officer.
4) Following the remedial training, and within the same tour of duty, the officer will be given one (1) additional attempt to successfully complete the qualification course based on the passing proficiency standard.
5) Should an officer unsuccessfully obtain the passing proficiency standard after the four (4) attempts, the officer’s testing cycle will be considered a failure to qualify.
6) Should an officer fail to qualify with their USP, they are prohibited from carrying the pistol, while on-duty or off-duty, until a passing score is achieved (CC ¶209). They will surrender their USP or PSP, along with any departmentally-issued ammunition, to the firearms training instructor (CC ¶209).
7) Additionally, if the officer failed to qualify with their USP, the officer will immediately contact their supervisor to surrender their departmental vehicle and be served with a Limitation of Police Powers form (LMPD #11- 0008) (refer to SOP 2.16).
8) Officers who have failed to qualify with their USP will be required to return to the FTC on the following business day (Monday-Friday) and receive additional remedial training. Upon completion of remedial training, the officer will continue the process outlined in this section until successfully achieving a passing proficiency standard score.
9) Officers are prohibited from qualifying with SWSs until a passing proficiency standard is achieved with their USP.
B) Supplemental Weapon System Qualifications
1) Qualifications for patrol rifles, shotguns, PSPs, or off-duty/backup pistols, referred to as SWSs, will be conducted at a minimum of once a calendar year at the discretion of the FTC staff.
2) The annual qualification for each SWS will be a qualification for that specific weapon system and will be based on proficiency standards and scored on a pass/fail basis.
3) For off-duty/backup pistol qualifications, officers will be required to conceal their weapons with an off-duty holster meeting the below specifications:
4.13.21 FIREARMS QUALIFICATIONS (CONTINUED)
a) Made by a reputable manufacturer (contact the FTC staff for guidance). b) Made from a material that maintains its shape after the pistol is drawn from it. c) Allow for either strong side or appendix carry and will completely cover the trigger guard. d) Set up for either in-the-waistband or outside-the-waistband carry configuration. e) SERPA-style holsters or “sticky” holsters are not authorized.
4) Should an officer unsuccessfully obtain the passing proficiency standards within two (2) consecutive attempts, within the same tour of duty, the officer’s testing cycle will be considered a failure to qualify, and the issued weapon system and ammunition will be surrendered to the FTC staff and secured in the armory (CC ¶209).
5) Personally-owned, off-duty firearms will NOT be surrendered to the FTC staff; however, officers will be prohibited from carrying them in an off-duty capacity and will turn-in issued duty ammunition to the FTC staff.
6) Any officer who fails to qualify with a departmentally-issued SWS will be required to complete four (4) hours of remedial training to be scheduled at the discretion of the FTC staff and the officer’s commanding officers.
7) Upon completion of the remedial training and as soon as feasible, the officer will have two (2) attempts to successfully achieve a passing proficiency standard score with the SWS.
8) If the officer is unsuccessful in achieving a passing proficiency standard score, post remedial training, they will repeat the remedial training again before any more attempts are made, until a passing proficiency standard score is obtained, excluding the patrol rifle.
9) Officers who fail to qualify with the patrol rifle, post remedial training, will be required to successfully complete a 40-hour Basic Patrol Rifle Course.
10) Officers who successfully obtain a passing proficiency standard score will be re-issued the SWS.
C) Less-Lethal Shotguns (KACP 1.8)
1) All officers will qualify with 12-gauge less-lethal shotguns on a schedule determined by the FTC. At a minimum, these qualifications will be held biennially.
2) Officers who fail to qualify will be given additional opportunities to meet the qualification standard by the FTC staff as time allows.
3) Should an officer fail to qualify with a 12-gauge less-lethal shotgun, the officer will be directed to turn in their assigned less-lethal system to their division command (if applicable).
4) Should an officer fail, the FTC staff will immediately notify the officer’s supervisor to ensure that the officer turns in the less-lethal shotgun (if applicable) and is not issued a 12-gauge less-lethal shotgun until the officer successfully passes the qualification.
4.13.21 FIREARMS QUALIFICATIONS (CONTINUED)
D) Return to Duty Qualifications
1) If an officer is returning to duty after being on administrative leave or administrative reassignment and is issued a temporary or loaned firearm, they must successfully qualify with this firearm prior to returning to duty.
2) When an officer is returning to duty after an officer-involved shooting (OIS), a member of the Peer Support Team (PST) or the departmental psychologist will be available to accompany them to the firearm qualification.
4.13.22 WEAPONS INSPECTIONS (KACP 27.3)
1) Weapons inspections are the responsibility of the FTC staff.
2) All weapons will be inspected during regular qualifications, at a minimum of once a year, by certified firearms instructors (KACP 1.10b).
3) Weapons will not be inspected at the division/section/unit level during formal or informal inspections.

sections.title: Departmental Vehicle Assignment and Usage
sections.text:
4.14 DEPARTMENTAL VEHICLE ASSIGNMENT AND USAGE
4.14.1 OVERVIEW (KACP 17.10)
The Louisville Metro Police Department (LMPD) maintains a 24-Hour Patrol Vehicle Program. Use of assigned vehicles is considered a privilege and not an employment right. The Chief of Police has the right to assign, deny, suspend, or remove any member from the 24-Hour Patrol Vehicle Program.
4.14.2 DEFINITIONS
24-Hour Patrol Vehicle Program: A program whereby officers are assigned departmental take-home vehicles to increase police presence in the community. Officers who are assigned take-home vehicles and while within the boundaries of Jefferson County are mandated to respond, as needed, to any calls for service as well as to render assistance to the public, in accordance with departmental policy.
Administrative Bureau: The Administrative Bureau, working in conjunction with Metro Fleet Services, is responsible for the daily operations (e.g., maintaining records of assignment, maintenance, recalls, and service) of departmental vehicles. The Assistant Chief of Police/Administrative Bureau retains the power to remove any vehicle from use if, in their opinion, further operation of the vehicle is unsafe or may cause damage to the vehicle. The Assistant Chief of Police/Administrative Bureau has the authority to make decisions regarding vehicle assignment, equipment, maintenance, repairs, or service to all departmental vehicles.
Departmental Vehicle: A car, truck, van, trailer, bus, boat, motorcycle, all-terrain vehicle (ATV), bicycle, Electric Standup Vehicle (ESV), aircraft, or any other vehicle owned, confiscated, leased, rented, maintained, or loaned to the department.
Take-Home Vehicle: A departmental vehicle assigned to a specific member that may be used during off-duty periods, in accordance with the guidelines set forth in this policy.
4.14.3 ASSIGNMENT OF TAKE-HOME VEHICLE
Officers who have completed one (1) year of sworn service with the LMPD may be assigned a departmental vehicle. The following policy also applies to professional staff who are assigned a departmental vehicle. Members who are residing within the boundaries of Jefferson County, Kentucky will be allowed take-home use of their assigned vehicle. Members whose primary residence is in the contiguous Kentucky counties of Jefferson County, Kentucky, are permitted to park their assigned vehicle at their primary residence while off-duty and use the vehicle for travel to, and from, work. These Kentucky counties include Bullitt, Spencer, Shelby, Oldham, Meade, and Hardin. Assigned vehicles are not permitted to be used outside of Jefferson County for personal use while off-duty. Members who are not residing in the contiguous Kentucky counties listed above are not permitted to drive their assigned vehicle outside of Jefferson County. Members who reside out-of-state (e.g., Indiana), in another Kentucky county not listed above, or who choose not to participate in the take-home vehicle program are required to park their assigned vehicle within Jefferson County, Kentucky, in a location approved by their division/section/unit commander, and complete an Out-of-County Resident Parking Location form (LMPD
4.14.3 ASSIGNMENT OF TAKE-HOME VEHICLE (CONTINUED)
#14-0009), in order to record where the vehicle is located during off-duty hours. Once this form has been completed, it will be forwarded, by the member, either by scanning the form and emailing it, or sending it via interdepartmental mail, to the Vehicle Impoundment Unit (VIU) Lieutenant and the Professional Standards Division (PSD) Adjutant Lieutenant. In times of need, vehicles assigned to non-residents may be used as pool vehicles.
Supervisors will perform a pre-inspection and post-inspection of any vehicle used in such a fashion to be aware of any damage that may have occurred during temporary use.
4.14.4 POOL VEHICLES
Each division/section/unit maintains a fleet of vehicles for use by on-duty members who are not yet eligible for the 24-Hour Patrol Vehicle Program. These vehicles are used at the discretion of the division/section/unit commander. The division/section/unit commander may temporarily issue such vehicles to members who qualify for the 24-Hour Patrol Vehicle Program, while their assigned vehicle is undergoing maintenance. The division/section/unit commander will designate a member of their staff to oversee the maintenance schedule of these pool vehicles. Pool vehicles will not be temporarily issued to members for the purpose of secondary employment.
4.14.5 REASSIGNMENT
When an officer is reassigned to another division/section/unit, their currently-assigned vehicle will remain in the division/section/unit that they are leaving. When an officer is assigned a vehicle within their respective division/section/unit, a Vehicle Change of Status form (LMPD #03-00-0065) will be completed and emailed to the Metro Fleet Services Vehicle Coordinator at “LMPD Fleet Management,” located within the department’s email distribution list. Any variation from this policy must be approved by the Fleet Coordinator.
4.14.6 USE OF VEHICLE DURING LEAVE
Any member, who will be off-duty, out-of-town, or on leave for more than seven (7) consecutive days, is required to inform their division/section/unit commander in advance. If needed, the member will turn in their vehicle prior to leaving town, as directed by their division/section/unit commander.
Sworn members, with the rank of major or above, have the authority to allow a member who is on extended vacation leave in excess of seven (7) days to keep their vehicle at their residence, if they live within Jefferson County. A member who lives outside of Jefferson County must secure their vehicle at their respective division/section/unit when on leave in excess of seven (7) days.
Take-home vehicle privileges may be suspended for members in the following situations:
• Extended leave
• Light-duty
4.14.6 USE OF VEHICLE DURING LEAVE (CONTINUED)
• Limited-duty
• Suspension
The revocation of vehicle privileges is determined by policy, the needs of the department, or at the discretion of the Chief of Police. In such cases, the vehicle will be turned in to the appropriate division/section/unit commander, or their designee.
4.14.7 VEHICLE USAGE
The following applies to all members:
• Members will adhere to all policies, procedures, laws, rules, and regulations as they pertain to vehicle usage, equipment, operation, and maintenance.
• Members will operate their departmental vehicle with due regard for public safety, at all times.
• Members will maintain proper control while operating a departmental vehicle.
• Members who are using departmental vehicles in an unauthorized manner or permitting the unauthorized use of a departmental vehicle may be subject to disciplinary action.
• Members who are using a departmental vehicle should exercise good judgment and avoid any conduct likely to cause unfavorable comment or embarrassment to the department.
• No member will use a departmental vehicle to further personal interests relative to any secondary employment or enterprise without written permission from the Chief of Police.
• Members will have their assigned departmental portable radio with them, at all times, when operating their assigned departmental vehicle.
• If a member loses the privilege of using an assigned departmental take-home vehicle, the member’s division/section/unit commander will send an email to the Police Human Resources (HR) Director that includes notice of the loss of the vehicle privilege, the member’s name, code number, and the date that the member was removed from the department’s take-home vehicle program.
• If a member loses the privilege of using an assigned departmental take-home vehicle, they will only borrow a departmental vehicle from another member or from a division/section/unit vehicle pool, with a commanding officer’s approval, for on-duty responsibilities.
• Members will not loan their departmentally-assigned vehicle to any other member who has lost their take-home vehicle privileges.
• Members will not loan their departmentally-assigned vehicle to any other member, even for legitimate departmental use, without the approval of a commanding officer.
• Members will not loan their departmentally-assigned vehicle to any non-departmental person, except to authorized members of Louisville Metro Government (LMG) for official business such as repairs, transports, or based on exigent circumstances.
• Members who are assigned a departmental take-home vehicle that is unavailable to the member for any reason (e.g., repairs) will not borrow a departmental pool vehicle for secondary employment, without the written approval of their division commander.
• If a member is eligible to be assigned a departmental take-home vehicle and the member decides that they do not wish to be assigned such a vehicle, they will inform their division/section/unit commander,
4.14.7 VEHICLE USAGE (CONTINUED)
who will send an email to the Police HR Director that includes notice of the voluntary removal from the department’s take-home vehicle program, the member’s name, code number, and the date that the member opted out.
• Any member who chooses not to participate in the take-home vehicle program will not use a pool vehicle for secondary employment purposes.
In addition to the above LMPD vehicle usage requirements and prohibitions, LMG vehicle use policies state, in part, that LMG employees will not engage in writing, sending, searching, or reading text-based communication on electronic wireless communications devices, whether such devices are owned by LMG or by the employee, including, but not limited to, a cell phone/smartphone, personal data assistant (PDA), pager, laptop, or tablet (e.g., iPad), when operating a moving LMG vehicle, when driving a personal vehicle on official LMG business, or when using electronic equipment supplied by LMG, while driving. Talking on a cell phone/smartphone while driving is also strongly discouraged, unless hands-free methods (e.g., speaker phone, headset, Bluetooth) are utilized (refer to SOP 4.30).
Mobile Data Terminals (MDTs) assigned to LMPD vehicles are considered an exempt device under the provisions of the LMG policy prohibitions, when safely used to receive, accept, or clear from calls for service or to perform other legitimate police functions (e.g., rolling license plate check). A member who is operating a departmental vehicle should not needlessly type, or otherwise manually enter data, which is not related to a dispatched call for service or other legitimate police function (e.g., text messaging or instant messaging), into an MDT while the vehicle is in motion. If the safe operation of the vehicle is impaired by the reading or viewing of the MDT screen (e.g., heavy traffic, higher speed conditions), a member should stop the vehicle in a safe location in order to use the MDT.
Volunteers are not permitted to operate any LMG vehicles pursuant to LMG policies.
4.14.8 OPERATIONAL JURISDICTIONS OF VEHICLES
While on-duty, members will not operate a departmental vehicle outside of Jefferson County without proper authorization from a commanding officer.
If authorization is given, the member will immediately notify MetroSafe of the location to which they will be traveling, their car number, and the authorizing commanding officer’s name.
Upon return to Jefferson County, the member will immediately notify MetroSafe of their return.
Exceptions not requiring a commanding officer’s prior approval include:
• Making a turnaround to return to the jurisdictional boundaries of the department.
• The authorized pursuit of a suspect or vehicle (refer to SOP 12.1).
• Local travel (refer to SOP 4.14.9).
• The authorized use of a take-home vehicle (refer to SOP 4.14.3).
4.14.9 LOCAL TRAVEL
Trips for official business, utilizing a departmental vehicle and not requiring an overnight stay, are considered local travel. Requests for local travel must be approved by a commanding officer with the rank of lieutenant or above (refer to SOP 2.18).
Additionally, local travel may be authorized for the following reasons:
• Training
• Official business in Frankfort or Richmond
• Firearms enhancement at Jefferson Gun Club
• Firearms enhancement at Knob Creek Gun Range
• Firearms enhancement at OpenRange Indoor Gun Range
• Firearms enhancement at Silver Creek Conservation Club
• Picking up departmentally-authorized uniform items from Galls in Lexington
• Picking up or dropping off departmentally-authorized firearms or equipment at Kiesler Police Supply
• Picking up departmentally-authorized uniform items from T-Box Tactical
• Investigations of crimes committed within Jefferson County
• Testifying in court cases outside of Jefferson County related to duties performed as a departmental member
Members who are seeking the use of a departmental vehicle for official business requiring an overnight or extended stay should refer to SOP 2.18.
4.14.10 ALCOHOLIC BEVERAGES/INTOXICATING SUBSTANCES
Members are prohibited from:
• Operating a departmental vehicle with any measurable amount of alcohol or any other substance in their system that could impair their ability to operate a vehicle.
• Transporting any intoxicant or illegal drugs in a departmental vehicle, except as required in an official capacity.
• Parking a departmental vehicle within the proximity of any establishment that serves alcoholic beverages as its main source of income, unless in an official capacity or in an emergency.
4.14.11 TOBACCO USE
In accordance with LMG Personnel Policy 1.18(3), the smoking of tobacco products and the use of e-cigarettes are prohibited in all departmental vehicles, which are defined in section 4.14.2 of this policy.
4.14.12 EATING
No more than two (2) marked vehicles and one (1) unmarked vehicle may be parked, at any given time, at a restaurant or other related establishment while on-duty. On-duty members are prohibited from eating at establishments whose primary source of income is derived from the sale of alcoholic beverages. On-duty members will refrain from eating at the bar area of any establishment.
4.14.13 USE OF SEATBELTS (KACP 21.4)
Members and volunteers are required to wear seatbelts while operating or riding in a departmental vehicle, unless a tactical situation dictates otherwise. Passengers are required to wear seatbelts, unless physical handicaps prevent proper usage. Small children and infants will always be secured in a child restraining device or seatbelt, as required by law, and will be positioned in the rear seats due to airbag concerns. Any prisoner who is being transported in a departmental vehicle should be secured with a seatbelt, unless a physical handicap or officer safety issues prevent the proper use of a seatbelt. If a seatbelt cannot be properly secured, members should request their commanding officer’s assistance with arranging alternate transportation (e.g., booking van). Members should refer to SOP 10.5 for detailed information regarding prisoner transportation.
4.14.14 OFF-DUTY POLICE ACTION
Off-duty officers who are operating a departmental vehicle within the boundaries of Jefferson County, Kentucky are required to monitor the police radio and take appropriate action to offenses that occur in their presence or requests for assistance from other officers. Appropriate action is that which is both necessary, considering the totality of the circumstances, and within their ability to handle at the time (e.g., availability of weapon, radio communication, physical condition).
At a minimum, an off-duty officer will brief on-duty officers of pertinent information (e.g., license number, descriptions, circumstances).
4.14.15 PASSENGERS
A member may use their assigned vehicle while off-duty to transport persons who they might normally transport in a personally-owned vehicle, in accordance with the following:
• If possible, off-duty officers who are responding to a serious offense or emergency should have any passengers exit the vehicle at a safe and secure location before proceeding to the call.
• Members will be held accountable for the appearance and conduct of their passengers.
On-duty officers are authorized to transport the following:
• Civilian riders (refer to SOP 8.10)
• Prisoners (refer to SOP 10.5)
• Civilians under police-related circumstances (refer to SOP 7.10)
• Other departmental members
4.14.16 PARKING
Members are prohibited from parking in handicapped zones, fire lanes, no parking or stopping zones (including peak time no parking), turning lanes, tow away zones, bus stops, or reserved parking spaces (e.g., media parking only, Crime Scene Unit (CSU) parking only, MetroSafe, Office of the Commonwealth’s Attorney, etc.).
Members should not utilize parking meters in the downtown area unless they are on official business or they pay the appropriate parking fee. The downtown area is defined as the area bounded by Roy Wilkins Avenue (9th Street), Brook Street, Broadway, and the Ohio River. Official business is defined as handling a call for service, taking some type of self-initiated activity (refer to SOP 1.11), conducting criminal investigations, or attending meetings at the direction of competent authority. Members who are on official business must display their “official business” parking permit on the dash of the departmental vehicle.
Official business privileges are not extended to members who are attending court, the Grand Jury, or official meetings at the Jefferson County Attorney’s Office or Office of the Commonwealth’s Attorney.
Members who are attending court or meetings near the courthouse buildings may park in the lot provided by the Fraternal Order of Police (FOP), via the lease agreement with LMG, or on a surface street or in a parking garage at their own expense.
If a member, who is in control of a departmental vehicle, receives a parking citation while not on official business, they are required to pay the fine in the same manner as a private citizen. The fine must be paid within seven (7) working days. Nothing in this policy prevents a member from appealing a parking citation, using the same appeals process as a private citizen.
If a member, who is in control of a departmental vehicle, receives a parking citation while conducting official business, they will write a memorandum that states when and where the citation was issued prior to the end of their next tour of duty. The memorandum should state the nature of the official business and the reason for parking in the particular location. The memorandum and a copy of the parking citation will be forwarded, through the appropriate chain of command, to the Assistant Chief of Police/Administrative Bureau. Any member who fails to pay a parking citation, when required to do so or to make the proper written notifications if the parking was justified, will be subject to disciplinary action.
4.14.17 UNATTENDED VEHICLES
Members should not leave departmental vehicles unsecured or running unattended. If circumstances are such that the officer is unable to secure the vehicle, the vehicle will be secured as soon as possible and MetroSafe should be notified of the location and circumstances.
4.14.18 IDLING
Members should not leave vehicle engines idling for extended periods, unless required for operational reasons, such as for the safety of police canines or human occupants or the active use of emergency lighting. Members should adopt fuel conservation practices, including reducing unnecessary engine idling.
4.14.19 VEHICLE APPEARANCE
Members are responsible for the appearance and cleanliness of their vehicle, regardless of whether the vehicle is temporarily or permanently assigned.
Members may take their vehicles to a vendor who is under contract with LMG no more than once every two (2) weeks. Members may also wash and clean the vehicles themselves or pay, at their own expense, for a commercial car wash, as needed.
Some vehicles may require detailed cleaning. In such cases, the member will complete a Vehicle Detailing Request form (LMPD #17-0006) and submit it, through the appropriate chain of command, to the Fleet Coordinator for approval. If the vehicle requires decontamination, members will clean the vehicle themselves if it is not severely contaminated and does not require detailed cleaning (refer to SOP 12.2). Departmental vehicles will not be used for the transportation of bulk material(s) protruding from the trunk or interior compartment. Exceptions to this standard would include departmental equipment or evidence.
4.14.20 DAMAGE TO/COLLISIONS INVOLVING DEPARTMENTAL VEHICLES
When a departmental vehicle is involved in a collision or damage is caused to a departmental vehicle, it will be reported on the Vehicle Damage or Collision Report form (LMPD #03-07-0190). Collisions must be reported even if there is no apparent damage to a departmental vehicle. If criminal charges are filed, damage to any property will be noted in the arrest/citation narrative. Members will obtain a copy of the property damage appraisal or the Newburg Road garage invoice and present to the prosecutor in order to request restitution for the damages. The request for restitution should be part of the plea agreement or sentencing. If a member alleges that a mechanical defect or failure was a factor in the collision, the departmental vehicle will be immediately towed to Metro Fleet Services for a mechanical inspection. Under no circumstances will a member operate a vehicle that is alleged to have a mechanical defect or failure. The vehicle in question must first be inspected and cleared by Metro Fleet Services before it can be operated again.
In cases where minor injuries, if any, occur as the result of a collision involving a departmental vehicle, a commanding officer from the division where the collision occurred will respond to the scene and complete the collision report and a Vehicle Damage or Collision Report form, as soon as possible following the incident (refer to SOP 7.7). In cases where very serious or life-threatening injuries occur as the result of a collision involving a departmental vehicle, the Traffic Unit will respond to the scene and complete the collision report. A commanding officer from the division where the collision occurred will respond to the scene and complete a Vehicle Damage or Collision Report form, as soon as possible following the incident (refer to SOP 7.7). In cases where the severity of injuries are unclear, or the collision scene is extremely complex, commanding officers will confer with the Traffic Unit to determine who will investigate the collision. The investigating officer will also create a diagram of the collision.
The Vehicle Damage or Collision Report form, including the collision report number, if applicable, will be forwarded electronically, no later than the end of the commanding officer’s tour of duty, to “LMPD Vehicle Damage Notification,” located within the department’s email distribution list. The original report will then be forwarded through the appropriate chain of command. Photographs of all damaged vehicles are to be taken by the investigating or responding supervisor, the collision investigator, or the Crime Scene Unit (CSU). These photos will be uploaded into the Digital Evidence Management System (DEMS), and copies attached to the
4.14.20 DAMAGE TO/COLLISIONS INVOLVING DEPARTMENTAL VEHICLES (CONTINUED)
original Vehicle Damage or Collision Report form. Any other paperwork (e.g., uniform citation, collision diagrams, etc.) associated with the damage will be submitted with the form (refer to SOP 7.7).
Members with damaged departmental vehicles will contact the Metro Fleet Services supervisors within seven (7) days of the damage to arrange for the vehicle’s evaluation and/or repair estimate. Members with rental vehicles will contact the leasing vendor within seven (7) days of the damage. Once the property damage assessment is complete, members have seven (7) days to schedule the needed repairs through the Metro Fleet Services supervisors. Officers will be responsible for keeping their scheduled appointment.
4.14.21 VEHICLE INSURANCE (KACP 2.2)
Off-duty members of the Louisville Metro Police Department (LMPD) who are operating departmental vehicles are covered under LMG’s self-insured automobile liability program. This liability insurance offers up to $100,000 per accident for any bodily injury or property damage caused by the member’s negligent operation of an LMG vehicle. This coverage is dependent upon the member’s cooperation with LMG in its investigation or defense of any suit. This insurance will not cover the member for amounts exceeding the $100,000 limit. Therefore, it is recommended that each member purchase supplemental insurance coverage at their own expense.
The current LMG automobile insurance identification (ID) card can be found on the LMPD Intranet. Click on the “Forms” link and double click on the “Vehicle” folder.
4.14.22 VEHICLE MAINTENANCE
Members should refer to SOP 4.15 for departmental vehicle maintenance procedures.

sections.title: Vehicle Maintenance
sections.text:
4.15 VEHICLE MAINTENANCE (KACP 21.5)
4.15.1 OPERATIONAL MAINTENANCE
Members are responsible for maintaining any departmental vehicles under their control. A departmental vehicle is defined as a car, truck, van, trailer, bus, boat, motorcycle, off-road all-terrain vehicle (ATV), bicycle, Electric Standup Vehicle (ESV), aircraft, or any other vehicle owned, confiscated, leased, rented, maintained, or borrowed by the department. Maintenance includes, but is not limited to, the following:
• Tire pressure;
• Tire treadwear;
• Brake performance;
• Emergency equipment;
• Vehicle wiper blades;
• Vehicle fluid levels;
• Vehicle operational lighting (e.g., headlights, taillights, side marker lights, parking lights, turn signals, etc.);
