2) Placing weight on a person’s head or back, such as with their knees or arms, for a prolonged period may increase the risk of injury. Therefore, officers should avoid placing weight on a person’s head or back for a period of time beyond that which is objectively reasonable to gain and/or maintain control.
3) Additionally, officers should avoid placing weight on a person’s neck for a period of time longer than that which is objectively reasonable to gain and/or maintain control of the subject due to the increased risk of injury as a result of air and/or blood flow restriction.
4) Carotid/vascular restraints and chokeholds are prohibited (KACP 1.14), unless deadly force is authorized (CC ¶173).
9.1.5 RESTRAINED PERSON
A) Force Against Restrained Persons
1) Once a person is handcuffed or otherwise restrained, the use of force is restricted to minimal force that is objectively reasonable to maintain control, unless the person is (CC ¶166):
a) Physically combative, uncontrollable, or violent; OR b) Presents an imminent threat to the safety of the officer(s), or others; OR c) To prevent escape.
2) Members are cautioned that the use of force that may be objectively reasonable against an unrestrained person may not be objectively reasonable when used on a restrained person.
B) Positioning of Restrained Persons
1) Restrained persons, who are not standing, are to be seated upright or placed on their side.
2) Members shall not allow a restrained person to remain in the following positions:
a) Face-down, as it may cause positional asphyxia (CC ¶167, 168); OR b) On their back, since it can cause nerve damage to the wrist and/or forearm area (CC ¶167).
C) Handcuff Pain or Injury
1) Officers will ensure that handcuffs are properly applied and double-locked (refer to SOP 10.5).
2) Handcuffs, by their design, are inherently uncomfortable. Complaints of pain caused by wearing handcuffs will be addressed as soon as possible, and when it is safe and feasible to do so, by readjusting or otherwise ensuring proper application.
3) Should any visible injury (e.g., bruising, swelling, bleeding, etc.) occur as a result of wearing handcuffs, or if there is a lasting complaint of pain following the removal of handcuffs, an Administrative Incident Report (AIR) will be completed as a Level 2 reportable force (refer to SOP 9.5).
9.1.6 OFFICER INTERVENTION (KACP 1.13)
1) Officers shall act to prevent or stop any officer, regardless of rank or assignment, from using force that is clearly objectively unreasonable or otherwise violates law or LMPD policy (LMCO 36.04) (CC ¶159(h)).
2) Intervention may be verbal and/or physical.
9.1.7 DUTY TO REPORT
1) Members shall report any incidents involving use of force that is objectively unreasonable to their commanding officer immediately, or as soon as practicable.
2) Once notified of potentially unlawful or excessive force, commanding officers will immediately notify the Special Investigations Division (SID) and/or the Professional Standards Division (PSD) Commander through their chain of command.
3) Members who are inhibited from reporting violations through the appropriate chain of command are required to submit the information directly to the SID or PSD Commander, as appropriate, or to the Chief of Police.
9.1.8 RETALIATION PROHIBITED (KACP 12.6b-c)
1) Members are prohibited from retaliating against any individual because they have prevented, intervened, or reported uses of force that violate law or LMPD policy (CC ¶159(j)).
2) Any member who engages in such retaliation will be subject to discipline, up to, and including, termination.
3) Any member who feels they have been subjected to such retaliation should report this action through the appropriate chain of command.
4) The division commander, or their designee, to whom the member reports will escalate the complaint to the PSD Commander or directly to the Chief of Police.
5) Any member who is inhibited from reporting retaliation through their chain of command should report the retaliation directly to the PSD Commander, or to the Chief of Police.
9.1.9 USE OF DEADLY FORCE (KACP 1.3b, e, 1.11a-b)
A) Standards for the Use of Deadly Force
1) Deadly force is only authorized when the officer reasonably believes, based on the totality of the circumstances, that the person against whom deadly force is used poses an imminent threat of death or serious injury to the officer, or another person.
2) Deadly force is not authorized unless other reasonable uses of force and de-escalation techniques have been exhausted or would clearly be ineffective or unsafe.
9.1.9 USE OF DEADLY FORCE (CONTINUED)
B) Standards for the Use of Deadly Force on Fleeing/Escaping Subjects
1) Pursuant to KRS 503.090, deadly force is authorized to arrest or prevent the escape of a fleeing subject when, under the facts and circumstances known to the officer, it is reasonable to believe (KACP 1.3c):
a) The arrest is for a felony involving the use of, or the threatened use of, physical force likely to cause death or serious physical injury; AND b) It is likely that the person to be arrested will clearly endanger human life unless they are apprehended without delay; OR c) The subject is an arrested person, and deadly force could justifiably have been used to make the arrest, and the escape of the subject would pose an imminent danger of death or serious physical injury to the officer, or another person.
C) Verbal Warning
1) In deadly force encounters, officers should identify themselves as a law enforcement officer and give a clearly audible verbal warning stating their intention to use deadly force, before the use of deadly force unless such actions are not safe and feasible or when the officer’s intentions are otherwise apparent (LMCO 36.04) (CC ¶211(b)).
D) Firearms Usage
1) The discharge of a firearm at a person is considered deadly force.
2) Officers who are discharging a firearm should remain cognizant of the following:
a) The direction in which the firearm is being discharged. b) The danger of discharging a firearm while running or moving.
3) Officers will only point their firearm at a person when the officer reasonably believes that the situation may escalate to create an imminent threat of serious physical injury or death to the officer, or another person (CC ¶210).
E) Prohibitions on the Use of Deadly Force
1) Deadly force is never authorized to apprehend a fleeing misdemeanor or non-violent felony suspect (NOBLE), unless the subject poses an imminent threat of death or bodily harm to the officer, or other persons.
2) Deadly force shall not be used against an individual whose actions present a threat only to themselves (CC ¶211(d)).
9.1.9 USE OF DEADLY FORCE (CONTINUED)
3) Warning shots are not permitted (KACP 1.3e).
4) Officers will not discharge a firearm unless the officer has identified the location of the intended target (CC ¶211(a)).
5) Officers will not discharge their firearms either at or from a moving vehicle except in response to gunfire, imminent threat of gunfire, or, in the rare case, where the vehicle is intentionally being used as a weapon against the officer, or others (LMCO 36.04) (CC ¶211(c)).
6) Officers will not discharge their weapons at vehicles simply because a subject is attempting to flee (CC ¶211(c)).
7) Officers will avoid tactics that unreasonably place them in a position where the vehicle can be used as a weapon against them (CC ¶211(c)).
9.1.10 MEDICAL CARE
1) Following a use of force, as soon as reasonably practical, officers will render medical aid consistent with their training and shall request Emergency Medical Services (EMS) to respond to the scene, as needed, when there is a visible injury, complaint of injury, sign of medical distress, or when medical attention is requested by any person (CC ¶174).
2) EMS will be contacted to respond to all incidents involving the successful application of a complete cycle of a CEW (CC ¶184). SOP 9.2 provides additional guidance regarding the use of CEWs and medical care to be provided.
3) In case of injury resulting from a use of force involving a juvenile, officers will provide medical attention to the juvenile and attempt to notify the juvenile’s parent, guardian, or other responsible adult as soon as possible, if known or otherwise provided by the juvenile (CC ¶165).
9.1.11 REPORTING AND REVIEW
1) All officers must report uses of force as required by SOP 9.3.
2) Officers must notify an uninvolved commanding officer immediately, or as soon as practicable, following the use of reportable force, as required in SOP 9.3.4.
3) A failure to notify a commanding officer regarding a use of any reportable force may result in discipline.

sections.title: Use of Intermediate Force Tools
sections.text:
9.2 USE OF INTERMEDIATE FORCE TOOLS (KACP 1.3b, 1.8, 1.11-b-c)
9.2.1 OVERVIEW (KACP 1.3f)
1) The purpose of this policy is to guide the use of intermediate force tools that are available to sworn departmental members. Intermediate force tool options (e.g., Conducted Electrical Weapons (CEWs), chemical agents, impact weapons, etc.) provide additional alternatives to the use of deadly force.
2) As with all uses of force, officers will continually assess the situation and modify their use of any force (CC ¶159(g)), including intermediate tools, in ways that are consistent with the sanctity of human life, dignity of all persons, and the safety of all involved, based on the totality of circumstances (refer to SOP 9.1) (CC ¶159(a- b)) (KACP 1.3a).
3) Officers will only carry, and use, departmentally-approved intermediate force tools that are enumerated in LMPD policy and in which they are trained and qualified to use, except in extenuating situations when an officer may use any resource at their disposal (CC ¶172).
4) The use of departmentally-approved intermediate force tools will be consistent with departmental training.
5) The use of intermediate force tools outlined in this policy will comply with Standard Operating Procedure (SOP) 9.1.4 requirements that such force is objectively reasonable, minimizes harm, and is continually assessed to adjust the use of force as the threat diminishes (KACP 1.3a).
6) Officers are required to report each use of an intermediate force tool, outside of a training setting, pursuant to SOP 9.3.
a) Officers must articulate the reason for each individual use of intermediate force tools.
9.2.2 CARRYING INTERMEDIATE FORCE TOOL OPTIONS
1) Uniformed and plainclothes capacity officers and commanding officers will carry the following departmentally- approved intermediate force tools on their person, in which they have been trained to use, at all times while on-duty, unless the officer or commanding officer is assigned to an administrative unit or is participating in an undercover operation (CC ¶175):
• CEW (optional for the ranks of lieutenant or above);
• Impact weapon; AND/OR
• Oleoresin Capsicum (OC) spray.
2) If either the impact weapon or OC spray is not carried on their person, it must be readily available in the officer’s vehicle.
3) On-duty plainclothes officers and commanding officers who are assigned to an administrative unit will have the following departmentally-approved intermediate force tools readily available in the officer’s vehicle:
• CEW (optional for the ranks of lieutenant or above);
9.2.2 CARRYING INTERMEDIATE FORCE TOOL OPTIONS (CONTINUED)
• Impact weapon; AND/OR
• OC spray.
4) Off-duty officers, while not in uniform, are not required to carry any intermediate force tools.
9.2.3 USE OF CEWS
1) The CEW probe activation is designed to stimulate a portion of the nervous system with sufficient pulsed electrical energy to cause neuro-muscular incapacitation (NMI), which overrides an individual’s voluntary motor functions.
2) A standard CEW cycle is the completed circuit between probes that allows a five (5) second burst of electrical energy designed to induce NMI (refer to SOP 9.1.2).
A) Standards for the Use of CEWs
1) The use of a CEW on a subject is a Level 2 use of reportable force.
2) Officers are authorized to activate CEWs on subjects when (CC ¶179):
a) There are grounds for arrest or detention present; AND b) Such force is necessary to protect the officer or another person from imminent danger.
3) Mere non-compliance or passive resistance, either verbal or physical, does not constitute imminent danger.
a) The subject must display behavior, through active physical or verbal means, which reasonably demonstrates an imminent danger to the officer, or another person.
4) Prior to the use of a CEW, officers should evaluate the apparent age, size, gender, physical/behavioral capabilities, and health concerns of a subject and the feasibility of lesser force options (CC ¶182(a)).
5) Officers may utilize the CEW on aggressive animals which present a physical threat to the officer, or another person (refer to SOP 8.33).
B) CEW Activation
1) Officers will activate the CEW on a subject the least number of times to mitigate the imminent danger (e.g., voluntary compliance, opportunity to restrain the subject) (KACP 1.3a).
2) All activations and subsequent cycles of the CEW must be objectively reasonable and otherwise comply with law and LMPD policy (CC ¶180).
3) The initial single probe activation and a second probe activation count as one (1) single Level 2 reportable force (CC ¶180).
9.2.3 USE OF CEWS (CONTINUED)
a) If the subject complies before the second probe is activated, the single probe activation is still considered a Level 2 reportable force (CC ¶180).
4) Additional probes may be activated if one (1) of the initial probes fail, until a circuit is completed, or the subject complies.
5) Officers are required to reevaluate the situation after the first complete standard CEW cycle to determine if subsequent cycles are necessary (CC ¶180).
a) In determining whether subsequent cycles are objectively reasonable, officers are required to consider whether the individual has the ability to comply and has been given a reasonable opportunity to do so prior to applying another cycle (CC ¶180).
6) Each additional probe activation or each subsequent cycle of the CEW is a separate application of force and requires the officer(s) to articulate the justification for each activation and cycle in their use of force statement (CC ¶180).
C) CEW Prohibitions
1) Except where deadly force is justified, officers should not activate CEWs (CC ¶182(f)):
a) When it’s reasonably evident that an activation may cause serious physical injury, including if the subject is in danger of falling from a significant height or drowning. b) If the subject is operating an automobile (i.e., car, truck, motorcycle), all-terrain vehicle (ATV), bicycle, scooter, or any other motorized vehicle or hazardous machinery. c) If the subject has been exposed to flammable material (e.g., gasoline, alcohol-based pepper spray).
2) Except in exigent circumstances that cause an imminent danger to the officer, or another person, officers should not discharge CEWs on a subject who is obviously (CC ¶182(g)):
• Pregnant • Visibly frail
• Elderly • Low body mass
• Small child (based on body mass)
3) No more than three (3) standard CEW cycles, or 15 seconds cumulative, will be activated against a subject during a single incident, unless exigent circumstances are present. If a subject does not respond to the three (3) standard CEW cycles, the officer is required to consider alternative control measures, absent exigent circumstances (CC ¶181).
a) EXIGENT CIRCUMSTANCES may include a situation where, although the CEW has been effective, that officer is alone and unable to control the suspect’s actions, placing the officer at risk of imminent danger following the standard CEW cycles.
9.2.3 USE OF CEWS (CONTINUED)
4) Officers shall not intentionally target the (CC ¶182(d)):
• Face • Breasts
• Head • Chest
• Neck • Genitals
5) Officers shall not intentionally activate more than one (1) CEW at a time against a subject (CC ¶182(e)). However, some activations are not successful due to poor probe spread, low muscle mass contact, missed probes, etc. In these situations, another officer may activate their CEW:
a) If such activation occurs, the second officer will shout the word “taser” and activate their CEW. b) The first discharging officer will discontinue use of their CEW and aid in securing the subject or consider another reasonable force alternative.
6) A CEW will not be activated solely on the basis that a subject flees from an officer (CC ¶182(h)), but may be used on a fleeing subject when:
a) They are, or were, using a deadly weapon or dangerous instrument; OR b) They are wanted for a violent felony; OR c) Such force is necessary to protect the officer, or another person, from imminent danger (CC ¶179).
7) Officers will not activate a CEW on a subject:
a) Who is restrained by handcuffs or other restraints, unless the prisoner is aggressively physically resisting and lesser means would likely be ineffective to subdue the individual or they have already failed (CC ¶182(i)); OR b) To prevent the swallowing of evidence or to dislodge, or retrieve, evidence from a subject’s mouth or other body cavities; OR c) To obtain compliance for evidence gathering.
D) Guidance Regarding CEW Use
1) Officers shall keep CEWs in a holster that is on the opposite side of their firearm to reduce the chances of accidentally drawing and/or firing a firearm (CC ¶182(j)).
2) When tactically feasible and if doing so does not place officers, or other persons, at-risk, the officer should:
a) Clearly warn the subject who is the target, prior to activating a CEW, and provide reasonable time to cease the activity that justifies the activation of a CEW (CC ¶182(b)); AND b) Prior to activation of a CEW, verbally announce their intentions to other officers present by shouting the word “taser” (CC ¶182(c)).
3) Officers will aim the CEW to target the lower center mass of the subject (i.e., below the shoulders in the back or below the ribcage in the front) (CC ¶ 182(d)).
9.2.3 USE OF CEWS (CONTINUED)
4) During, and following, any standard CEW cycle, the arresting officer(s) will focus on the window of opportunity when the subject may be immobilized by the CEW to physically restrain and secure the subject, in order to minimize the number of standard CEW cycles (e.g., cuffing under power).
a) Officers will engage in restraint techniques that do not impair a person’s respiration (CC ¶183).
5) When using the CEW, officers will continually assess each standard CEW cycle to determine whether further activations are necessary, or a different tactic should be used (CC ¶180) (KACP 1.3a).
a) Officers will consider whether the individual has the ability to comply, and has been given reasonable opportunity to do so, prior to applying another cycle (CC ¶180).
E) Post Use of CEW
Medical Care
1) In cases where the CEW probes are activated, officers will only remove the probes in a manner consistent with their training (CC ¶183).
a) After removing the probes from the subject, the officer(s) will collect the probes by putting them in a proper sharps container in an ambulance, at a medical facility, or at the Evidence Property Unit (EPU) for disposal.
2) In situations where the probes are in the head, neck, breast, groin, buttocks, or other sensitive areas, medical personnel will perform the removal (CC ¶183).
a) For the purposes of this policy, a Health and Safety Officer (HSO)-certified Emergency Medical Technician (EMT) will not be considered medical personnel.
3) Officers will continually monitor the subject while in police custody and update MetroSafe in situations where the subject displays any of the following unusual reactions (CC ¶183):
a) The subject complains of chest pains. b) Through observation or complaint, the subject experiences shortness of breath. c) The subject is, or was, unconscious as a result of the use of the CEW. d) The subject is evidently under the influence of drugs. e) The subject displays a continued state of agitation after the use of the CEW. f) The subject falls after the use of the CEW and is injured as a result of the fall, unless the injury is a minor scrape or cut.
4) If a subject displayed unusual reactions as a result of the use of the CEW, the cartridge(s) and probes will be turned in to the EPU as evidence (CC ¶183).
5) Emergency Medical Services (EMS) will be contacted to respond to all incidents involving the application of a completed cycle of a CEW and an appropriate medical evaluation will be performed (CC ¶184).
9.2.3 USE OF CEWS (CONTINUED)
a) Officers should not transport a subject prior to EMS arrival, unless other medical necessities require immediate transport and the officer is closer to a medical facility than EMS. b) If the arrested person displays any of the unusual reactions listed above, but refused treatment from EMS, officers will immediately transport them to University of Louisville Hospital for examination by emergency room (ER) personnel.
6) Officers will inform EMS or other medical personnel of the facts and circumstances of the CEW discharge (CC ¶183).
7) Officers will obtain the EMS Unit number and the run number related to the treatment of the subject and record the information on the Administrative Incident Report (AIR), as well as any arrest citation so the Louisville Metro Department of Corrections (LMDC) can reference.
F) Downloading CEW Data
1) After an officer uses their CEW, their commanding officer, as standard procedure in a use of force investigation, will ensure that the involved CEW battery is docked and data is uploaded to Evidence.com. The CEW download report will be linked as an attachment to the BlueTeam entry as part of the AIR documentation, in accordance with SOP 9.5.
2) If an officer is suspected of misusing their CEW, their commanding officer, the Professional Standards Division (PSD), or the Public Integrity Unit (PIU) may retrieve the CEW from the officer and download the data by docking the battery. The downloaded information will be stored as a departmental record and as evidence.
G) CEW Maintenance and Inspections
1) Officers will maintain a fully-loaded CEW magazine. At the conclusion of an incident in which a CEW was discharged, the officer will obtain replacement cartridges from the EPU.
2) Officers are responsible for verifying their CEWs and batteries are in working order before the start of their tour of duty.
3) During formal inspections, commanding officers will inspect their officers’ CEWs for damage, low batteries, and a full magazine.
9.2.4 USE OF CHEMICAL AGENTS
1) With the exception of the Special Weapons and Tactics (SWAT) Team and Special Response Team (SRT) (as noted below), the use of chemical agents is limited to OC spray and pepper ball munitions.
2) The use of chemical agents, other than OC spray and pepper ball munitions, used solely by the SWAT Team and SRT will be in accordance with this policy, the respective team’s operations manual, and the manufacturer’s recommendations.
3) The use of chemical agents for crowd control or civil disturbance will be conducted pursuant to SOP 12.6.5.
9.2.4 USE OF CHEMICAL AGENTS (CONTINUED)
A) Standards for the Use of OC
1) The use of OC spray on a subject is a Level 2 reportable force.
2) The use of OC spray is permitted against subjects who display:
a) Active resistance; OR b) Present an imminent danger to officers, or others.
3) The initial, and each subsequent, use of OC spray must be objectively reasonable, including when used for crowd dispersal or protection (CC ¶187, 188) (KACP 1.3a).
B) Deployment of OC
1) Officers shall, whenever practical and reasonable, issue a verbal warning to the subject, and allow a reasonable amount of time for the subject to comply with the warning, before using OC spray (CC ¶191).
2) Officers will aim for the eyebrows/eyes of the subject.
3) Where OC spray is used on a person in a crowd, officers will direct the spray only at the person(s) who are displaying active resistance or presenting an imminent danger to the officer(s), others, or risk of harm to property (refer to SOP 12.6.5) (CC ¶190).
C) Prohibitions of OC Use
1) Officers are prohibited from using OC spray on a person who is handcuffed or restrained, unless that person is (CC ¶192):
a) Physically combative or violent; AND b) Presents an imminent threat to the safety of the officer(s), or others, OR to prevent escape.
2) OC spray will not be used on a subject in a police vehicle, unless that person (CC ¶193):
a) Presents an imminent threat of physical harm to the officer(s), themselves, or others, OR is attempting to materially damage the vehicle; AND b) Less intrusive means have been, or are likely to be, ineffective or increase the likelihood of harm to the officer, the subject, or another person.
3) OC spray will not be used to disperse crowds unless the objective risk of harm to officers, bystanders, or property outweighs the risk of harm to bystanders from the use of OC spray (CC ¶189).
D) Standards for the Use of Pepper Ball Launchers
1) Pepper ball launchers can be utilized for a dual purpose, both as a chemical agent dispersal system and as an impact weapon.
9.2.4 USE OF CHEMICAL AGENTS (CONTINUED)
2) When used as a chemical agent dispersal system, pepper ball launchers may be deployed where the use of OC spray would be authorized (see above).
a) Officers should direct munitions at the ground or another hard surface nearby.
3) When used as an impact weapon, pepper ball launchers may be utilized on subjects:
a) Who display active resistance; OR b) Present an imminent danger to officers, or others.
4) Unlike Special Impact Munitions Systems (SIMS) (e.g., 40mm launcher/sock round), the pepper ball launchers, when used as an impact weapon, should not cause death, even when striking prohibited areas.
5) The use of pepper balls as a chemical agent or impact weapon on a subject is a Level 2 reportable force, unless it meets the criteria of a Level 3 reportable force (refer to SOP 9.3).
E) Prohibitions of Pepper Ball Use
1) When used as a chemical dispersal system, officers should avoid aiming directly at subjects.
2) When used as an impact weapon, officers are NOT authorized to target the head, neck, spine, and groin, unless exigent circumstances exist.
F) Post-Use of Chemical Agents
1) Officers will render aid consistent with their training and experience, as soon as practicable, to include flushing affected areas (CC ¶195).
2) If an officer uses OC spray on a person in a police vehicle, they will allow air inside of the vehicle to circulate, such as leaving the doors or windows open (CC ¶194).
3) Officers will obtain an appropriate medical evaluation by EMS or a medical facility for subjects on whom OC spray has been used under the following circumstances (CC ¶195):
a) When the subject(s) complains of, or exhibits, continued effects after affected areas have been flushed; OR b) When they have informed officers that they have a pre-existing medical condition (e.g., asthma, emphysema, bronchitis, heart ailment) that may be aggravated by OC spray.
G) Decontamination
1) Areas of the body contaminated with chemical agents will be treated in a manner consistent with the manufacturer’s recommendations and departmental training, as soon as practical.
2) For any exposed mucous membranes, the officer will ensure decontamination is offered with fresh water and/or saline solution.
9.2.5 USE OF SPECIAL IMPACT MUNITIONS SYSTEMS (SIMS)
1) SIMS projectiles are designed to be used as direct impact less than lethal munitions. They are deployed utilizing the 40mm launcher or designated shotguns.
A) Standards for the Use of SIMS
1) The use of SIMS on a subject is a Level 2 reportable force.
2) The use of SIMS is authorized on subjects who present an imminent danger to the safety of the officers, or others, when the officer reasonably believes the use of SIMS may mitigate the imminent danger.
3) Lethal force backup should be in place as support, prior to the deployment of SIMS.
B) Prohibitions for the Use of SIMS
1) Due to the potential for SIMS projectiles to inflict serious injury, or death, officers shall avoid intentionally targeting the head, neck, spine, groin, or chest, unless deadly force is authorized.
2) Officers are prohibited from deploying sock rounds through intermediate barriers, such as glass, unless deadly force is authorized, due to the potential for serious injury or death.
C) Post-SIMS Deployment
1) Any time SIMS is used and the projectile makes contact with the subject, EMS will be contacted to evaluate the subject and transport them to the hospital, if necessary.
9.2.6 USE OF IMPACT WEAPONS
A) Standards for the Use of Impact Weapons
1) Only departmentally-approved impact weapons are authorized for officers to carry (refer to SOP Chapter 4).
2) Impact weapons are authorized as a means of:
a) Physical restraint or control; OR b) Defense of any person.
3) The use of impact weapons to strike is authorized on subjects who present imminent danger to the safety of the officers, or others, when the officer reasonably believes the use of the impact weapon will mitigate the imminent danger.
4) The use of an impact weapon to strike a subject is a Level 2 reportable force, unless it meets the criteria of a Level 3 reportable force (refer to SOP 9.3).
5) The initial, and each subsequent, use of an impact weapon to strike a subject must be objectively reasonable (CC ¶185).
9.2.6 USE OF IMPACT WEAPONS (CONTINUED)
B) Prohibitions for the Use of Impact Weapons
1) Because of the potential for serious injury, or death, officers shall avoid intentional strikes to the head, neck, throat, clavicle, spine, or kidney area with an impact weapon, of any sort, unless deadly force is justified (NOBLE).
2) Officers are prohibited from using impact weapons on a person who is handcuffed or restrained, unless that person is physically combative or violent AND presents an imminent threat to the safety of the officer(s), or others (CC ¶186).
9.2.7 USE OF CANINE
1) The Canine Unit provides highly-trained canine teams that can be deployed in situations to enhance officer effectiveness and the safety of officers and other persons alike.
2) The use of a canine in the direct apprehension of a subject constitutes a use of force and poses a risk of injury, so careful consideration must be given prior to making the decision to deploy.
a) Canine handlers and/or canine commanding officers will consider the circumstances surrounding a search, the safety of others, and the safety capabilities of the canine.
3) Any instance in which a canine is involved in the direct apprehension of a subject, regardless of whether a bite occurs, will be a reportable force (refer to SOP 9.3).
4) An unintended canine bite or injury, which is not related to an intentional canine deployment, is not reported as reportable force, but will be reported separately through an AIR (refer to SOP 3.1 and SOP 9.3).
A) Standards for the Use of Canines
1) The use of a canine must be objectively reasonable under the Fourth Amendment, based on the totality of circumstances and evaluated under the guidelines of Graham v. Connor (490 U.S. 386(1989)) (KACP 1.3a).
2) Canine handlers will notify their commanding officer of all deployments for the purpose of apprehension and, if feasible, prior to the deployment of the canine (CC ¶199).
3) Canines will only be deployed for direct apprehension in the following circumstances, when the subject being sought:
a) Has an arrest warrant for a violent felony or is wanted for fresh charges for the commission of a violent felony (pursuant to SOP 12.1.1) AND the subject is displaying active resistance (CC ¶196(a)); OR b) Has an arrest warrant for a felony or is wanted for fresh charges for the commission of a felony (unless the only felony charge is fleeing) (CC ¶196(b)); AND
o Has concealed themselves; AND o Has refused to surrender after warnings have been given; AND
9.2.7 USE OF CANINE (CONTINUED)
o A search of the premises would expose officers to a risk of injury.
4) Canines will only be deployed off-leash for the purpose of apprehension in the following situations (CC ¶197(a- b)):
a) The subject is suspected of having committed a violent felony AND the subject is displaying active resistance; OR b) The subject is reasonably suspected of having committed a felony; AND
o Is reasonably suspected of being armed, based upon individualized information specific to the subject; OR o Where the area to be searched is contained and reasonably secured by police with minimal risk of canine contact with an uninvolved individual.
5) In rare circumstances, and with prior approval of a canine commanding officer, a canine can be used on a lead to determine the direction of travel of non-felony criminal suspects.
a) In this circumstance, at no time will a canine be deployed to engage in the direct apprehension of any non-felony criminal suspect, unless the suspect becomes wanted for a felony and the criteria above is met.
B) Prohibitions of Canine Use
1) When it is reasonably believed that the subject is a juvenile, canine handlers will not deploy a canine for apprehension, unless the juvenile is wanted for a violent felony offense (pursuant to SOP 12.1.1) AND is displaying active resistance.
2) Canine handlers are prohibited from deploying a canine into an occupied vehicle, unless apprehension of the subject in the vehicle by other means poses a risk of injury to the officer, or others (CC ¶201).
3) When reasonably apparent, canine handlers will not deploy a canine to bite, or otherwise make contact with, a subject who is surrendering.
4) Canine teams will not be used for crowd control.
C) Canine Handler Verbal Warnings
1) Canine announcements are made to prevent innocent people from inadvertently being injured by the canine and to allow the suspect(s) an additional opportunity to surrender.
2) Prior to releasing a canine to search or make a direct apprehension, canine handlers will issue three (3) loud and clear verbal warnings that a canine will be deployed and advise the suspect to surrender, unless such warnings impose an imminent threat of danger to the canine handler, or other officers and persons on-scene (CC ¶200).
3) The canine handler will issue verbal warnings consisting of:
9.2.7 USE OF CANINE (CONTINUED)
a) Identification of authority (i.e., Louisville Metro Police Department). b) Directions to the subject (i.e., “Speak to me now,” “Come out,” etc.). c) Intention (i.e., “Police officer, come out or I will release my dog,” “When my dog finds you, he will bite you,” etc.). d) Result (i.e., dog will be released if directions are not followed, and the subject could be bitten).
4) Canine handlers will allow a reasonable amount of time between each warning to provide the subject an opportunity to surrender (CC ¶200).
5) Canine handlers will repeat the warnings during deployment as the canine and handler move into areas beyond earshot of the initial warnings (CC ¶200).
D) Canine Handler Guidelines
1) When safe and feasible, canine handlers will keep their canines within visual and auditory range during deployments, at all times, with the following exceptions (CC ¶198).
a) EXCEPTIONS include when a canine clears a threshold (e.g., rounding a corner, entering a room, ascending/descending a stairwell, or entering a confined space, such as a crawlspace) or when a person is escaping (CC ¶198).
2) In instances where a canine apprehends a person by biting, the canine handler will remove the canine as soon as it is safe to have the canine release the bite (CC ¶202).
3) If a canine fails to release on command, either through verbal command or physical out, the canine will not be deployed again for the apprehension of a person until it is evaluated for decommission or retraining, and it is retrained if that is the recommendation (CC ¶202).
a) The fact that a person struggles when seized or confronted by a canine, by itself, does not establish that a canine cannot safely release a bite (CC ¶202).
4) EMS will be contacted to respond to all incidents of canine bites, as soon as practicable. If the subject requires additional medical attention, they will be transported to a medical facility for treatment (CC ¶203).
9.2.8 REPORTING AND REVIEW
1) All officers must report a reportable force as required by SOP 9.3.
2) Members must notify an uninvolved commanding officer immediately, or as soon as practicable, following the reportable force.

sections.title: Use of Force Reporting and Review
sections.text:
9.3 USE OF FORCE REPORTING AND REVIEW (KACP 1.11a-c)
9.3.1 OVERVIEW
1) The LMPD categorizes force into four (4) levels with specific requirements for reporting, investigating, and reviewing a use of force incident to ensure a fair, thorough, and impartial assessment of officers’ actions (CC ¶176).
2) Officers are required to accurately, timely, and completely report on all levels of reportable force, used or observed (CC ¶159(i), 215).
3) All uses of reportable force require reporting when they exceed minimal force or injury results (CC ¶176).
4) The Chief of Police, or their designee, at their discretion may reassign the investigation and/or review of a reportable force at any level to another appropriate unit for investigation (CC ¶218).
9.3.2 REPORTABLE LEVELS OF FORCE
A) Level 1 Reportable Force
1) Level 1 reportable force includes when any of the following types of force are utilized, resulting in no obvious injury to, or complaint of injury by, the subject:
a) Pain compliance techniques, excluding control or escort techniques that are not reasonably expected to cause injury (CC ¶176(a)(i)); b) Pointing a firearm at a subject (CC ¶176(a)(ii)); c) Using the Conducted Electrical Weapon (CEW) warning alert (CC ¶176(a)(iii)); d) Forcible takedowns (CC ¶176(a)(iv)); e) Canine apprehension without a bite or physical contact between a canine and the subject; OR f) Deployment of the grappler, in which the grappler makes contact with an occupied vehicle.
2) Level 1 reportable force Administrative Incident Reports (AIRs) will be completed by the officer who was involved.
3) Commanding officers who review a Level 1 use of reportable force will hold a permanent-rank higher than any involved officer(s) who used or ordered that it be used (CC ¶218) (refer to SOP 9.4 on the investigative and review process).
4) If a lieutenant or above is involved, the review will be conducted by an uninvolved lieutenant or above (CC ¶218) (refer to SOP 9.4 on the investigative and review process).
B) Level 2 Reportable Force
1) Level 2 reportable force is any instance of force resulting in a physical injury, or complaint of injury, OR any instance when the following types of force are utilized, unless it rises to a Level 3 or 4 use of reportable force (CC ¶176(b)(i)):
9.3.2 REPORTABLE LEVELS OF FORCE (CONTINUED)
a) CEW activation (CC ¶176(b)(ii)); b) Use of Oleoresin Capsicum (OC) spray or other chemical agent (CC ¶176(b)(iii)); c) Weaponless defense techniques that include elbow or empty hand strikes, knee strikes, or kicks (CC ¶176(b)(iv)); d) Discharge of a Special Impact Munition System (SIMS) or similar less-lethal launcher/munition (i.e., pepper balls) (CC ¶176(b)(v)); e) Canine apprehension resulting in a bite or canine-inflicted injury (CC ¶176(b)(vi)); f) Strikes with an impact weapon (CC ¶176(b)(vii)); g) Intentional vehicle strikes of an occupied vehicle or a subject (CC ¶176(b)(viii)). Vehicle strikes during the application of the grappler will not be considered an intentional strike; OR h) Forcible takedowns of handcuffed subjects.
2) Level 2 reportable force AIRs will be completed by an uninvolved commanding officer and reviewed by an uninvolved lieutenant before submission to the Force Investigations Review Unit (FIRU), with a copy to the division major (CC ¶218, 204) (refer to SOP 9.5 on the investigative and review process).
3) If a lieutenant or above is involved, the Level 2 reportable force will be completed and reviewed by an uninvolved lieutenant or above (CC ¶218).
C) Level 3 Reportable Force
1) Level 3 reportable force is any of the following, unless it rises to a Level 4 use of reportable force:
a) Any use of force that results in the loss of consciousness or admittance for hospitalization of the subject (treatment in an emergency room (ER) does not constitute hospitalization) (CC ¶176(c)(i)); b) Use of deadly force that does not meet a Level 4 use of reportable force (CC ¶176(c)(ii)); c) The use of chokeholds or carotid/vascular restraints (CC ¶176(c)(iii)) (KACP 1.14); d) Any strikes with an impact weapon, including SIMS or similar less-lethal launcher/munition to the following sensitive areas: head, neck, sternum, spine, groin, or kidney area (CC ¶176(c)(iv)); e) Any kick to a person’s head or neck (CC ¶176(c)(v)); f) Any strike to a person’s throat (CC ¶176(c)(vi)); g) Any knee strike to a prone (lying flat on stomach) or supine (lying flat on back) person’s head, neck, or spine (CC ¶176(c)(vii)); OR h) Any application of more than three (3) standard CEW cycles to an individual during a single encounter, regardless of whether the applications are by the same, or different, officers.
2) Level 3 reportable force AIRs will be completed by an uninvolved, permanent-rank lieutenant and reviewed through a division major, or acting major, before submission to the FIRU (CC ¶218) (refer to SOP 9.5 on the investigative and review process).
3) The Public Integrity Unit (PIU) may be consulted on Level 3 reportable force incidents involving deadly force and may assume control of the investigation.
9.3.2 REPORTABLE LEVELS OF FORCE (CONTINUED)
D) Level 4 Reportable Force
1) Level 4 reportable force is any instance of force resulting in death or serious physical injury OR any instance when the following types of force are utilized, even if they don’t result in death or serious physical injury (CC ¶176(d)):
a) Discharge of a firearm at a subject. b) Any use of bladed/edged weapons on a subject.
2) Level 4 reportable force investigations will be conducted by the Public Integrity Unit (PIU), in accordance with the PIU Operations Manual (CC ¶267).
9.3.3 NOTIFICATION
A) Officer-Involved or Witnessing Officer
1) Any member who is involved in a use of reportable force, or witnesses a use of force, will verbally notify an uninvolved commanding officer immediately, or as soon as practicable, following the use of force (CC ¶214).
2) Only one (1) notification is required for a group of officers who are involved in the same reportable force incident.
3) If, for any reason, based on the level of reportable force, an uninvolved commanding officer of equal (lieutenants only) or higher rank is unavailable in the division of the occurrence, the involved officer or commanding officer will contact MetroSafe and have them check all channels for a commanding officer of appropriate rank for the level of reportable force to respond.
a) In situations where a commanding officer from another division is requested to respond and complete an AIR involving a reportable force incident, the AIR will be submitted for review to an uninvolved lieutenant or higher rank in the division of the primary involved officer.
B) Investigating Commanding Officers
1) For all Level 2 and 3 reportable force incidents, the investigating commanding officer will notify the division chain of command, via email, of the basic facts and circumstances of the incident prior to the end of the investigating commanding officer’s tour of duty in which the force occurred, absent extenuating circumstances (CC ¶214).
2) In addition, if an investigating commanding officer is unable to complete the AIR by the end of their tour of duty in which the force occurred, the investigating commanding officer will send an email to the “LMPD AIR Notification” email group (LMPDAIR@louisvilleky.gov) with the basic facts and circumstances of the incident, as known (refer to SOP 3.1.1).
9.3.4 CATEGORIZING THE LEVELS OF FORCE
1) Upon notification, the commanding officer will inquire about injuries and the nature of the force used to properly categorize the use of force.
2) If there is any doubt regarding a Level 1 use of reportable force, the commanding officer will respond to the scene to make the final determination.
3) When an incident involves multiple types of force or multiple officers, the entire incident will be reported and investigated at the highest level of force used by any officer during the incident (CC ¶222).
4) The chain of command who investigates or reviews use of force incidents may reclassify the level of reportable force, including to a higher level if applicable, that appears to have been inappropriately or improperly categorized based on facts during their investigation or review (CC ¶219).
5) Any recategorization will require the appropriate level of review and a determination, if initially categorized at a lower level, of why it was miscategorized, and if corrective action is required (CC ¶220). This will be documented within the AIR in the chain of command’s review.
9.3.5 REPORTING AND REVIEWING GUIDELINES
A) Articulation
1) Officers must articulate the justification for each use of force and are prohibited from using conclusory statements, boilerplate, or canned language (e.g., “furtive movement” or “fighting stance” or “characteristics of an armed person”), without supporting with incident-specific details in the use of force reporting (CC ¶223).
B) Use of Force Statement
1) Officers who are involved in a Level 1 use of reportable force will provide a use of force statement within the narrative of their AIR.
2) Every officer who uses Level 2 or Level 3 reportable force will submit a written Use of Force Statement form (LMPD #24-0001), which must be signed and forwarded to the investigating commanding officer by the end of the involved officer’s tour of duty, absent extenuating circumstances (CC ¶204, 237, 250).
3) The involved officer(s) will document within the use of force statement:
a) A detailed account of the incident from the officer’s perspective (CC ¶237(a), 250(a)); b) The reason for the initial police presence (CC ¶237(b), 250(b)); c) A specific description of the acts that led to the use of force (CC ¶237(c), 250(c)); d) The level of resistance encountered (CC ¶237(d), 250(d)); e) A description and articulation of every type of force used and the reason for the force (CC ¶237(e), 250(e)); AND f) Any injuries, or complaint of injuries, related to the use of force incident.
4) In addition to the above requirement, if the Level 2 or 3 reportable force involved a canine-inflicted injury, the involved canine handler will include the following in their use of force statement:
9.3.5 REPORTING AND REVIEWING GUIDELINES (CONTINUED)
a) Whether there was contact between the canine and the subject, including contact with the subject’s clothing (CC ¶204(a)); b) The approximate duration of the canine’s contact with the subject (CC ¶204(b)); AND c) The approximate distance of the canine from the handler at the time the canine made contact with the subject (CC ¶204(c)).
5) Officers who have authored and submitted a Use of Force Statement form (LMPD #24-0001) may not submit a supplemental statement.
6) The Use of Force Statement form (LMPD #24-0001) can be found on the LMPD Intranet by clicking on the “Electronic Forms” link.
C) Material Statements
1) Officers and commanding officers will be subject to corrective action, including discipline, as appropriate, if they submit a Use of Force Statement form or use of force report (AIR) with material omissions or inaccuracies (CC ¶224).
2) The appropriate commanding officer or investigative unit (PIU/PSU) will thoroughly review the entire incident, including the new information previously omitted or provided inaccurately to determine the facts of the incident and determine if the officers’ actions complied with policy (CC ¶226).
3) If, during the investigation or review, the material omissions or inaccuracies are found to be deliberate, the officer or commanding officer will be subject to corrective action, up to, and including, termination (CC ¶225).
4) Commanding officers and investigators (PIU/PSU) must promptly notify the chain of command if they determine that an officer’s statement reveals evidence of any potential serious misconduct in violation of law or LMPD policy and document their notification in the AIR or investigative case file (CC ¶221).
D) Concurrent Criminal Investigations
1) If a Level 2 or Level 3 reportable force incident overlaps with an active investigation of a violent felony, such that interviewing the witnesses and gathering evidence could jeopardize the criminal investigation of the suspect, the criminal investigation of the matter will take precedence over the reportable force administrative investigation.
2) In such event, a Level 2 or Level 3 reportable force investigation may be necessarily limited in-scope, as a matter of practicality.
3) The investigating commanding officer will coordinate with the lead investigating unit to obtain necessary interviews and collection/documentation of evidence.
9.3.6 DETERMINING THE REASONABLENESS OF FORCE (KACP 1.3a-c)
A) Graham v. Connor (490 U.S. 386 (1989))
1) Uses of force must comply with LMPD policy, to include being “objectively reasonable,” as required by the United States Constitution and federal law.
2) Graham v. Connor maintains that applying the Constitution’s Fourth Amendment to uses of force requires such force to be reasonable. Reasonableness is assessed with special attention to the following:
• The severity of the crime at issue;
• The immediacy of any threat to the safety of the officer, or others;
• Whether the subject is actively resisting; OR
• Whether the subject is attempting to evade arrest by flight.
3) Further, this assessment “must be judged from the perspective of a reasonable officer on the scene, rather than with the 20/20 vision of hindsight.”
B) Totality of Circumstances
1) When determining whether an officer has used reasonable force under the totality of circumstances, the facts and circumstances known, or reasonably should be known, by the officer that should be considered include, but are not limited to:
a) Whether the subject posed a threat of injury to themselves, the officer, or others, and the immediacy of the threat; b) The resistance of the individual who is being confronted by the officer and whether, and how, the subject fled; c) Prior knowledge of the subject’s violent tendencies or propensity to carry weapons; d) The officer’s and subject’s age, size, relative strength, skill level, injuries sustained, level of exhaustion or fatigue, and the number of officers versus subjects; e) The effects of drugs and alcohol; f) The subject’s mental state or capacity; g) Proximity to weapons or dangerous improvised weapons/devices; h) The degree to which the subject has been effectively restrained and their ability to resist, despite being restrained; i) The training and experience of the officer; j) The environment wherein the incident is occurring/presence of bystanders; AND/OR k) The risk of escape.
9.3.7 REVIEW OF BODY-WORN CAMERA FOOTAGE
1) Investigating commanding officers and reviewers shall review sufficient video footage to make an evidence- based determination as to whether the force was in compliance with LMPD policy.
9.3.7 REVIEW OF BODY-WORN CAMERA FOOTAGE (CONTINUED)
2) In conducting a use of force investigation and review, the commanding officer and reviewer shall, at a minimum, view all available Body-Worn Camera (BWC) video and/or third-party video, and document their review (CC ¶239(j); 254(i)) of the following:
a) The entire use of force incident, from the initial contact with the individual against whom the force was used up to the point at which the individual is in custody on-scene and finally secured in a police or emergency vehicle; b) Any interactions between involved officers and civilians, or other officers, preceding a use of force incident that provide information about the subject upon whom the force was used; AND c) The transition of the detainee from the police vehicle to the custody of jail personnel.
3) The commanding officer and reviewer shall utilize discretion to review video that is believed to be irrelevant to determine if the use of force complied with LMPD policy. This provision does not preclude the reviewer from looking at additional video footage of the incident.
4) Commanding officers will apply bookmarks to BWC footage that pertain to the use of force, any identified deficiencies with policy, supervision, tactics, and/or training, and any identified potential policy violations.
5) Commanding officers will bookmark investigative steps taken on Level 2 and Level 3 reportable force incidents.
9.3.8 FORCE INVESTIGATIONS REVIEW UNIT REVIEW
1) The FIRU will conduct an administrative assessment of all Level 2 and Level 3 reportable force incidents after the chain of command has completed its review, pursuant to SOP 1.14.7 (CC ¶216, 217).
2) The FIRU will review these incidents to assess whether:
a) The findings by the chain of command regarding the use of force are consistent with departmental policies and law and are supported by a preponderance of the evidence; b) The investigation was complete; AND c) There are tactical, equipment, or policy considerations to be addressed.
3) After completing the assessment, the FIRU will:
a) Return any reports recommending corrective action to the appropriate commanding officer within the chain of command; b) Determine if any action involved possible misconduct by any officer and notify the appropriate Bureau Commander for determination if a referral to the PIU or PSD is warranted for investigation; AND c) Document the findings of its review and any subsequent corrective actions recommended and taken.
9.3.9 REPORTS ON ASSAULTS AGAINST OFFICERS
1) All incidents of Assault 3rd Degree (KRS 508.025) on an LMPD officer require the involved officer to immediately notify a commanding officer.
9.3.9 REPORTS ON ASSAULTS AGAINST OFFICERS (CONTINUED)
2) Upon notification, the commanding officer will respond to the scene.
A) Criminal Investigation
1) The commanding officer will investigate the criminal incident and complete the Records Management System (RMS) incident report and the Kentucky Uniform Citation, listing themselves as the reporting and charging officer.
2) An on-duty detective may be requested by the commanding officer to respond and conduct the criminal investigation, completing the RMS incident report and the Kentucky Uniform Citation.
3) An assaulted officer should never be the reporting or charging officer in any case in which they are a victim.
4) The PIU may assume control of the investigation based on the criteria set forth in SOP 1.9.
B) Administrative Incident Report (AIR)
1) If the incident doesn’t involve reportable force, the commanding officer will complete an AIR as required by SOP 3.1.1.
2) If the incident includes a reportable use of force, an uninvolved commanding officer, based on the level of reportable force and rank of the involved officer, will respond to the scene and complete the appropriate AIR, adding “Assault 3” as a category.
3) AIRs will be completed, via the BlueTeam link, located on the LMPD Intranet (refer to SOP 3.1).

sections.title: Level 1 Reportable Force
sections.text:
9.4 LEVEL 1 REPORTABLE FORCE (KACP 1.11b)
9.4.1 LEVEL 1 USES OF REPORTABLE FORCE
A) General Requirements
1) Officers who are involved in a Level 1 reportable force incident will notify their commanding officer of the use of force, while on-scene (CC ¶214).
2) If the commanding officer confirms that the force falls within the Level 1 reportable force category, the officer will be responsible for completing an Administrative Incident Report (AIR), via the BlueTeam link, located on the Louisville Metro Police Department (LMPD) Intranet.
3) If a commanding officer is involved in the Level 1 reportable force incident (actively participates or orders), then the commanding officer will complete the AIR, and it will be reviewed by an uninvolved lieutenant.
4) The involved officer must specifically ask the subject, in which force was used, if there are any injuries.
5) If any physical injuries are indicated, the force is a Level 2 reportable force, or above, and the appropriate commanding officer, based on the rank of the involved officer, must respond to the scene and assume control of the investigation.
6) A commanding officer’s response to the scene of a Level 1 reportable force incident is not required, unless the officer’s Body-Worn Camera (BWC) did not capture the incident in its entirety (e.g., a failure to activate or the camera being displaced from their body). If this occurs, the commanding officer will respond to the scene to search for additional sources of video. This search will be documented in the AIR, and any obtained video will be attached within the BlueTeam entry.
B) AIR Narrative
1) The narrative of the AIR will contain, at a minimum:
a) A detailed account of the incident from the officer’s perspective (CC ¶228(a)); b) The reason for the initial police presence (CC ¶228(b)); c) A specific description of the acts that led to the use of force (CC ¶228(c)); d) The level of resistance encountered (CC ¶228(d)); e) A description and articulation of every type of force used (CC ¶228(e)); AND f) Any injuries, or complaint of injuries, related to the use of force incident.
C) AIR Attachments
1) Officers who are completing the AIR will attach:
a) Relevant BWC footage from all officers who used or observed the Level 1 use of reportable force (CC ¶229); b) Photos of involved officers and the subject, documenting injuries or a lack thereof; AND c) Any citations or relevant documentation.
9.4.1 LEVEL 1 USES OF REPORTABLE FORCE (CONTINUED)
D) AIR Submission
1) The AIR must be completed and forwarded to the appropriate uninvolved commanding officer of the division in which the incident occurred within 72 hours, or by the end of the next tour of duty, whichever is later (CC ¶229).
9.4.2 COMMAND ASSESSMENT/REVIEW OF LEVEL 1 USES OF REPORTABLE FORCE
A) Commanding Officer Assessment
1) An uninvolved commanding officer (typically a permanent rank sergeant) of an officer who uses a Level 1 reportable force will thoroughly review the AIR for consistency with LMPD policy (CC ¶230).
2) To ensure consistency with LMPD policy, this review will consist of:
a) Ensuring all required documentation, photos, and relevant BWC or third-party video has been attached to the AIR, via BlueTeam; b) Whether the use of force was properly categorized (CC ¶230); c) Ensuring that supplemental evidence or statements from witnessing officers, witnesses, or subjects are obtained when it appears that additional relevant and material evidence is necessary to resolve any discrepancies, provide missing information, or improve the reliability or credibility of the findings (CC ¶231). d) Whether the AIR was timely, thorough, and complete (CC ¶232); e) Making the necessary and appropriate findings of whether the use of force was consistent with LMPD policy and law (CC ¶232), including whether the force was objectively reasonable (refer to SOP 9.3.7); AND f) Initiating necessary corrective action (CC ¶231).
3) The review will be completed, absent extenuating circumstances, within 72 hours, or by the end of the next tour of duty, whichever is later, after receiving the involved officer’s AIR (CC ¶230).
4) The commanding officer who is completing the assessment will forward the AIR, via BlueTeam, to an uninvolved lieutenant for final review and determination (CC ¶234).
B) Command Review
1) The uninvolved lieutenant is responsible for ensuring the accuracy and completeness of the first review of the AIR, and for initiating necessary corrective action (CC ¶231).
2) The uninvolved lieutenant’s review will consist of:
a) Whether the findings of the assessment are consistent with law and LMPD policy, and supported by a preponderance of the evidence (CC ¶234(a)); b) Whether the assessment was timely, thorough, and complete (CC ¶232, 234(b)); AND c) Whether there are tactical, equipment, policy, or other opportunities for improvement (CC ¶234(c)).
3) If the lieutenant believes that the findings from the assessment are not supported by a preponderance of the evidence, they will consult with the commanding officer who completed the assessment about any
9.4.2 COMMAND ASSESSMENT/REVIEW OF LEVEL 1 USES OF REPORTABLE FORCE (CONTINUED)
recommended changes to the findings and document the request within the review section of the AIR (CC ¶233).
4) If the lieutenant identifies any potential violation of policy, they will forward the completed AIR with their review to the major, or acting major, for review (CC ¶235).
5) The major, or acting major, will review the incident and determine what, if any, corrective action is needed and whether there should be a referral to the Professional Standards Division (PSD) (CC ¶235).
6) The major, or acting major, will complete their review within 72 hours after receiving the incident, or before the end of their next tour of duty, whichever is later, absent extenuating circumstances (CC ¶235).
7) If the lieutenant does not identify any possible violation(s) of policy, they will submit their final review and approval of the AIR, via BlueTeam, to the Professional Standards Unit (PSU) (CC ¶236).
8) All chain of command reviews must be completed within 21 days of the incident, absent extenuating circumstances (CC ¶232).

sections.title: Level 2 and 3 Reportable Force
sections.text:
9.5 LEVEL 2 AND 3 REPORTABLE FORCE (KACP 1.11a-c)
9.5.1 LEVEL 2 AND 3 USES OF REPORTABLE FORCE
A) General Requirements
1) Any involved officer, or witnessing officer, to a Level 2 or Level 3 use of reportable force will immediately, or as soon as practicable, contact an uninvolved commanding officer to respond to the scene of the incident (CC ¶214, 238).
2) Every officer who uses a Level 2 or Level 3 reportable force will submit a written Use of Force Statement form (LMPD #24-0001), by the end of their tour of duty, absent extenuating circumstances (refer to SOP 9.3.5) (CC ¶204, 237, 250).
3) Level 2 reportable force incidents will primarily be investigated by an uninvolved commanding officer with the rank of sergeant or above.
4) Level 3 reportable force incidents will primarily be investigated by an uninvolved commanding officer with the rank of lieutenant or above.
9.5.2 COMMAND RESPONSE/INVESTIGATION OF LEVEL 2 AND 3 USES OF REPORTABLE FORCE
A) Level 2 and 3 Reportable Force Command Response
1) For a Level 2 or a Level 3 reportable force incident, an uninvolved commanding officer (sergeant or lieutenant) will respond to the scene and determine, based on policy and the facts then known, if the use of force meets the criteria of a Level 2 reportable force (CC ¶238, 251).
2) If the uninvolved sergeant determines, based on policy and the facts known, the criteria for a Level 3 reportable force is met, they will immediately notify an uninvolved lieutenant to respond to the scene and conduct the investigation (CC ¶252).
3) The uninvolved lieutenant will promptly respond to the scene and assume control of the Level 3 reportable force investigation (CC ¶253).
4) Prior to the arrival of the responding uninvolved lieutenant, the initial responding commanding officer will take steps to secure the scene and manage involved personnel until turning the scene over to the lieutenant to conduct the investigation (CC ¶251).
B) Level 2 and 3 Reportable Force Command Investigation
1) For Level 2 and Level 3 reportable force incidents, the appropriate uninvolved commanding officer, based on the level of reportable force, will assume control of the investigation and be responsible for:
a) Recording the entire on-scene investigation on their Body-Worn Camera (BWC); b) Ensuring medical treatment has been sought for any injuries to involved subjects or officers;
9.5.2 COMMAND RESPONSE/INVESTIGATION OF LEVEL 2 AND 3 USES OF REPORTABLE FORCE (CONTINUED)
c) Identifying and separating, when feasible, all subjects, involved officers, and witnesses, once the scene is secure (CC ¶239(a), 254(a)); d) Canvassing the area for any civilian witnesses. Commanding officers will record all interviews with civilian witnesses on their BWC and interview them separately, when feasible, and (CC ¶239(b), 254(b)):
o Notate identifying information for inclusion in the Administrative Incident Report (AIR); AND o Keep in mind that these statements are voluntary, and witnesses cannot be detained, or otherwise compelled, to speak to officers.
e) Requesting the subject’s statement regarding the use of reportable force. If a subject is free to leave, the commanding officer will advise them and will not extend the subject’s detention to facilitate the investigative process of the use of reportable force (CC ¶239(c), 254(c));
o Commanding officers should conduct direct questioning regarding the use of force actions and injuries, without asking about any criminal actions that may necessitate Miranda Warnings (refer to SOP 8.25).
f) Capturing interviews of the subject, or the subject’s refusal to be interviewed, on their BWC (CC ¶239(d), 254(d)); g) Conducting an in-person oral use of force statement, absent extenuating circumstances, while on-scene, but no later than the end of the investigating commanding officer’s tour of duty, from officers who used or observed force individually about the specific facts that led to the use of reportable force (CC ¶239(e,g), 254(e)). This interview will include (CC ¶254(e)):
o The reason for the initial police presence; o The level of resistance encountered; AND o A description of every type of force used or observed.
h) Refraining from asking officers, or other witnesses, leading questions that suggest legal justifications for the officers’ actions, where such questions are contrary to appropriate law enforcement techniques (CC ¶239(f), 254(f)); i) Using trauma-informed techniques, where appropriate (e.g., subject or witness interviews in the presence of involved officer(s), out of sight of involved officer(s)) (CC ¶239(h), 254(g)); j) Canvassing the area to collect relevant evidence, including available third-party video footage, that may have captured any part of the use of reportable force (CC ¶239(i), 254(h)):
o If no video is available or relevant, document the efforts to canvass for such video within the AIR (CC ¶239(i), 254(h)). o If multiple videos are available, document which videos were collected and why they were sufficient to capture the incident within the AIR (CC ¶239(i), 254(h)). o Keep in mind that privately-owned videos must be obtained voluntarily and cannot be seized, or otherwise compelled. o Should the media be unable to be uploaded to evidence.com, the commanding officer should contact the Video Forensics and Analysis Squad (VFAS) to arrange for assistance.
9.5.2 COMMAND RESPONSE/INVESTIGATION OF LEVEL 2 AND 3 USES OF REPORTABLE FORCE (CONTINUED)
k) Obtaining written Use of Force Statement forms from all involved officers by the end of their tour of duty (CC ¶204, 237, 250); l) Reviewing BWC, or other relevant video, which may have recorded all, or part, of the use of force, as soon as reasonably practicable, and document the review within the AIR (refer to SOP 9.3.7) (CC ¶239(j), 254(i)). m) Photographing the scene and items/objects pertinent to the investigation, including any departmental, governmental, or private property damaged as a result of an officer’s involvement (CC ¶239(k), 254(j)):
o Note that personal property/belongings may not be “seized” only for the purpose of an administrative investigation.
n) Photographing the officer for identification purposes and capture evidence of injuries, or claims of injury, and document the lack of injury, when applicable (CC ¶239(l), 254(k)):
o At a minimum, four (4) photos will be taken – two (2) stand-up photos (one (1) showing the front of the officer and one (1) showing the back) and one (1) photo each of the front and back of the hands. o Any injuries sustained by officers and/or any damage to equipment, uniforms, or property will be photographed.
o) Photographing the subject(s) for identification purposes and capture evidence of injuries, or claims of injury, and document the lack of injury, when applicable (CC ¶239(l), 254(k)):
o All efforts should be made to take at least two (2) stand-up photos (one (1) showing the front of the subject and (1) showing the back). o Photos will be taken of any injuries or areas where there is a complaint of injury.
9.5.3 COMMAND ASSESSMENT OF LEVEL 2 AND 3 USES OF REPORTABLE FORCE
A) Commanding Officer Assessment
1) The investigating commanding officer will include in the AIR, at a minimum:
a) A detailed, narrative description of the incident (CC ¶241(a), 255(a)); b) The force used by the officer(s) and the subject(s) (CC ¶241(a), 255(a)); c) Any injuries sustained by the subject(s) and officer(s) (CC ¶241(a), 255(a)); d) The sequence of events comprising the incident, with sufficient detail to provide a commander who reviews the report with a complete understanding of the incident (CC ¶241(a), 255(a)); e) Documentation of the investigating commanding officer’s actions in conducting the initial investigation (CC ¶241(b), 255(b)); f) Documentation of all evidence that was gathered, including physical evidence, photographs, and video footage (CC ¶241(c), 255(c)); g) The names, phone numbers, addresses, and recorded statements of the subject(s) of the use of force and any civilian witnesses to the incident (CC ¶241(c), 255(c)); h) Statements by involved and witnessing officer(s) (CC ¶241(c), 255(c)); AND i) Notation of any material inconsistencies in the evidence or witness statements (CC ¶241(d), 255(d)).
9.5.3 COMMAND ASSESSMENT OF LEVEL 2 AND 3 USES OF REPORTABLE FORCE (CONTINUED)
2) The investigating commanding officer will thoroughly assess the incident for consistency with law and LMPD policy (CC ¶240).
3) The investigating commanding officer will include in their assessment, a determination of whether each use of reportable force was objectively reasonable under the Fourth Amendment, to effect an arrest, a lawful detention, or protect the officer or other person, in accordance with Graham v. Connor (490 U.S. 386(1989)) (refer to SOP 9.3.6), and otherwise compliant with law and LMPD policy (CC ¶242, 256).
4) The investigating commanding officer will identify, if applicable, potential opportunities for improvement to relevant policy, training, equipment, or tactics. The investigating commanding officer will also ensure, where appropriate, that timely, constructive feedback is provided to the involved officer(s) and documented in the AIR (CC ¶243, 257).
5) The investigating commanding officer will complete the AIR and attach all relevant documentation, BWC footage, third-party video, photographs, officers’ written Use of Force Statement forms, extension request, and Conducted Electrical Weapon (CEW) audit trails to the BlueTeam entry as part of the AIR documentation.
B) Command Assessment Submission
1) The investigating commanding officer will complete the AIR within seven (7) calendar days of the incident, or before the end of their next tour of duty, whichever is later, absent extenuating circumstances (CC ¶240, 255).
a) EXTENSIONS: If additional time is needed (e.g., to obtain video, complete the narrative, conduct interviews, etc.), the division commander, or their designee, may approve a reasonable extension of time (CC ¶255), in writing (an email will suffice), that contains a detailed explanation as to why the extension is needed. This authorization must be subsequently attached to the BlueTeam entry as part of the AIR documentation.
2) The investigating commanding officer will forward the completed AIR, via BlueTeam, to an uninvolved lieutenant (or higher rank) of the officer(s) who used the reportable force, for final review and determination.
3) The investigating commanding officer will, by the end of their tour of duty, during which the force occurred, send an email notification to the division chain of command notifying them of the basic facts and circumstances of the incident, as known (CC ¶214).
4) If the investigating commanding officer is unable to complete the AIR by the end of their tour of duty, during which the force occurred, the investigating commanding officer will send an email to the “LMPD AIR Notification” email group (LMPDAIR@louisvilleky.gov) with the basic facts and circumstances of the incident, as known (refer to SOP 3.1.1).
a) The investigating commanding officer may carbon copy the division command staff on the email to the “LMPD AIR Notification” email group to suffice the notification requirement above.
9.5.4 COMMAND REVIEW OF LEVEL 2 AND 3 USES OF REPORTABLE FORCE
1) For a Level 2 reportable force incident, a lieutenant will typically be the last level of review within a division before an AIR is submitted to the Force Investigations Review Unit (FIRU) (CC ¶249).
2) For a Level 3 reportable force incident, a major will typically be the last level of review within a division before an AIR is submitted to the FIRU.
A) Command Review
1) When an uninvolved lieutenant conducts a Level 2 reportable force investigation due to a sergeant or lieutenant being involved in the use of force incident, an uninvolved lieutenant (or higher rank) will review the report prior to submission to the FIRU (CC ¶218).
2) When an uninvolved lieutenant conducts a Level 3 reportable force investigation, the lieutenant will submit the AIR to the division major, or acting major, who will review the AIR prior to submission to the FIRU (CC ¶258).
3) The lieutenant’s, major’s, or acting major’s review will evaluate whether the investigating commanding officer’s AIR was timely, thorough, accurate, and complete (CC ¶245, 246, 259, 260).
4) The lieutenant, major, or acting major will make the necessary and appropriate findings of whether the use of force was consistent with LMPD policy (CC ¶245, 259), to include initiating any corrective action (CC ¶246, 260).
5) During the lieutenant’s, major’s, or acting major’s review, they will return the AIR to the appropriate investigating commanding officer for correction, when it appears that additional relevant and material evidence is necessary to resolve any discrepancies, provide missing information, or improve the reliability or credibility of the findings (CC ¶246, 260).
6) If a reviewing lieutenant, major, or acting major believes the findings of the AIR are not supported by a preponderance of the evidence, they will consult with the investigating commanding officer, or previous reviewer(s), about recommended changes to the findings and will document all requests for changes within their review. Any commanding officer in the chain of command may discuss the findings with any reviewing commanding officer (CC ¶247, 261).
7) For a Level 2 reportable force, if the reviewing lieutenant identifies or is notified by the investigating commanding officer about any potential misconduct in their review or assessment, the AIR will be forwarded to the major, or acting major, in their chain of command, via BlueTeam, for review of the incident (CC ¶244). The major, or acting major, will determine what, if any, corrective action is needed and whether there should be a referral to the Professional Standards Division (PSD) (CC ¶248).
8) For a Level 3 reportable force, if the reviewing major, or acting major, identifies or is notified by the investigating Lieutenant about any potential misconduct in their review, the AIR will be forwarded to the appropriate Bureau Commander in their chain of command, via BlueTeam, for review of the incident. The Bureau Commander will determine what, if any, corrective action is needed and whether there should be a referral to the PSD (see below on the timeframe of review) (CC ¶262). The Bureau Commander will document their review, to include any corrective action initiated, within the AIR.
B) Command Submission
9.5.4 COMMAND REVIEW OF LEVEL 2 AND 3 USES OF REPORTABLE FORCE (CONTINUED)
1) The lieutenant’s review will be completed within seven (7) calendar days of receiving the report, or by the end of their next tour of duty, whichever is later, absent extenuating circumstances (CC ¶244).
2) For a Level 2 reportable force, if there is no potential misconduct identified, the lieutenant will forward the completed AIR, via BlueTeam, to the FIRU for review within 21 days of the use of force incident, absent extenuating circumstances (CC ¶215, 216).
3) For a Level 3 reportable force, or Level 2 reportable force with potential misconduct, the reviewing lieutenant will forward the completed AIR, via BlueTeam, to the division major, or acting major, for review.
4) If the AIR is forwarded to the major, or acting major, due to a Level 3 use of reportable force or potential misconduct, the major, or acting major, will complete their review within ten (10) days, absent extenuating circumstances (CC ¶259). If misconduct is identified, the major, or acting major, will immediately make a referral to the Public Integrity Unit (PIU) or Professional Standards Unit (PSU), as appropriate. Upon completion, the AIR will be forwarded, via BlueTeam, to the FIRU within 21 days of the use of force incident, absent extenuating circumstances, documenting their review and/or referral (CC ¶ 245, 248, 258).
5) Incidents that are forwarded to a Bureau Commander due to possible misconduct will be reviewed within ten (10) days of receiving the AIR, absent extenuating circumstances (CC ¶259). The Bureau Commander will document their review and/or referral within the AIR and forward, via BlueTeam, to the FIRU.

sections.title: Level 4 Reportable Force
sections.text:
9.6 LEVEL 4 REPORTABLE FORCE (KACP 1.11a-c, 1.12)
9.6.1 LEVEL 4 REPORTABLE FORCE INVESTIGATIONS
1) The purpose of this policy is to set forth the requirements for responding to, reporting, investigating, and reviewing Level 4 reportable force incidents, and/or in-custody deaths.
2) The Public Integrity Unit (PIU) will conduct a criminal investigation of all Level 4 reportable force incidents to ensure a fair, thorough, and impartial assessment of the officer’s actions.
3) The Professional Standards Unit (PSU) will conduct a concurrent administrative investigation of Level 4 reportable force incidents to ensure the officer’s actions were within the standards of LMPD policy (refer to SOP 9.6.9).
a) Only personnel within the PSU who have been specially-trained to conduct use of reportable force investigations and/or in-custody deaths will conduct these administrative investigations, and other uses of reportable force, as assigned to the PSU by the Chief of Police, or their designee (CC ¶271(a)).
4) The assigned PIU and PSU investigators will have the appropriate expertise, independence, and investigative skills to (CC ¶270, 274):
a) Identify whether uses of reportable force were consistent, or contrary, to law and/or policy; AND b) Identify policy, training, equipment, or tactics related to the use of reportable force.
9.6.2 OFFICER RESPONSIBILITIES
1) For all use of force incidents, when reasonably safe to do so and based on the security of the scene, officers will immediately render aid to the injured subject, consistent with their training and experience, until Emergency Medical Services (EMS) responds to the scene (CC ¶174).
2) Officers who used, or observed, a Level 4 reportable force will immediately notify MetroSafe, via radio, and request an uninvolved commanding officer to respond to the scene (CC ¶264).
