3) Involved and witness officers will remain on-scene until the PIU assumes command of the scene. If safety concerns arise, or the removal of the officers will help de-escalate the incident, officers may be transported to another location with the approval of the PIU. This action will be documented in the Administrative Incident Report (AIR).
9.6.3 RESPONDING COMMAND RESPONSIBILITIES
1) An uninvolved commanding officer will:
a) Respond to the scene of the Level 4 reportable force incident, and/or in-custody death, to assume control of the scene and manage involved personnel as the Incident Commander (IC) until turning the scene over to a higher-ranking commanding officer or arriving PIU personnel (CC ¶264, 266); b) Immediately notify, through the chain of command, the PIU (CC ¶265);
9.6.3 RESPONDING COMMAND RESPONSIBILITIES (CONTINUED)
c) Take initial steps to secure and maintain the integrity of the scene, which will be left intact to be processed by the PIU (CC ¶264, 266);
o If the situation dictates, request additional units to help secure the scene.
d) Request medical resources for any injured officer or the subject, if this has not already been done; e) Make reasonable attempts to identify and separate involved and witness officers, along with civilian witnesses who are on-scene, and keeping them on the scene until PIU personnel arrive, absent extenuating circumstances (CC ¶266);
o Escort officers should be assigned to involved and witness officers until members of the Peer Support Team (PST) arrive on-scene.
f) If applicable, obtain a public safety statement from any officer who discharged their firearm (refer to SOP 9.6.4);
o The responding commanding officer or IC will not conduct a comprehensive interview of the involved officer(s). Comprehensive interviews will only be conducted by the PIU and/or PSU.
g) If appropriate, designate a command post area, response staging area, and a media staging area (contact the Public Information Officer for coordination of a media staging area); AND h) Ensure the continual security of the scene and separation of the involved officers and witnesses until relieved by the PIU or through the Incident Command System (ICS).
2) An on-scene commanding officer will not seize an able-bodied officer’s firearm. All firearms used during the incident will be maintained by the involved officer and will accompany them to the PIU office.
a) If feasible, attempts will be made by the commanding officer, or a designated uninvolved officer, to secure an involved officer’s firearm(s) at the scene if the involved officer was injured and transported to a medical facility.
3) Upon relief by the PIU or through the ICS, the IC will be reassigned as the scene’s perimeter security detail commander and continually evaluate the needs of the personnel who are assigned to the incident, unless given other directions by the relieving IC.
4) The initial responding commanding officer, in the chain of command of the involved officer, will complete a shell AIR, via BlueTeam, for a Level 4 reportable force incident and firearm discharge, if applicable (refer to SOP 3.1.1 and the BlueTeam Instruction Manual). The commanding officer will document in the AIR:
a) The involved officer(s) and witnessing officer(s) response; b) The response and actions taken at the scene by the responding commanding officer; c) If applicable, memorialization of public safety statement(s) obtained; AND d) If applicable, coordination of involved and/or witnessing officers’ removal from the scene prior to the PIU’s arrival.
5) The Level 4 reportable force and firearm discharge AIR will be forwarded, via BlueTeam, through the division chain of command, up to the major. The major will review the AIR for accuracy and forward it to the PSU, via BlueTeam, within 21 days of the incident.
9.6.4 PUBLIC SAFETY STATEMENT
1) The strict purpose of a public safety statement is to gather time-sensitive information to determine existing threats to public safety and identify transitory evidence that needs to be preserved.
2) An involved officer will provide, as soon as possible after the scene is stable, a public safety statement to an uninvolved commanding officer when an officer has been involved in an officer-involved shooting (OIS), where they have discharged their firearm (CC ¶268).
3) The statement is compelled, without representation, and must be handled by an uninvolved commanding officer, barring exigent circumstances.
4) The commanding officer will capture the public safety statement on their Body-Worn Camera (BWC) (CC ¶ 268).
5) Due to the compulsion of the statement, the uninvolved commanding officer will clearly state that it is an order for the involved officer(s) to answer the questions of an exigent nature.
6) These compelled questions include, but are not limited to:
a) Did you fire your weapons? In what direction? (CC ¶268(a)); b) If not already known, is anyone injured? Where are they? Has medical aid been rendered and EMS been requested? (CC ¶ 268(c, e)); c) What is the description of non-apprehended suspects, their direction of travel, and time elapsed since last seen? (CC ¶268(d)); d) What weapons are the suspects armed with? (CC ¶268(d)); e) Did the suspect(s) fire a weapon? In what direction? (CC ¶268(a)); f) Are you aware of weapons or evidence that still needs to be secured? Where? (CC ¶268(b, f)); AND g) Are you aware of any witnesses? Where are they? (CC ¶268(e)).
7) Every officer-involved incident is unique and there may be other appropriate and necessary questions not listed above that need to be asked to ensure officer and public safety and assist in apprehending outstanding suspects (CC ¶268(g)).
8) Upon completion of the public safety statement(s), the officer(s) will be advised:
a) Not to discuss this incident with anyone, including commanding officers, with the exception of the officer’s legal representation (CC ¶276(e)); AND b) Power down their BWC and await instructions from the PIU.
9) If applicable, the uninvolved commanding officerwill broadcast pertinent suspect/threat information obtained from the public safety statement to MetroSafe, via radio.
9.6.5 PUBLIC INTEGRITY UNIT RESPONSIBILITIES
1) The PIU will be responsible for responding to the scene of all incidents involving a Level 4 use of reportable force, and/or in-custody death, and conducting a criminal investigation involving the officer(s)’ and/or the suspect(s)’ criminal actions, or as ordered by the Chief of Police, or their designee (CC ¶267, 271(b)).
9.6.5 PUBLIC INTEGRITY UNIT RESPONSIBILITIES (CONTINUED)
2) The product of the investigation may result in the criminal prosecution of the officer(s), as well as the suspect(s).
3) The PIU will be called out for the following incidents involving Level 4 uses of reportable force and/or in- custody deaths:
a) Officer-involved use of reportable force actions resulting in death or serious physical injury; b) All incidents involving the discharge of a firearm by an officer during a police action, regardless of injuries. This excludes the discharge of firearms for target practice or the discharge at animals; AND c) All incidents resulting in the death or serious physical injury to persons while in the custody of the Louisville Metro Police Department (LMPD).
4) The PIU Commander, or their designee, will be available, at all times, to evaluate potential referrals from commanding officers (CC ¶273).
9.6.6 PUBLIC INTEGRITY UNIT COMMAND RESPONSIBILITY
1) The PIU Commander will respond to the scene of all Level 4 reportable force incidents, and/or in-custody deaths, and lead all investigative activity, to include:
a) Ensuring the ICS has been established and a post-incident command post has been established; b) Ensuring all injured person(s) have received medical attention; c) Ensuring the scene/evidence has been properly secured; d) Ensuring all notifications have been made; e) Ensuring all witnesses and involved officers have been identified and separated; f) Facilitating the download of any data available from BWCs; g) Ensuring all involved and witness officers are transported to the PIU office; h) Ensuring PIU investigators conduct a canvass of the area to identify witnesses and other evidence that may exist; i) Ensuring arrangements have been made to have the Crime Scene Unit (CSU) process the scene; AND j) Reviewing and approving all search warrants prior to their execution.
9.6.7 PUBLIC INTEGRITY UNIT INVESTIGATORY RESPONSIBILITY
1) The PIU will conduct all investigations in a thorough, unbiased manner, in accordance with the PIU Operations Manual.
2) PIU investigators will immediately notify the PIU Commander of any recusal issues prior to being assigned an investigation or immediately upon identification of a recusal issue (refer to SOP 5.1.50).
3) The PIU’s investigatory responsibilities include:
a) Responding to the scene (CC ¶267); b) Upon arrival, assuming control of the reportable force investigation (CC ¶276(a)); c) Ensuring all injured parties receive medical attention; d) Identifying involved officers and witnesses of the incident;
9.6.7 PUBLIC INTEGRITY UNIT INVESTIGATORY RESPONSIBILITY (CONTINUED)
e) Separating all involved and witness officers until all officers are interviewed (CC ¶276(d)); f) Ordering all involved and witness officers to not discuss the incident with anyone, other than legal counsel, prior to being interviewed (CC ¶276(e)); g) Recording (with audio and/or video) all interviews with involved and witness officers, as soon as practical (CC ¶276(c));
o If an officer affirmatively refuses to give a voluntary interview, and there is probable cause to believe the officer has committed a crime, PIU personnel will consult with the appropriate prosecuting agency, and seek approval from the Chief of Police, or their designee, before taking a PSU compelled statement from the involved officer as part of an administrative investigation (CC ¶276(j)).
h) Recording all interviews with civilian witnesses, unless the civilian witnesses refuse to be recorded (CC ¶276(b)); i) Recording (with audio and/or video) an interview of the subject(s) on which the Level 4 use of reportable force was used to obtain their account of what happened, if possible and/or practicable (CC ¶276(i)); j) Ensuring no leading questions are asked during interviews that suggest a justification of the officer’s action or that otherwise are contrary to sound investigative techniques (CC ¶593(a)); k) Arranging with PSU investigators for any officer who discharged their firearm to be drug and alcohol tested, absent extenuating circumstances (CC ¶276(m)); l) Ensuring a canvass of the area is conducted in order to identify witnesses; m) Ensuring the scene is processed and all evidence related to the reportable force incident is collected; n) Arranging for the CSU to process the scene and provide any relevant work product (e.g., photos of the scene and involved individuals) to the PIU, as soon as practicable (CC ¶276(h)); o) Ensuring all available video evidence is gathered (e.g., private or public video, cell phone video footage, BWC footage, etc.) (CC ¶276(f));
o PIU personnel will arrange a canvass for any publicly or privately-owned video that may have captured the incident and attempt to obtain copies voluntarily (CC ¶276(f)). o If the owner of the privately-owned video refuses, PIU personnel will document the location and/or owner of the video (CC ¶276(f)). o If no privately-owned video was discovered, PIU personnel will document none was found (CC ¶276(f)).
p) Reviewing BWC or other video footage which may have recorded all, or part, of the use of reportable force and document the review of the video (CC ¶276(g));
o PIU personnel will obtain copies of all relevant video and include them in the electronic investigative case file to review, as soon as reasonably practicable (CC ¶276(g)).
q) Ensuring that involved officers do not review any BWC recordings related to the incident prior to being interviewed by the PIU or before the recordings are released to the public (CC ¶276(k)); r) Documenting all requests and decisions to hold in abeyance any aspect of an administrative investigation (CC ¶276(l)); s) Compiling all evidence and attempting to resolve any material inconsistencies; t) Presenting the investigative case file to the PIU Commander, once completed; u) Presenting the investigative case file to the Commonwealth Attorney’s Office, or other appropriate prosecutor, for review and/or prosecution;
9.6.7 PUBLIC INTEGRITY UNIT INVESTIGATORY RESPONSIBILITY (CONTINUED)
v) Submitting a summary of the investigation, in memorandum form, to the PIU Commander and including the memorandum in the investigative case file at the completion of the investigation; AND w) Attending briefings/meetings pertaining to assigned PIU investigations at the direction of the Chief of Police, Deputy Chief of Police, Special Investigations Division (SID) Commander, and/or the PIU Commander.
9.6.8 PUBLIC INTEGRITY UNIT CASE REVIEW
1) The PIU Commander will review every Level 4 reportable force investigation prior to presentation to the Commonwealth Attorney’s Office, or other appropriate prosecutor.
2) The PIU Commander will ensure each investigation is complete and thoroughly investigated.
3) Upon final disposition of the investigation, the PIU Commander will review the investigation before closure.
4) The Chief of Police will determine if closed investigations need to be reviewed by external agencies.
9.6.9 PROFESSIONAL STANDARDS UNIT INVESTIGATION
A) General Overview
1) The PSU is the LMPD’s primary administrative investigating entity of Level 4 reportable force incidents, and in-custody deaths, and will provide a thorough review of the actions of officers for consistency with LMPD policy (CC ¶269).
a) The PSU may call upon other units to assist or provide technical expertise during an administrative investigation (CC ¶269).
2) The PSU Commander, or their designee, will be available, at all times, to evaluate potential referrals from commanding officers (CC ¶273).
3) The PSU will conduct administrative investigations of all Level 4 reportable force incidents, and in-custody deaths, concurrently with any PIU criminal investigation into the same incident, absent specific circumstances that would jeopardize the criminal investigation and upon approval by the Chief of Police, or their designee (CC ¶272).
a) PIU and PSU investigations need not be initiated on the same day to be considered concurrent (CC ¶272). b) PIU and PSU investigators may coordinate their investigative steps to advance the purposes of the concurrent investigations (CC ¶272).
B) Investigative Requirements
1) The PSU investigation will be an administrative investigation evaluating the initial response, the incident, and post-incident actions of involved officers to determine violations of LMPD policy (CC ¶269).
9.6.9 PROFESSIONAL STANDARDS UNIT INVESTIGATION (CONTINUED)
2) The PSU investigator will lead all investigative activity related to the administrative investigation, which includes (CC ¶269):
a) Observing or reviewing interviews conducted by the PIU; b) Conducting follow-up interviews; AND c) Supplementing the investigation, which may include locating and interviewing additional witnesses and locating additional video that may have captured the incident.
3) The administrative investigation will be completed within 180 days from initiation (CC ¶277, 581), absent any extenuating circumstances covered in the collective bargaining agreement (CBA) (refer to the CBA between Louisville/Jefferson County Metro Government and the River City Fraternal Order of Police (FOP) Lodge #614).
a) All extenuating circumstances will be documented within the administrative investigation case file.
4) At the conclusion of each Level 4 reportable force, and/or in-custody death, administrative investigation, the PSU investigator will prepare an investigative report (CC ¶ 277), which will include the following:
a) A narrative description of the incident, including a precise description of the evidence, to determine if the officer’s conduct complied with policy (CC ¶277(a)); b) Documentation of all evidence that was gathered, including names, phone numbers, and addresses of witnesses to the reportable force incident (CC ¶277(b));
o If there are no known witnesses, or witnesses who refused to be interviewed or are unable to be identified, the report will state this fact (CC ¶277(b)).
c) The names of all LMPD members who witnessed any part of the use of reportable force (CC ¶277(c)); d) An evaluation of the basis for the use of reportable force, based on the independent review of the evidence gathered, including the PSU’s recommendation regarding whether the involved officer’s actions appear to comply with policy (CC ¶277(d)); AND e) If the involved officer used a weapon, documentation of the officer’s qualification and training for the weapon, if applicable (CC ¶277(e)).
5) The PSU will maintain their administrative investigation case files in a centrally-located database (CC ¶279).

sections.title: Enforcement
sections.text:
10.1 ENFORCEMENT
10.1.1 DEFINITIONS
Arrest/Bench Warrant: A written order issued by a judge or other proper authority for a law enforcement officer to place a person under arrest.
Criminal Citation: A Kentucky Uniform Citation that is issued to a person for criminal charges based upon a criminal summons or, with probable cause, on open criminal charges.
Felony: An offense that is punishable by death or by confinement in a penitentiary, whether or not a fine or other penalty may also be assessed (Kentucky Revised Statute (KRS) 431.060).
Misdemeanor: An offense that is punishable by confinement, other than in a penitentiary, whether or not a fine or other penalty may also be assessed (KRS 431.060).
Physical Arrest: Taking a person into police custody based upon a warrant or, with probable cause, on open criminal charges in accordance with law and this policy.
Probable Cause: The level of evidence, held by a rational and objective observer, necessary to justify logically accusing a specific suspect of a particular crime, based upon reliable objective facts.
Reasonable Articulable Suspicion: A suspicion, based on specific, objective, articulable facts, taken together with the member’s training and experience, that a subject has committed, is committing, or is about to commit a crime.
Traffic Citation: A Kentucky Uniform Citation that is issued to a person for traffic charges.
Violation: An offense that is punishable by a fine or other penalty less than confinement in a jail or penitentiary (KRS 431.060).
10.1.2 JURISDICTION (KACP 1.6)
In general, KRS 431.005 and KRS 431.007 provides when a Louisville Metro Police Department (LMPD) officer may utilize arrest powers. Specifically, KRS 431.007 governs the LMPD’s arrest powers in another county. Both LMPD on-duty and off-duty officers have jurisdiction to arrest within the boundaries of Jefferson County.
Officers who enter Indiana in fresh pursuit of an individual in order to arrest them on grounds that they are believed to have committed a felony in Kentucky have the same authority to arrest, and hold such person in custody, as any law enforcement officer in Indiana. The arrested person will be turned over to the appropriate Indiana police department having jurisdiction and taken, without unnecessary delay, before a judge of the county in which the arrest is made. If the judge determines the arrest to be lawful, the person will be held for a reasonable time until an extradition warrant can be obtained. If the arrested person voluntarily signs an Indiana extradition waiver, the officer may return to Kentucky with the prisoner, without taking the prisoner before a judge in Indiana.
10.1.3 CITATIONS
An officer may issue verbal warnings or Kentucky Uniform Citations for violations committed in their presence.
When making an arrest or issuing a citation on open charges, without a warrant, the officer will specify the offense(s) being charged and enter a detailed statement of probable cause in the narrative section of the Kentucky Uniform Citation. The statement of probable cause must sufficiently describe the actions of the accused that the officer relied on to meet the elements of the offense(s). Merely re-stating the charges or making a reference to an incident report number is not sufficient for establishing probable cause or meeting the elements of the offense (refer to Kentucky Rules of Criminal Procedure [(RCr) 3.02(2)]). Victim/witness name(s) and address information will be entered in the appropriate blocks on the Kentucky Uniform Citation.
The failure to meet the elements of the offense and adequately describe the probable cause for the arrest or citation may result in the dismissal of the charges in court.
Pursuant to Jefferson County Attorney’s Office’s (JCAO’s) policies, an officer will not routinely write citations for small amounts (one (1) ounce or less) of marijuana or paraphernalia only used for marijuana use (refer to LMPD General Order #19-009).
KRS 431.015 specifies that an officer shall issue a citation instead of making a physical arrest for misdemeanors committed in their presence, except for the examples cited below, and offenses within the statutes covered by the following KRS chapters and KRS, where the option to issue a citation or make a physical arrest is at the discretion of the officer:
• KRS Chapter 508 (Assault and Related Offenses)
• KRS Chapter 510 (Sexual Offenses)
• KRS Chapter 527 (Offenses relating to Firearms and Weapons)
• KRS 189A.010 (Driving Under the Influence)
o Driving Under the Influence (DUI) of a motor vehicle, either committed in the officer’s presence or not committed in the officer’s presence with probable cause (the issuance of a citation, in lieu of a physical arrest, requires the approval of a commanding officer) (refer to SOP 7.12) (KACP 23.1d)
• KRS 511.050, Possession of burglar’s tools
• KRS 511.085, Domestic violence shelter trespass
• KRS 514.110, Receiving stolen property
• KRS 523.110, Giving police officer false identifying information
KRS 431.015 specifies that an officer may also make a physical arrest instead of issuing a citation for:
• Any misdemeanor committed in the officer’s presence in which the defendant poses a risk of danger to themselves or another person. The arrest citation narrative must contain specific language indicating how the arrestee posed the risk of danger.
• Any misdemeanor committed in the officer’s presence in which the defendant refuses to follow the officer’s reasonable instructions. The arrest citation narrative must contain specific language indicating how the defendant failed to follow the officer’s reasonable instructions.
10.1.3 CITATIONS (CONTINUED)
• Any violation or misdemeanor committed in the officer’s presence where there are reasonable grounds to believe that the defendant, if cited, will not appear in court at the designated time. The arrest citation narrative must contain specific language indicating why there are reasonable grounds to believe that the defendant will not appear in court.
An officer may also make a physical arrest instead of issuing a citation for certain misdemeanors and violations, some of which are included in the arrest authority conferred by KRS 431.015, including:
• Measurement/Weight violation of a motor truck, semi-truck, or trailer (KRS 189.223)
• Reckless/Careless driving (KRS 189.290)
• Failure to comply with a traffic officer’s signal (KRS 189.393)
• DUI of a non-motorized vehicle (KRS 189.520)
• Accident-related responsibilities (e.g., leaving the scene, failure to report) (KRS 189.580)
• DUI of a boat (KRS 235.240)
• Violating motor carrier regulations (federal or state) (KRS 281.600)
• Criminal Trespass 3rd Degree (KRS 511.080)
• Harassment (KRS 525.070) (KACP 30.4)
• The authority of an officer, in uniform, to arrest for all offenses during a declared emergency (KRS 39A.190)
• Violating motor vehicle and boating offenses (except for offenses that only carry a fine as punishment) (KRS 281.765)
• Shoplifting (KRS 433.236(3)) either committed in the officer’s presence or not committed in the officer’s presence with probable cause
• Cruelty, mistreatment, or torture of animals (KRS 436.605(2)) (refer to SOP 8.33)
• Violating the terms/conditions of probation, parole, or conditional release (KRS 533.050)
• The authority of Kentucky Department of Fish and Wildlife Resources (KDFWR) Conservation Officers and all other peace officers to arrest for violating any statute in KRS Chapter 235 (KRS 235.310)
• The authority of KDFWR Conservation Officers to arrest or cite persons hunting on private land without permission, at their discretion (KRS 150.092(3))
If in doubt about whether to issue a citation or make a physical arrest, officers should contact a commanding officer for guidance. During normal business hours, officers may also contact the JCAO.
When issuing a citation, officers will explain the following to the violator, prior to their release:
• The reason for the citation
• The date of court appearance
• The optional or mandatory nature of the court appearance
• The option of prepaying a fine or satisfying the citation without going to court
• The option of traffic school (if applicable) for the offense
Officers may not issue a citation for the following misdemeanors. Officers will make a physical arrest for:
10.1.3 CITATIONS (CONTINUED)
• Assault 4th Degree (Domestic Violence) (KRS 508.030) (KACP 30.1)
• Violating any order of protection (e.g., Emergency Protective Order (EPO), Domestic Violence Order (DVO), Interpersonal Protective Order (IPO), Foreign Protective Order (FPO), etc.) issued pursuant to KRS 403.715 to 403.785 or as defined in KRS 456.010
• Violating pretrial release conditions, imposed by the court, for offenses involving assault, sexual offenses, or violation of an order of protection
Officers must have the approval of a commanding officer before issuing a citation for a felony offense. The commanding officer who is granting this approval will notify the appropriate division/section/unit commander, as soon as practicable, and be able to articulate the reason why a citation was issued rather than making a physical arrest. For the purposes of this section of the policy only, an acting sergeant is not considered a commanding officer.
Members who are authorized to issue citations are responsible for the accountability for electronic or paper citations issued to them. All officers must sign the Citation Accountability Log (LMPD #06-0017) for all paper citations issued to them. Any voided paper citations must be turned in to the division/section/unit and logged on the Voided Citation Log (LMPD #06-0048) (KACP 22.4a). While individual members are responsible for citations issued to them, the Kentucky State Police (KSP) has the final authority for accountability for issued and voided eCitations. KRS 431.455 prohibits members from invalidating, or attempting to invalidate, destroying, or attempting to destroy, a uniform citation which has been lawfully issued.
Officers are required to complete a Citizen Stop Report in the Records Management System (RMS) for all self- initiated pedestrian investigative stops and self-initiated traffic stops, regardless if an arrest was made or citation was issued (refer to SOP 3.6, SOP 7.12, and SOP 8.8).
Officers who are utilizing the Kentucky Open Portal Solution (KYOPS) to issue a citation will not change the court date provided by the KYOPS unless the defendant needs an earlier court date due to safety concerns. Officers who are issuing handwritten citations will assign court dates six (6) weeks out, based on the court assignment calendar and Jefferson County Office of the Circuit Court Clerk (OCCC) guidelines, with the exception of juvenile citations. Juveniles are not assigned court dates at the time that citations are issued (refer to SOP 10.7 and SOP 10.8).
Officers will forward all original handwritten paper citations (traffic, criminal, and juvenile) to their commanding officer by the end of their tour of duty. If the officer is off-duty, the original citations must be forwarded by the end of their next tour of duty. Commanding officers, or their designees, are responsible for forwarding citations to the Data Resolution Unit (DRU) within seven (7) days of the issue date of the citation for court processing. Courts will not accept late citations. Any citations forwarded after seven (7) days require a memorandum from the officer to the Assistant Chief of Police/Administrative Bureau, explaining the reason for the delay. Copies of eCitations do not need to be forwarded.
10.1.4 ARRESTS WITHOUT A WARRANT (KACP 1.6)
An officer may make an arrest without a warrant under the following circumstances:
10.1.4 ARRESTS WITHOUT A WARRANT (CONTINUED)
• A felony committed in the officer’s presence or with probable cause to believe that a felony has been committed and that the person being arrested committed it.
• Any misdemeanor committed in the officer’s presence that meets the statutory guidelines allowing a physical arrest in lieu of a citation.
• A misdemeanor not committed in the officer’s presence, when probable cause exists to believe that a subject has committed:
o Theft by Unlawful Taking (TBUT) (Shoplifting) o Assault 4th Degree (Domestic Violence) (KRS 508.030) (KACP 30.1) o DUI of Intoxicants (the issuance of a citation, in lieu of a physical arrest, requires the approval of a commanding officer) (refer to SOP 7.12) (KACP 23.1d) o Violation of an EPO, DVO, IPO, or FPO o Violation of Pretrial Release Conditions
• A violation of Assault 4th Degree (KRS 508.030) on property that is owned or used by a hospital (including a parking lot or parking garage), which was not committed in the officer’s presence and the officer has probable cause to believe that the person being arrested committed it (KRS 431.005(1)(f)).
• A violation committed in the officer’s presence, involving:
o Criminal Trespass 3rd Degree o Harassment o Reckless Driving o Failure to Comply with a Traffic Officer Signal o Leaving the Scene of an Accident o DUI of Intoxicants/Non-Motor Vehicle
• A violation committed in the officer’s presence, if there are reasonable grounds to believe that the person being cited will not appear to answer the charge in court (KRS 431.015(2)).
When making an arrest or issuing a citation on open charges, without a warrant, the officer will enter a detailed statement of probable cause in the narrative section of the Kentucky Uniform Citation. The statement of probable cause must sufficiently describe the actions of the accused that the officer relied on to meet the elements of the offense(s). Merely re-stating the charges or making a reference to an incident report number is not sufficient for establishing probable cause (refer to Kentucky Rules of Criminal Procedure [(RCr) 3.02(2)]). Victim/witness name(s) and address information will be entered in the appropriate blocks on the Kentucky Uniform Citation.
Officers will not make any arrest based solely on the following:
• Information received from an anonymous source
• Reasonable articulable suspicion, not amounting to probable cause
The failure to meet the elements of the offense and adequately describe the probable cause for the arrest or citation may result in the dismissal of the charges in court.
10.1.5 ARRESTS WITH A WARRANT (KACP 1.6)
Only a sworn officer may make an arrest in obedience to a warrant issued by a court of competent jurisdiction within the Commonwealth of Kentucky, including another county’s valid arrest warrant(s).
When executing a warrant, an officer must be especially diligent in identifying the person who is to be arrested as the person who is named on the warrant. This is particularly important when the suspect claims not to be the person who is named. The officer will also determine if the warrant is valid on its face. The warrant will be verified through:
• The National Crime Information Center (NCIC) (KACP 26.3)
• The Law Information Network of Kentucky (LINK) (KACP 26.3)
• eWarrants
• Calling the county clerk of the originating jurisdiction (the full name, title, and phone number of the person who is verifying the warrant must be legibly written on the warrant or the citation if the officer does not have a copy of the warrant)
If an officer is in possession of a printed eWarrant with an unserved watermark, they will validate the warrant, at the time of service, in eWarrants. Any paper copies of warrants with an unserved watermark, that have been served, will be destroyed.
NCIC hits for wanted or Circuit Court warrants will be verified through the service channel prior to service.
When making an arrest in obedience to a valid warrant, the officer will list, at a minimum, the issuing court, the warrant number, and the offense(s) as listed on the warrant in the narrative section of the Kentucky Uniform Citation.
10.1.6 eWARRANTS/WANTED CHECK
eWarrants is a statewide database of all circuit and district court warrants and/or summonses issued in participating counties in the Commonwealth of Kentucky. Checking an individual in eWarrants does not eliminate the necessity of performing a LINK/NCIC warrant check for other statewide or nationwide offenses (KACP 26.3).
Outstanding warrants and summonses that are found in the eWarrants database are valid and no further verification is needed. The eWarrants system is only used for:
• Adult criminal complaints
• Arrest warrants and summonses resulting from adult criminal complaints
• Bench warrants
• EPO, DVO, IPO, and FPO notifications
The eWarrants system is NOT used for:
• 202A Petitions (refer to SOP 12.11)
• Juvenile petitions (refer to SOP 10.7)
10.1.6 eWARRANTS/WANTED CHECK (CONTINUED)
Prior to the service of Circuit Court warrants, officers will notify the NCIC Unit by phone or radio.
If an officer is serving a warrant originating from Jefferson County through eWarrants, it is considered verified and may be executed immediately. Officers will use their Mobile Data Terminal (MDT) or desktop computer to perform a records check through the LINK/NCIC and eWarrants of arrested subjects prior to booking. Officers may request that MetroSafe perform these records checks. Should outstanding charges be present on the subject, MetroSafe will attempt to verify and confirm with the entering agency any “hit” or outstanding warrant, except outstanding warrants and summonses found in eWarrants, which are valid and need no further verification. All verifications will be performed in accordance with current LINK/NCIC and eWarrants protocols (KACP 26.3).
Once the arrested individual has been delivered to the LMDC, the officer will enter the arrest information into eWarrants, print a copy of the warrant, and click the “SERVED” button. This can be done from the officer’s MDT or from one (1) of the computers located in the LMDC sally port.
Warrant service is prioritized based on the severity of the offense. Warrants involving violent crimes and felony offenses will be served first.
10.1.7 CRIMINAL SUMMONS
When an officer determines that an individual has an outstanding summons, they are not required to have the summons in their possession in order to serve it (refer to Kentucky Rules of Criminal Procedure [(RCr) 2.10]). In such cases, the officer may serve the summons by issuing a citation containing the following information:
• The charges, as listed on the summons
• The assigned court case number
• The date, time, and location where the subject has been ordered to appear
The officer who is serving the summons will check eWarrants to enter the summons as served, if appropriate.
If using an MDT or desktop computer, the officer will enter the service in eWarrants and print, sign, and turn in the summons with the citation. If an MDT or computer is unavailable, the officer will simply issue a paper citation. eWarrants will be updated as soon as possible, but no later than the end of the officer’s tour of duty.
10.1.8 EXECUTING AN ARREST (KACP 1.6)
An officer who is not in uniform will display their badge, identify themselves as a police officer, and communicate the reason for the arrest. If, during an arrest, identifying oneself as a police officer could unnecessarily increase the risk to the officer, or other parties, the announcement can be delayed until practical. An officer who is making an arrest in the field will advise MetroSafe that an arrest has occurred once the individual is safely in custody.
Should physical force be necessary in order to execute an arrest, an officer will use only that force which is reasonable to gain control of the subject (NOBLE) (refer to SOP 9.1). The use of physical force, other than a
10.1.8 EXECUTING AN ARREST (CONTINUED)
control hold, to effect an arrest requires the completion of an Administrative Incident Report (AIR), via the BlueTeam link, located on the LMPD Intranet (refer to SOP 3.1).
Officers who are needing to enter a home for the purpose of serving an arrest/bench warrant will complete a Risk Assessment Matrix Warrant Service form (LMPD #05-0016), whenever they have credible information that an arrest by normal means would prove dangerous to the officers who are involved (refer to SOP 8.1). Examples of credible information could include, but are not limited to, knowledge of weapons in the home and the suspect’s violent criminal history.
All completed matrices will be forwarded, through the appropriate chain of command, to the Support Bureau Commander or Patrol Bureau Commander. A copy of the completed matrix will be forwarded to the Special Weapons and Tactics (SWAT) Team Commander (KACP 19.6d).
Nothing in this section prohibits a commanding officer from consulting the SWAT Team Commander, even if the matrix requirements for a call-out are not met.
Officers are reminded that they may only enter a home for the purpose of serving an arrest/bench warrant under the following circumstances:
• The officers have consent to enter the home; or
• The officers have a warrant for a serious felony; and
• The officers have a reasonable belief that the person who is named on the warrant lives in the home; and
• The officers have a reasonable belief that the person who is named on the warrant is in the home at the time of service.
An arrest warrant does not justify entry into a third person’s home to search for the subject of an arrest warrant.
If it becomes apparent that there is no probable cause or valid warrant to support an arrest, the individual will be released and a commanding officer will be immediately notified. An AIR will be completed, via the BlueTeam link, located on the LMPD Intranet (refer to SOP 3.1).
10.1.9 TRANSACTIONS WITH PRISONERS
Members are prohibited from accepting, or buying, any article from any suspect, prisoner, or associate of any suspect or prisoner.
10.1.10 DOCUMENTATION (KACP 22.4a-b)
Officers will complete a Kentucky Uniform Citation when making a physical arrest of a subject. When making an arrest or issuing a citation on open charges, without a warrant, the officer will enter a detailed statement of probable cause in the narrative section of the Kentucky Uniform Citation. The statement of probable cause must sufficiently describe the actions of the accused that the officer relied on to meet the elements of the offense(s).
10.1.10 DOCUMENTATION (CONTINUED)
Merely restating the charges or making a reference to an incident report number is not sufficient for establishing probable cause (refer to Kentucky Rules of Criminal Procedure [(RCr) 3.02(2)]).
Victim/witness name(s) and address information will be entered in the appropriate blocks on the Kentucky Uniform Citation. The primary officer who is establishing probable cause for the arrest should be listed at the bottom of the citation (e.g., officer who is initiating arrest, investigating detective).
Assisting officers who were also responsible for establishing probable cause should be listed on the front of the citation, either in the Witness box or the Narrative box, with their rank, code number, and “LMPD” as the address. Division/section/unit or individual addresses should not be used.
All Kentucky Uniform Citations will be reviewed by the issuing officer’s immediate supervisor (KACP 4.4).
10.1.11 POSTHUMOUS CHARGES
Posthumous charges may be placed against an individual when an investigation reveals that a deceased person has committed a crime and such charges are necessary in order to clear the case. A clearance by exception may be used to clear a case where the identified perpetrator has died.
Posthumous charges must have prior approval of an Assistant Chief of Police. In all cases, probable cause must be shown that would be sufficient to charge the individual if they were still alive.
10.1.12 SUPERVISORY REVIEW
Commanding officers will review the paper citations and arrest slips of those officers under their direct supervision. The commanding officer will place their code number on the upper right hand corner of the citation, indicating that they have reviewed the citation. The citation review should include, but is not limited to, the following:
• Missing/incomplete personal information of the offender
• The Citizen Stop Report incident number (if applicable)
• The appropriate charges
• The arrest or citation date, time, and location
• The arrest or citation narrative, statement of probable cause, and elements of the crime
• The valid court date, time, and location
• The report number, if the citation or arrest is related to clearing a reported incident
• Language indicating how the defendant posed a risk of danger (if applicable) (refer to SOP 10.1.3)
• Language describing how the defendant failed to follow the officer’s reasonable instructions (if applicable) (refer to SOP 10.1.3)
• Language indicating why there are reasonable grounds to believe that the defendant will not appear in court (if applicable) (refer to SOP 10.1.3)
• Legible handwriting
10.1.13 IMMIGRATION ENFORCEMENT
Immigration enforcement is not a local law enforcement matter. It falls under the jurisdiction of the United States Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE). LMPD officers lack the jurisdiction to enforce federal immigration law. However, there are situations where ICE, or any other federal law enforcement agency, may request the assistance of the LMPD. In order for officers to only respond to situations in which they have legal authority to act, the following measures will be implemented when receiving a call for service to assist ICE, or any other federal law enforcement agency, with immigration-related matters:
• MetroSafe will obtain a contact phone number for the ICE, or any other federal law enforcement agency, employee who is requesting assistance.
• If a member receives a request directly from an ICE, or any other federal law enforcement agency, employee, they will immediately contact their commanding officer for guidance prior to providing any assistance.
• A commanding officer will contact the requesting ICE, or any other federal law enforcement agency, employee, using a recorded line transferred through MetroSafe, and determine if the situation is one in which the LMPD should be involved. Generally, if the situation involves a criminal or safety matter, the LMPD will respond, as the LMPD would respond for any other public safety agency.
• If it is determined that the LMPD will provide support in any way, a commanding officer will respond to the scene prior to any assistance being rendered.
• If there are reasonable grounds to believe that the individual may be armed, has a history of violence, or presents a danger to ICE, or any other federal law enforcement, agents, or to other members of the public, the LMPD may respond as backup only. LMPD members will assume non-contact positions, such as securing the perimeter or observational positions, unless a public safety situation occurs.
• Under no circumstances will an LMPD member be the primary contact on a civil or administrative immigration matter.
• LMPD members are prohibited from using Louisville Metro Government (LMG) resources for the purpose of determining an individual’s immigration or citizenship status; however, nothing in this policy prohibits LMPD members from sharing information gathered during the normal course of operations with other law enforcement agencies, including immigration authorities.
• In order for members of the LMPD to detain, arrest, or transport an individual, they must be wanted on a criminal warrant issued by a court or there must be underlying probable cause for Kentucky criminal charges.
• Validity of warrants will be verified by the commanding officer prior to a service attempt.
• LMPD members will not initiate contact with an individual for the sole purpose of assisting ICE, or any other federal law enforcement agency, in making contact. One (1) of the above criteria must be met prior to an attempt at making contact.
In emergency situations (e.g., 10-30/Officer in Distress), MetroSafe will immediately dispatch officers to the location and notify their commanding officer, who will immediately respond to the scene.
When an officer is requested to go to the ICE office to arrest a person who is wanted on outstanding criminal warrant(s) and transport them to the LMDC, MetroSafe will directly dispatch officers and notify their commanding officers.
10.1.13 IMMIGRATION ENFORCEMENT (CONTINUED)
ICE may issue civil detainers or administrative warrants for people who are believed to be in violation of United States immigration laws. Even when assisting ICE, or any other federal law enforcement agency, officers may not detain, arrest, or transport a person solely based on a civil immigration detainer or administrative warrant. The individual must have a criminal warrant issued by a court or underlying probable cause for Kentucky criminal charges in order to be detained, arrested, or transported by an LMPD officer.
Through routine patrol, officers may also encounter individuals with immigration warrants. To verify if an immigration warrant is civil, administrative, or criminal in nature, LMPD officers will have MetroSafe contact the ICE Law Enforcement Support Center at the phone number listed on the NCIC hit or by calling (802) 872-6050. The ICE Law Enforcement Support Center is available 24 hours a day, seven (7) days a week, and 365 days a year. If the immigration warrant is for a criminal violation and has been issued by a federal judge or magistrate, officers will honor this warrant and handle it in the same manner as any other criminal warrant.
A commanding officer will complete an Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) Assistance Form (LMPD #17-0004) at the conclusion of the contact, response, or phone call.

sections.title: Exemptions from Arrest
sections.text:
10.2 EXEMPTIONS FROM ARREST (KACP 1.6)
10.2.1 OVERVIEW
The Louisville Metro Police Department (LMPD) acknowledges certain individuals and circumstances are exempted from arrest under specific legal provisions.
10.2.2 EXEMPTIONS
The following certain individuals and circumstances are exemptions from arrest:
• Kentucky General Assembly members while going to, or returning from, any session of the house in which they belong (refer to Kentucky Revised Statute (KRS) 6.050). Exceptions include treason, felony, or breach or surety of the peace.
• Participants in Angel Initiative Programs while voluntarily seeking substance abuse treatment “shall not be placed under arrest” or “prosecuted for possession of any controlled substance or drug paraphernalia surrendered to the law enforcement agency” (refer to KRS 15.525). Exceptions include ineligible participants, which include person(s) with arrest warrants, person(s) under 18 years of age and do not have consent of a parent/guardian, or person(s) placing law enforcement or its representatives in reasonable apprehension of physical injury.
• Person(s) with gubernatorial pardons cannot be arrested for pardoned offenses and “any further legal proceedings concerning the pardoned conduct, including indictments” must be ceased (refer to Fletcher
v. Graham, 192 S.W.3d 350 (Ky. 2006)).
• Diplomatic agents and ambassadors of foreign nations are generally immune from arrest due to the principles of international law and treaty obligations, including the Vienna Convention of Diplomatic Relations (refer to Rivera-Reyes v. Commonwealth, 2006 WL 2986495 (Ky. 2006) (citing Gomez v. Commonwealth, 152 S.W.3d 238 (Ky. App. 2004) (holding “the Vienna Convention does not confer standing on an individual foreign national to assert a violation of the treaty in a domestic criminal case”)).
10.2.3 KENTUCKY NATIONAL GUARDSMEN OR ACTIVE MILITIA
Kentucky National Guards or Active Militia ordered into state active duty by the Governor are considered peace officers and granted immunities in state active duty, including they shall not be arrested, “except in case of felony, while going to, remaining at, or returning from a place where [they are] ordered for state active duty” (refer to KRS 38.480(2)).
10.2.4 DIPLOMATIC AGENTS AND AMBASSADORS OF FOREIGN NATIONS
Under international law, all accredited diplomatic agents and ambassadors of foreign nations are generally immune from being handcuffed, detained, or arrested. They may be detained only for the time necessary to confirm their diplomatic status and should be informed that the detention is only for identification purposes. Should an individual claim to have diplomatic immunity, the officer will contact their supervisor. The supervisor
10.2.4 DIPLOMATIC AGENTS AND AMBASSADORS OF FOREIGN NATIONS (CONTINUED)
will request that MetroSafe contact the United States Department of State to determine the subject’s status prior to taking any enforcement action.
A diplomatic agent or ambassador found to be driving under the influence (DUI) will be either:
• Transported to their local destination and their vehicle released to family members or friends after obtaining permission from the diplomatic agent or ambassador.
• Provided the use of a telephone to call a family member or friend.
• Released to family members or friends.
A citation may be issued for traffic law infractions. However, a diplomatic agent or ambassador cannot be forced to sign the citation.
An officer seeking to place charges on a subject claiming diplomatic immunity will notify their immediate supervisor. The supervisor will request that MetroSafe contact a representative from the United States Attorney’s Office for appropriate legal advice.
Correspondence and other property belonging to a foreign diplomat is more closely protected from search and seizure under international law. An officer will seek legal advice prior to search and seizure.

sections.title: Arrests of Injured/Sick
sections.text:
10.3 ARRESTS OF INJURED/SICK
10.3.1 TREATMENT
It is the policy of the Louisville Metro Police Department (LMPD) that any person who is injured as a result of police action or is injured prior to police arrival, and subsequently taken into custody, will be provided with appropriate first aid and/or medical treatment prior to being transported to the Louisville Metro Department of Corrections (LMDC). A commanding officer will be advised of the injuries, respond to the scene, photograph the injuries, and complete an Administrative Incident Report (AIR), via the BlueTeam link, located on the LMPD Intranet (refer to SOP 3.1) (KACP 17.4).
10.3.2 HOSPITAL ARRESTS (KACP 1.6)
No injured or ill person will be removed from a hospital, for the purpose of making an arrest, without the approval of the admitting or treating physician or, if they are unavailable, the hospital staff physician.
An officer who has a warrant for a subject in the hospital must first obtain permission from the treating physician before making contact with the subject. The physician should be advised of the situation and the charges for which the subject is wanted. A commanding officer may decide to either delay serving the warrant until the release of the subject from the hospital or serve the warrant on the hospitalized subject and provide an officer to guard the prisoner (KACP 17.4). This decision will be based on the seriousness of the charges, the physician’s opinion, and the degree of illness or injury of the subject. If the person is incapable of leaving the hospital at that particular time, arrangements may be made for the division/section/unit to be notified as to when the person may be able to leave on their own accord. At that time, a guard will be placed on the prisoner.
If an officer determines that a wanted person is a patient at University of Louisville Hospital, they may obtain a Law Enforcement/Correctional Discharge Notification Request form from hospital security. This form provides the hospital staff with information about charges and warrants and specifies who to contact. The hospital staff has agreed to notify the listed contact person two (2) hours prior to the patient’s discharge to facilitate the arrest. The hospital’s form is for patients who are admitted to University of Louisville Hospital, not emergency room (ER) patients.
10.3.3 PRISONER DETAILS
If a prisoner must be hospitalized and a guard posted, the following will apply:
• The patrol division that is making the arrest or assuming custody of a prisoner involving an off-duty arrest is responsible for guarding the prisoner during the first 72 hours of hospitalization.
• It is the responsibility of a commanding officer from the patrol division in which the arrest was made, with the approval from the division commander, to contact the Assistant Chief of Police/Patrol Bureau, or their designee, regarding the establishment of a prisoner detail, if it appears the detail will exceed the involved division’s 72-hour rotation.
• Once a prisoner detail is established, after the first 72-hour period, a rotation among the other divisions will begin. Each division will be responsible for guarding the prisoner for a 24-hour period.
10.3.3 PRISONER DETAILS (CONTINUED)
• If a prisoner is arrested by a specialty team or an investigative unit, the rotation of guards among the patrol divisions will begin immediately, starting with the division in which the arrest was made for the first 24-hour period. The commander of the team or unit that made the arrest has the responsibility of contacting the appropriate patrol division commanding officers to provide a guard. The team or unit commander will also contact the Assistant Chief of Police/Patrol Bureau, or their designee, regarding the establishment of the prisoner detail.
• Officers who are assigned to a prisoner detail will be aware that they are responsible for the prisoner. They will remain with the prisoner until they are relieved. For security reasons, officers will remain inside of the room, out of public view, at all times, and will not stand in the doorway or hallway. The only exceptions to this requirement are to allow an attorney/client visit, during which time the officer may stand immediately outside of the door, if requested by the attorney, the prisoner, or if the hospital staff determines that the prisoner has a contagious illness, at which time the officer will be seated immediately outside of the door and maintain visual contact with the prisoner.
• Officers who are on detail at University of Louisville Hospital are prohibited from remaining in an operating room (OR) suite during the surgical process. The officer will be seated outside of the surgical suite door in the OR hallway. For security reasons, the officer may follow the prisoner to the OR to verify that the final anesthesia is administered for the surgical procedure through a glass window.
• Officers who are on detail at University of Louisville Hospital and in need of a short break will request that the nursing staff contact hospital security. Hospital security may only relieve the officer for a short period of time.
• Prisoners will be handcuffed to the bed unless it interferes with medical treatment (KACP 1.5). If an officer believes that it is not practical to handcuff or shackle a prisoner, they will seek verbal approval from their commanding officer.
• Officers who are guarding prisoners will not use patient phones. If an officer needs to use a phone, they will request a phone through the nurse call system and its use is limited to ten (10) minutes.
• While performing a prisoner detail, officers will not use departmental or personal electronic devices (e.g., cameras, cell phones/smartphones, laptops, tablets, audio or video recorders, etc.) while accompanying a prisoner at the hospital, whether it be inside or outside of the prisoner’s room.
• Officers may not restrict or limit a prisoner’s use of a television.
• Generally, in-patient prisoners, regardless of whether in the emergency room (ER), intensive care unit (ICU), or in a private or semi-private unit, are not allowed to have visitors. Exceptions may only be made subject to the policies of the hospital and with the approval of the commander of the division/section/unit that placed the initial charges and hospital nursing staff. Exceptions may include, but are not limited to, the following:
o A prisoner has a critical injury, or terminal illness, and is near death. Visitation will be restricted to immediate family members (e.g., parent, sibling, child by blood/adoption/marriage, spouse/“significant other,” grandparent, grandchild, etc.). Only one (1) family member may visit at a time and no other family members will be allowed on the floor during the visit. Visits are limited to two (2) people per day for no more than 30 minutes each. o An attorney who represents the prisoner on the charges for which they are being incarcerated may visit, regardless of the condition of the patient. There is no time limit on the length of an attorney visit. o The investigating or arresting officer(s) who placed the initial charges may visit a prisoner, subject to any applicable legal restrictions.
10.3.3 PRISONER DETAILS (CONTINUED)
• All non-law enforcement visitors will be searched prior to being allowed to visit, using a handheld metal detector. The metal detector is kept in the University of Louisville Hospital Security Office and will be delivered to the unit, as needed, upon request by the officer. Visitors are prohibited from bringing anything into the prisoner’s room (e.g., coats, purses, gifts, packages, flowers, plants, balloons, etc.).
• Approval of all visits will be in compliance with the visitation policies of the hospital. In addition, if a visitor is disruptive or an officer has an articulable reason why the visitor is a security risk, the officer may terminate the visit.
• An officer who has a reason to restrict the phone usage of a prisoner must obtain the approval of a commanding officer. For the purpose of this policy, an acting sergeant is not considered a commanding officer.
10.3.4 INVOLUNTARY DETENTION
An officer who is responding to a suicide attempt should try to persuade the subject to agree to voluntary commitment or advise the subject’s family to seek involuntary commitment. If the situation is of an extreme nature and the officer has probable cause to believe that the subject is a danger to themselves, or others, the officer may arrest the subject without a warrant and transport them to University of Louisville Hospital.
10.3.5 DOCUMENTATION (KACP 30.8)
Officers who knowingly transport prisoners who have a history of serious mental or physical illness, or who display suicidal tendencies, will note such information on the Kentucky Uniform Citation. These conditions will only be noted if they serve a valid law enforcement purpose.

sections.title: Special Notifications
sections.text:
10.4 SPECIAL NOTIFICATIONS (KACP 1.6)
10.4.1 UNITED STATES POSTAL SERVICE MAIL CARRIERS
United States Postal Service (USPS) mail carriers are not exempt from arrest while on-duty. If an arrest is made, an officer will stay with the mail vehicle until a representative from the USPS arrives at the scene.
10.4.2 MILITARY DESERTERS
Officers are authorized to arrest subjects who are absent without leave (AWOL) from the armed services. Verification of the AWOL status must be made by either the National Crime Information Center (NCIC) Unit or the military police. Subjects charged with being AWOL will be booked as any other prisoner would be.
10.4.3 ON-DUTY FIREFIGHTERS
Unless extenuating circumstances exist, an officer will perform the following prior to arresting an on-duty firefighter:
• Notify MetroSafe to request that the on-duty Assistant Louisville Metro Fire Chief contact them at a particular telephone number. When a firefighter from an agency other than Louisville Metro Government (LMG) is to be arrested, a commanding officer from the affected fire district will be contacted.
• Update the Assistant Fire Chief, or commanding officer, of the situation, name, and location of the firefighter. The Assistant Fire Chief, or commanding officer, may make arrangements to provide a replacement firefighter for the person being arrested.
• Affect the arrest of the on-duty firefighter after their relief, if any, is in place.
10.4.4 SCHOOL PERSONNEL DURING SCHOOL HOURS
School administrators will be notified prior to any onsite arrest of employees during school hours. Unless unusual circumstances exist, officers should request that the employee report to the office to facilitate the arrest.
10.4.5 FOREIGN NATIONALS
Foreign National: Any person who is a citizen of any country other than the United States, including non- immigrant visitors, lawful permanent residents, and illegal aliens.
Officers will not inquire into the immigration or citizenship status of an individual, except where the inquiry relates to a specific criminal or homeland security investigation.
The United States is obligated and legally bound under international agreements and customary international law to notify consular officials when foreign nationals are detained or arrested, or when a foreign national is seriously injured or dies, in the United States.
Reviewed 11/26/24
10.4.5 FOREIGN NATIONALS (CONTINUED)
Consular officials will also be notified if a foreign aircraft crash/shipwreck occurs in the United States or the appointment of guardians for foreign nationals who are minors or incompetent adults. Upon knowingly detaining or arresting a foreign national, officers will:
• Determine the foreign national’s country of nationality.
• Immediately advise the foreign national of their right to consular notification.
• Immediately contact MetroSafe and inform them that they have has detained or arrested a foreign national, indicating the country to which the foreign national belongs. MetroSafe will advise the officer if the country is a mandatory or non-mandatory notification country. MetroSafe will also be responsible for notifying the Administrative Services Division Commander that the officer has detained or arrested a foreign national.
• Obtain a call for service/Computer Aided Dispatch (CAD) number from MetroSafe.
If the subject is from a mandatory notification country, the officer will inform them that the department is required to notify their consulate and they may communicate with them. If the subject is from a non-mandatory notification country, the officer will inform them of the right to have their government informed of the event, if they so desire, and they may communicate with them. The following must be documented:
• The date and time the foreign national was informed that they could communicate with consular officials and, if applicable, could request that consular officials be notified, without delay, of the detention or arrest. The foreign national’s signature and date will be obtained to verify they were advised of this and to accept or decline notification.
• Whether the foreign national requested notification, if applicable.
• Whether the consulate was notified and, if so, the date and time of notification, method of notification, and confirmation of receipt, if available.
If the subject has a dual nationality (citizen of two (2) separate countries), the consulates of both countries will be notified if notification is required or requested.
Officers who are detaining or arresting foreign nationals are required to contact the NCIC Unit and provide them with the following information, regardless of whether a consulate is to be notified:
• Officer name and code number
• Call for service (CAD) number
• Date and time of the detention or arrest
• Name, date of birth (DOB), and place of birth of the foreign national
• Passport number, with the date and place of issuance, if available
The NCIC Unit uses the information provided by the officer to complete a fax form. If notification is required or requested, the NCIC Unit will fax the form to the appropriate consulate. If notification is not mandatory or declined, the NCIC Unit will complete the fax form, indicating that notification was not mandatory or declined, and will not forward the form to the consulate. The NCIC Unit will be responsible for storing the forms and emailing a copy of each form to the Homeland Security Team Commander, regardless of whether notification was made or declined.
Reviewed 11/26/24
10.4.5 FOREIGN NATIONALS (CONTINUED)
A current list of telephone numbers for all foreign consulates as well as a current list of mandatory notification countries is kept on file at MetroSafe.
If the subject is from a non-mandatory notification country and they initially decline notification but later changes their mind, the appropriate consulate will then be notified.
The officer will record the time and date that the NCIC Unit was notified of the arrest on the Uniform Citation.
If a foreign national requests asylum, they will be referred to the United States Department of State.
10.4.6 LOUISVILLE METRO GOVERNMENT MEMBERS
Complaints against any LMG member involving the physical or sexual abuse of a minor will be immediately investigated by the Office of Sexual and Physical Investigations (OSPI) and immediately reported to the Public Integrity Unit (PIU) and the Kentucky Cabinet for Health and Family Services (CHFS).
The PIU will be immediately notified whenever an LMG member is suspected of committing a felony offense. The PIU will also be notified whenever an officer is arrested for any criminal offense. The PIU should be notified prior to the arrest, whenever possible.
Members who are summoned to any court, before any judge, concerning matters in which they, or other members, may become a defendant in a criminal prosecution must report the facts, in detail, to the Chief of Police, through the appropriate chain of command, as soon as practical.
Reviewed 11/26/24

sections.title: Care of Persons in Police Custody
sections.text:
10.5 CARE OF PERSONS IN POLICE CUSTODY
10.5.1 OVERVIEW
1) This policy establishes guidelines pertaining to the custody and care of detainees, including on-duty, off- duty, and secondary employment situations.
2) Officers should remember that the safety of the detainee, or other persons in their care, is their primary responsibility.
3) When transporting a detainee, the officer will not initiate, or assist in, a vehicular pursuit or other Code 3 response.
4) Only where the risk to third parties is both clear and grave, and the risk of escape or injury to the transported detainee is minimal, should an officer stop to render assistance or take other enforcement action (KACP 25.1).
10.5.2 SEARCH OF DETAINEES (KACP 1.7b)
A person who is under arrest will be thoroughly searched by each transporting officer.
10.5.3 INSPECTIONS OF TRANSPORTING VEHICLE (KACP 1.7c)
The detainee area of a transporting vehicle will be thoroughly searched for evidence and contraband before, and after, detainee transport and at the beginning, and end, of each tour of duty.
10.5.4 TRANSPORTATION EQUIPMENT
When transporting a detainee, transporting officers should ensure that:
a) The rear doors of all vehicles used to transport detainees are modified to prevent opening from the inside and the rear windows are modified to prevent opening from any place other than the driver’s seat. b) All marked vehicles used for detainee transport are equipped with a safety barrier separating the detainee from the officer, and that any conversation between the officer and detainee will not be impeded by the barrier. c) Police vehicles that are not equipped with a safety barrier may be utilized to transport a detainee based on the severity of the offense, the detainee’s demeanor, or the transporting officer’s discretion. d) Non-compliant detainees will not be transported in a vehicle without a safety barrier.
10.5.5 SEATING OF DETAINEES (KACP 21.4)
A) Vehicles Without Safety Barrier
1) In a vehicle without a safety barrier, a single officer will only transport one (1) detainee.
2) It is strongly encouraged to transport the detainee in the passenger-side front seat to maintain a better visual of the detainee, but they may be transported in the passenger-side rear seat.
3) Under no circumstances will a detainee be placed behind the driver while being transported without a safety barrier.
B) Vehicles With Safety Barrier
1) In vehicles equipped with a safety barrier, no more than three (3) detainees may be transported at one (1) time.
C) Safety Belt
1) Pursuant to KRS 189.125, any detainee who is being transported in a departmental vehicle shall be secured with a seatbelt.
2) If physical handicap or articulable officer safety issues prevent the proper use of a seatbelt, the officer will request their commanding officer’s assistance with arranging alternate transportation (e.g., booking van) (refer to SOP 10.5.12 for disabled detainees).
3) Detainees transported by the booking van will be secured with the installed lap bar and/or seatbelt.
10.5.6 DETAINEE OF OPPOSITE SEX
1) A female detainee and a male detainee will not occupy the same vehicle without a commanding officer’s approval. Refer to SOP 8.47.6 regarding transgender detainee transports.
2) When an officer transports a detainee of the opposite sex, they will notify MetroSafe of their beginning and ending odometer readings (refer to SOP 10.5.11) (KACP 1.7d-e).
10.5.7 JUVENILE DETAINEES
Juvenile detainees will not be transported in the same vehicle or in direct contact (sight or sound) with adult detainees (KRS 610.220).
10.5.8 DECONTAMINATION OF DETAINEES
1) Detainees who have come in contact with hazardous materials (HAZMAT) (e.g., HAZMAT incident, weapons of mass destruction (WMD), terrorist attack, clandestine laboratory) will be decontaminated by the responding HAZMAT or fire department personnel, prior to being placed in the vehicle.
2) Officers who are handling contaminated detainees will use flex cuffs and appropriate personal protective equipment (PPE) gear, when practical, to prevent cross contamination (refer to SOP 12.2).
3) Commanding officers will complete an Administrative Incident Report (AIR), on all contaminated detainees, outlining the type and nature of the exposure (refer to SOP 3.1), and contact a Health and Safety Officer (HSO) to respond to the scene.
4) The HSO and the responding HAZMAT or fire department personnel will make the determination as to whether the detainee requires additional treatment at a medical facility.
10.5.9 DETAINEE TRANSPORTED TO A MEDICAL FACILITY (KACP 1.7f, i)
1) Detainees who are transported to a medical facility by an officer, or by Emergency Medical Services (EMS), remain the officer’s responsibility. The officer will:
a) Keep the detainee in view, whenever possible. b) Accompany the detainee to the treatment room.
2) The type and degree of restraint utilized by the officer should be objectively reasonable, taking into consideration the detainees’ injuries and the safety of the officer and medical staff. However, detainees should not be completely unrestrained, unless directed by EMS or a physician, because of medical necessity (KACP 1.7a).
3) Upon completion of treatment, a medical clearance (i.e., discharge paperwork) signed by the physician needs to be obtained and presented to Louisville Metro Department of Corrections (LMDC) personnel.
10.5.10 DETAINEE ADMITTED TO A MEDICAL FACILITY (KACP 1.7f, i)
1) If a detainee who is transported to a medical facility by an officer, or EMS, is to be admitted for treatment, the officer will notify their commanding officer.
2) The officer will maintain a vigilant guard as near as possible to the detainee.
3) The officer should remain in the room with the detainee, if possible. If medical personnel advise the officer to leave the room, the officer will assume a position immediately outside of the door (refer to SOP 10.3).
4) The officer will not relinquish custody of their detainee until properly relieved by another officer.
10.5.11 TRANSPORTATION NOTIFICATION (KACP 1.7d-e)
1) When an officer transports a detainee, they will:
a) Inform MetroSafe, via police radio, of their intended destination (e.g., LMDC, medical facility, police facility) (KACP 1.7d). b) Provide MetroSafe, via police radio, with the current odometer reading (KACP 1.7d). c) Proceed directly to their intended destination without any intermediate stops. d) Notify MetroSafe, via police radio, of any delay en route (KACP 1.7d-e). e) Upon arrival at the intended destination, provide MetroSafe, via police radio, with their current odometer reading (KACP 1.7e).
2) MetroSafe tracks the beginning and ending transport times within the Computer Aided Dispatch (CAD) system (KACP 1.7 d-e).
10.5.12 TRANSPORTING DISABLED DETAINEES (KACP 1.7f)
1) If the nature of a detainee’s disability prevents the use of a vehicle equipped with a safety barrier for transportation, the officer will request their commanding officer’s assistance with arranging alternate transportation.
2) If a detainee has a physical disability which requires the use of a mobility device (e.g., wheelchair, cane, walker, leg braces, etc.), the mobility device will be transported with the detainee to the LMDC.
3) If a detainee is utilizing an electric wheelchair or scooter, and they should not be removed from the device for health reasons, officers will contact the LMDC to send a specialized van to transport the detainee and the device.
10.5.13 VISUAL OBSERVATION OF DETAINEE (KACP 1.7i)
1) In order to promote the security and safety of officers, detainees, and the public, an officer will maintain visual observation of their detainees.
2) Appropriate exceptions may be made to allow the detainee to use the restroom or to receive medical treatment.
3) In patrol divisions equipped with temporary detention rooms, a Temporary Detention Room Observation form (LMPD #09-0012) will be completed by the custodial officer whenever a detainee is placed in the temporary detention room.
4) The detainee’s name, if known will be recorded on the Temporary Detention Room Observation form, along with the date and time that the detainee was placed in the temporary detention room and the required information of the custodial officer.
10.5.13 VISUAL OBSERVATION OF DETAINEES (CONTINUED)
5) Officers who are responsible for the custody and care of the detainee will visually observe the detainee in the temporary detention room and check on their welfare at intervals not to exceed 30 minutes. Each observation is to be recorded on the form, to include the officer’s code number who conducted the welfare check.
6) The Temporary Detention Room Observation forms are maintained in close proximity to the temporary detention room and filed with the division commander upon final removal of the detainee from the temporary detention room.
7) Juvenile detainees will not be placed in a departmental temporary detention room with adults.
10.5.14 MEALS/RESTROOM
1) Under ordinary circumstances, the officer is not responsible for providing a detainee with a meal or multiple uses of a restroom that are unreasonable.
2) If the officer is escorting a detainee on a long trip (e.g., extraditions), meals and restroom stops should be taken at random times and locations for security reasons.
3) No detainee will be directly observed using the restroom unless an officer has reason to believe the observation would prevent harm to the officer or the detainee, or the opportunity exists for the destruction of evidence or contraband.
10.5.15 COMMUNICATIONS WITH OTHERS
1) Detainees who are under escort during long trips (e.g., extraditions) are not permitted unauthorized visitors or communications, without the approval of the division commander.
2) Refer to SOP 10.3 for detainees under hospital arrest.
10.5.16 RESTRAINING DEVICES (KACP 1.5, 1.7a)
A) Restraining Devices Overview
1) All persons will be restrained when taken into custody and remain restrained during all phases of transportation. Exceptions are permissible if the investigating officer has reason to believe a greater degree of cooperation may be achieved from the person by being unrestrained. When a detainee is not restrained, the officer should exercise extreme caution.
2) An individual may be restrained, even though they are not under arrest, if the officer is legally detaining the individual (e.g., status offenders, subjects who are present during search warrants) (refer to SOP 10.5.17).
10.5.16 RESTRAINING DEVICES (CONTINUED)
3) Age, sex, or physical conditions alone should not be deciding factors as to whether or not to restrain an individual. Officers will consider the nature of a physical or mental disability, sickness, or injury and the severity of the offense charged in determining which authorized restraints should be applied (KACP 30.8).
The following should be considered prior to the application of restraints on such detainees:
a) The potential for escape. b) The degree of threat posed by the detainee to the officer, or others. c) Whether the use of restraints would increase the severity of injury or aggravate an existing illness or condition.
4) Restraints are to be removed from the in-custody individual at the direction of the LMDC.
5) The hog-tying of detainees is strictly prohibited. Hog-tying is the technique of handcuffing an individual behind their back and securing their legs to the handcuffs or other restraint while the subject is in the prone (face-down) position or lying on their side.
B) Hand Restraints
1) The preferred method of restraint is to handcuff an individual behind the back, with their palms facing outward. Exceptions are permissible if the officer who is in charge of the detention feels another accepted method is more appropriate (e.g., extradition, physical impairment).
2) Officers will only use departmentally-approved handcuffs or other departmentally-approved restraining devices.
3) Handcuffs should only be tightened enough to effectively secure the person’s wrists. Officers will check the handcuffs to ensure they are not too tight by placing one (1) finger between the handcuff and detainee’s wrist.
4) All handcuffs will be double-locked.
5) Complaints of pain caused by wearing handcuffs should be addressed as soon as possible, and when safe and feasible to do so, by readjusting or otherwise ensuring proper application.
6) In special circumstances (e.g., patrol divisions without temporary detention rooms), an adult may be handcuffed to a fixed object for a reasonable period of time.
7) Under no circumstances will a juvenile be handcuffed, or secured, to a fixed object (KRS 610.220).
C) Other Approved Restraints
1) When the use of regular handcuffs is not sufficient (e.g., combative detainees, detainees who are presenting a high escape risk), officers may apply approved leg restraints. Approved leg restraints include the following:
